units.label: First words
units.title: Nice to meet you.
units.description: Seven characters. Your first conversation.

goal.text: 我是學生。
goal.pinyin: wǒ shì xuéshēng
goal.meaning: I am a student.

units.label: People & connections
units.title: A little more to say.
units.description: 13 new words and forms. More ways to talk about people.

goal.text: 他們也是我的學生。
goal.pinyin: tāmen yě shì wǒ de xuéshēng
goal.meaning: They are my students too.

units.label: Things & places
units.title: A little world around you.
units.description: 13 new words and forms. Point, describe, and say where things are.

goal.text: 我們都在這裡。
goal.pinyin: wǒmen dōu zài zhèlǐ
goal.meaning: We are all here.

units.label: Actions & plans
units.title: What would you like to do?
units.description: 13 new words and forms. Go, read, speak, and make a plan.

goal.text: 我想學中文。
goal.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng xué Zhōngwén
goal.meaning: I want to learn Chinese.

units.label: Tea & conversation
units.title: A little conversation over tea.
units.description: 8 new words and expressions. Offer a drink, share a preference, and say thanks.

goal.text: 你要不要喝茶？
goal.pinyin: nǐ yào bu yào hē chá?
goal.meaning: Would you like some tea?

units.label: Family & photos
units.title: My Family
units.description: 10 new words and forms. Meet the family and talk about photos.

goal.text: 這是我的家人。
goal.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de jiārén.
goal.meaning: This is my family.

units.label: Descriptions & weekends
units.title: What Shall We Do This Weekend?
units.description: 10 new words and activities. Describe, share hobbies, and make a weekend plan.

goal.text: 我們去看電影吧。
goal.pinyin: Wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
goal.meaning: Let’s go see a movie.

units.label: Plans & invitations
units.title: Let’s Make a Plan Together
units.description: 8 new words and expressions. Give opinions, invite someone, and agree on a day and activity.

goal.text: 我們明天一起去游泳，怎麼樣？
goal.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ qù yóuyǒng, zěnmeyàng?
goal.meaning: How about going swimming together tomorrow?

units.label: Sports, music & choices
units.title: Sports, Music & Choices
units.description: 6 new words and expressions. Talk about music and sports, ask someone to choose, and explain your preferences.

goal.text: 你喜歡打籃球還是踢足球？
goal.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān dǎ lánqiú háishì tī zúqiú?
goal.meaning: Do you like playing basketball or soccer?

units.label: Routines, food & dinner plans
units.title: Routines & Common Ground
units.description: 7 new words and expressions. Talk about morning and evening routines, choose Vietnamese food for dinner, and explain what your group does or does not share.

goal.text: 我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
goal.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn, hǎo bu hǎo?
goal.meaning: How about we eat dinner together this evening?

units.label: Order a drink · for here or to go
units.title: A Drink to Go
units.description: 7 new words and expressions. Order cups of hot tea or coffee, choose a size, and say whether your order is for here or to go.

goal.text: 我要一杯熱茶，外帶，謝謝。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ yào yì bēi rè chá, wàidài, xièxie.
goal.meaning: I would like a cup of hot tea to go, thank you.

units.label: Numbers & everyday prices
units.title: How Much Altogether?
units.description: 13 new words and forms. Build numbers up to 99, read drink prices, and ask how much one item or a whole order costs.

goal.text: 一共多少錢？七十五塊。
goal.pinyin: Yígòng duōshǎo qián? Qīshíwǔ kuài.
goal.meaning: How much altogether? Seventy-five dollars.

units.label: At the shop
units.title: Buying Snacks & Asking for Help
units.description: 10 new words and forms. Ask a shopkeeper a question, order buns, ask for help, and read prices in hundreds and thousands.

goal.text: 請幫我買兩個包子。
goal.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ mǎi liǎng ge bāozi.
goal.meaning: Please buy two buns for me.

units.label: Describe, compare & choose
units.title: Choosing a Phone
units.description: 13 new words and forms. Talk about phones, new and old items, price, the kind you want, and what a device can do.

goal.text: 這支手機能上網嗎？
goal.pinyin: Zhè zhī shǒujī néng shàngwǎng ma?
goal.meaning: Can this phone go online?

units.label: Noodles, soup & small eats
units.title: Food Favorites & Ordering
units.description: 12 new words and forms. Describe food, choose a favorite, order bowls, and understand prices such as thirty-something dollars.

goal.text: 我想點一碗牛肉麵。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng diǎn yì wǎn niúròu miàn.
goal.meaning: I would like to order a bowl of beef noodles.

units.label: Restaurants, cooking & learning
units.title: Spicy Food & Cooking Skills
units.description: 13 new words and forms. Talk about yesterday, react to spicy food, explain a choice, and describe cooking skills.

goal.text: 我會做飯，也做得不錯。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuòfàn, yě zuò de búcuò.
goal.meaning: I can cook, and I do it pretty well.

units.label: Local food & recommendations
units.title: Food Worth Trying
units.description: 10 new words and expressions. Name local dishes, share what you know or have heard, and recommend a meal.

goal.text: 我知道那家店。你一定要吃小籠包！
goal.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nà jiā diàn. Nǐ yídìng yào chī xiǎolóngbāo!
goal.meaning: I know that shop. You really must try the xiaolongbao!

units.label: Schools, scenery & locations
units.title: Around the School
units.description: 12 new words and forms. Describe a school and its surroundings, find places, and say where you study.

goal.text: 我現在在圖書館裡面看書。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài zài túshūguǎn lǐmiàn kàn shū.
goal.meaning: I am reading inside the library now.

units.label: Destinations, distance & errands
units.title: Visiting Friends & Nearby Shops
units.description: 11 new words and forms. Visit a friend, describe distance, and find a nearby place to shop or eat.

goal.text: 我今天要和朋友一起吃飯。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yào hé péngyǒu yìqǐ chīfàn.
goal.meaning: I am going to have a meal with a friend today.

units.label: Dorms, floors & campus buildings
units.title: Finding Places on Campus
units.description: 12 new words and forms. Find dorms and classrooms, describe floors, and distinguish front, behind and beside.

goal.text: 圖書館旁邊的教室在二樓。
goal.pinyin: Túshūguǎn pángbiān de jiàoshì zài èr lóu.
goal.meaning: The classroom beside the library is on the second floor.

units.label: Gentle actions, appointments & clock time
units.title: Making Plans by the Clock
units.description: 11 new words and forms. Soften requests, make an appointment, tell exact time, and say when you are free.

goal.text: 你什麼時候有空？
goal.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou yǒu kòng?
goal.meaning: When are you free?

units.label: Afternoon schedules, ongoing actions & routines
units.title: A Busy Afternoon
units.description: 13 new words, plus the transparent combinations 每天 and 剛開始. Tell afternoon times, describe ongoing actions, and distinguish every day from not every day.

goal.text: 我每天下午都上書法課。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xiàwǔ dōu shàng shūfǎ kè.
goal.meaning: I have calligraphy class every afternoon.

units.label: Recent routines, useful expressions & permission
units.title: Can I Go Check It Out?
units.description: 10 new words and forms, with 每天 and 剛開始 reviewed from Unit 22. Talk about recent activities and ask, grant, or refuse permission.

goal.text: 我可不可以去看比賽？
goal.pinyin: Wǒ kě bù kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài?
goal.meaning: May I go watch the game?

units.label: Transportation, companions & implicit comparison
units.title: How Are You Getting There?
units.description: 12 new words and forms. Start this lesson with transportation, going with someone, asking how, implicit comparison with 比較, and 又…又….

goal.text: 你怎麼去學校？
goal.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme qù xuéxiào?
goal.meaning: How do you go to school?

units.label: Getting around & explicit comparison
units.title: Which Way Is Faster?
units.description: 10 new this lesson words and forms. Get around with Taiwan transport vocabulary and compare two choices explicitly with 比.

goal.text: 騎機車比坐公車快嗎？
goal.pinyin: Qí jīchē bǐ zuò gōngchē kuài ma?
goal.meaning: Is riding a scooter faster than taking the bus?

units.label: Holidays, plans & feasibility
units.title: What Are You Planning?
units.description: 11 genuinely new these lessons words and forms. Close the this lesson tail, then talk about breaks, travel plans, and when something will happen.

goal.text: 我打算跟朋友去旅行。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn gēn péngyǒu qù lǚxíng.
goal.meaning: I plan to travel with friends.

units.label: Duration, free time & suggestions
units.title: How Long Will You Be Away?
units.description: 10 new this lesson words and forms. Ask how long, describe what happens during free time, and give simple suggestions for places and activities.

goal.text: 你應該去夜市。
goal.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi qù yèshì.
goal.meaning: You should go to a night market.

units.label: Travel time, duration & transport
units.title: How Long Is the Trip?
units.description: Master the this lesson duration system while repairing real this lesson travel vocabulary gaps, with each recovered item tied back to time, routes, tickets, or trip planning.

goal.text: 我們放三天的假。
goal.pinyin: Wǒmen fàng sān tiān de jià.
goal.meaning: We have three days off.

units.label: Visit plans, conditions & fruit
units.title: If You Come to Visit
units.description: Finish visit dates and conditions, then transition into fruit language through one continuing visit-and-hosting context.

goal.text: 要是你來，我就給你一塊水果。
goal.pinyin: Yàoshi nǐ lái, wǒ jiù gěi nǐ yí kuài shuǐguǒ.
goal.meaning: If you come, I’ll give you a piece of fruit.

units.label: Fruit, trying & descriptions
units.title: Try It and Describe It
units.description: Identify fruit, make a guess, try an action, describe a subjective impression, and talk about photos and clothing.

goal.text: 這是西瓜吧？你吃吃看。
goal.pinyin: Zhè shì xīguā ba? Nǐ chīchīkàn.
goal.meaning: This is watermelon, right? Try it and see.

units.label: People, hotels & reasons
units.title: The One in Blue
units.description: Continue this lesson through people and hotel descriptions: identify people with modifying clauses, describe changes with sentence-final 了, express direction with 往, and connect causes and effects with 因為…所以….

goal.text: 因為現在去玩的人比較少，所以旅館不太貴。
goal.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiànzài qù wán de rén bǐjiào shǎo, suǒyǐ lǚguǎn bú tài guì.
goal.meaning: Because fewer people are traveling now, the hotel is not too expensive.

units.label: Renting & rooms
units.title: A Place to Rent
units.description: Begin this lesson with renting and the home: landlords, rooms, left/right location, nearby places, walking time, 來 + activity, and the single-sentence 就 that marks unexpectedly little time or distance.

goal.text: 我來看房子。走路五分鐘就到了。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ lái kàn fángzi. Zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
goal.meaning: I came to look at the place. It is only a five-minute walk to get there.

units.label: Landlords, repairs & natural speech
units.title: Settling Into the New Place
units.description: Cover this lesson the conversation through the landlord phone call: already/getting used to, household problems, waiting and appointments, repairs and payment, existential subjects with 有, the likelihood use of 會, and natural omission of understood subjects and objects.

goal.text: 熱水器的水好像不熱。今天我會去看看。
goal.pinyin: Rèshuǐqì de shuǐ hǎoxiàng bú rè. Jīntiān wǒ huì qù kànkan.
goal.meaning: The water from the water heater doesn't seem hot. I'll go take a look today.

units.label: Study plans, sequence & scholarships
units.title: How Long Will You Study?
units.description: Begin this lesson with study plans and duration, 先…再… sequencing, language-center and university study, total time needed, cost, scholarships, and grades.

banner.pinyin: Xiān niàn Zhōngwén, zài niàn dàxué

goal.text: 我先在語言中心念一年，再念四年大學，所以需要五年。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ xiān zài yǔyán zhōngxīn niàn yì nián, zài niàn sì nián dàxué, suǒyǐ xūyào wǔ nián.
goal.meaning: I will first study for one year at a language center, then study at university for four years, so I need five years.

units.label: Tuition, future work & past-event focus
units.title: Who Paid the Tuition?
units.description: Finish this lesson the conversation with tuition, company support, future work plans, studying while working, encouragement, and the 是…的 focus construction for past events.

banner.text: 我的學費是公司替我付的
banner.pinyin: Wǒ de xuéfèi shì gōngsī tì wǒ fù de

goal.text: 我的學費是公司替我付的。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ de xuéfèi shì gōngsī tì wǒ fù de.
goal.meaning: My tuition is paid by my company for me.

units.label: Work, after-events & easy/hard actions
units.title: Is That Job Easy to Find?
units.description: Complete this lesson with the conversation: work and business, returning home, Event + 以後, finding a job, trying, and the special 好/難 + verb patterns.

banner.text: 這樣的工作在你們國家好找嗎
banner.pinyin: Zhèyàng de gōngzuò zài nǐmen guójiā hǎo zhǎo ma

goal.text: 我回國以後，也想找個有機會說中文的工作。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ huíguó yǐhòu, yě xiǎng zhǎo ge yǒu jīhuì shuō Zhōngwén de gōngzuò.
goal.meaning: After I go back home, I would also like to find a job with opportunities to speak Chinese.

units.label: Birthday calls, returning & remembering
units.title: Tomorrow Is Your Birthday
units.description: Begin this lesson with a birthday phone call: identify yourself, greet someone after a long time, say you came back, react to forgetting, and say you remember.

goal.text: 啊，我怎麼忘了！謝謝你還記得。
goal.pinyin: A, wǒ zěnme wàng le! Xièxie nǐ hái jìde.
goal.meaning: Oh! How could I forget! Thank you for still remembering.

units.label: Language exchange, politeness & meeting plans
units.title: I'll See You After Class
units.description: Finish the birthday phone call: language exchange, politeness, birthday plans, meeting arrangements, and 一…就….

banner.pinyin: Yí xiàkè, jiù qù zhǎo nǐ

goal.text: 明天我一下課，就去你們學校找你。
goal.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ yí xiàkè, jiù qù nǐmen xuéxiào zhǎo nǐ.
goal.meaning: Tomorrow, as soon as class ends, I'll go to your school to find you.

units.label: Gifts, birthday food & completed actions
units.title: What Did You Order?
units.description: Begin the birthday dinner: gifts, food preferences, completed actions with verbal 了, and 不 vs. 沒（有）.

banner.text: 我已經訂了豬腳麵線和蛋
banner.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng dìng le zhūjiǎo miànxiàn hé dàn

goal.text: 我已經訂了豬腳麵線和蛋。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng dìng le zhūjiǎo miànxiàn hé dàn.
goal.meaning: I already ordered pork knuckles, fine noodles, and an egg.

units.label: Food preferences, totality & birthday customs
units.title: What Does Everyone Eat?
units.description: Formalize all-inclusive question words, do-more/do-less actions, and the birthday-custom discussion.

goal.text: 我什麼都吃。你多吃一點。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ shénme dōu chī. Nǐ duō chī yìdiǎn.
goal.meaning: I eat anything. Have a little more.

units.label: Confirmation, comparison & birthday wishes
units.title: Happy Birthday and Best Wishes
units.description: Finish the birthday topic with confirmation questions, equality comparisons, birthday wishes, and a four-objective capstone.

goal.text: 祝你生日快樂、萬事如意、心想事成。
goal.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè, wànshì rúyì, xīnxiǎng shìchéng.
goal.meaning: Happy birthday; may everything go your way and all your wishes come true.

units.label: Weather & four seasons
units.title: Weather and the Four Seasons
units.description: Describe weather, name all four seasons, ask whether it snows or rains, and explain seasonal preferences.

goal.text: 因為我怕冷，所以我比較喜歡春天。
goal.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ pà lěng, suǒyǐ wǒ bǐjiào xǐhuān chūntiān.
goal.meaning: Because I'm sensitive to the cold, I prefer spring.

units.label: Duration & imminence
units.title: How Long and What's About to Happen
units.description: Contrast completed duration with duration up to now, talk about missing home, and describe events that are about to happen.

goal.text: 我在臺灣住了半年多了。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ zài Táiwān zhù le bànnián duō le.
goal.meaning: I have been in Taiwan for a little over half a year.

units.label: Typhoons & comparisons
units.title: Typhoons and Comparisons
units.description: Discuss typhoons, give caution, compare conditions with 更 and 沒有…那麼, and complete the cumulative weather capstone.

goal.text: 希望這次的沒有上次的那麼可怕。
goal.pinyin: Xīwàng zhè cì de méiyǒu shàng cì de nàme kěpà.
goal.meaning: I hope this one isn't as scary as the last one.

units.label: Symptoms & feeling sick
units.title: Symptoms and Feeling Sick
units.description: Ask about discomfort, describe symptoms, and say how long a condition has lasted.

goal.text: 我一直流鼻水，頭很痛，胃口很差。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí liú bíshuǐ, tóu hěn tòng, wèikǒu hěn chā.
goal.meaning: I have a runny nose, my head hurts, and my appetite is poor.

units.label: Diagnosis & treatment
units.title: Diagnosis, Medicine, and Treatment
units.description: Identify illness, discuss medicine and recovery, and use introductory 把.

banner.pinyin: Qǐngwèn wǒ děi chī yào ma?

goal.text: 回去把藥吃了，多喝水，多休息。
goal.pinyin: Huíqù bǎ yào chī le, duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxí.
goal.meaning: Go back and take the medicine, drink more water, and rest more.

units.label: Stomach trouble & help
units.title: Stomach Trouble and Getting Help
units.description: Describe stomach trouble, offer or decline help, and sequence a completed event with 就.

goal.text: 我陪你去看病，好不好？
goal.pinyin: Wǒ péi nǐ qù kànbìng, hǎo bu hǎo?
goal.meaning: I'll go with you to see a doctor, okay?

units.label: Advice & recovery
units.title: Advice, Comparisons, and Recovery
units.description: Give health advice, compare improvement and actions, use separable verbs, read the prescription card, and close this lesson cumulatively.

goal.text: 現在臉色比早上好得多了。
goal.pinyin: Xiànzài liǎnsè bǐ zǎoshang hǎo de duō le.
goal.meaning: Now your complexion is much better than in the morning.

units.label: Asking directions
units.title: Lost? Ask the Way
units.description: Offer help, ask for a route to NTNU, and turn at an intersection.

goal.text: 請問，到師大怎麼走？
goal.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, dào Shīdà zěnme zǒu?
goal.meaning: Excuse me, how do I get to NTNU?

units.label: Following the route
units.title: Lights, Cash, and Local Help
units.description: Complete a route and ask where to withdraw money.

goal.text: 過了第二個紅綠燈，就看見師大了。
goal.pinyin: Guò le dì èr ge hónglǜdēng, jiù kànjiàn Shīdà le.
goal.meaning: After the second traffic light, NTNU comes into view.

units.label: Reading a map
units.title: Walk with a Map
units.description: Learn to use a map, describe continuing actions, and talk about shops and alleys.

goal.text: 他們看著地圖，經過兩個巷子。
goal.pinyin: Tāmen kànzhe dìtú, jīngguò liǎng ge xiàngzi.
goal.meaning: They keep looking at the map and pass two alleys.

units.label: Distance and two actions
units.title: Near the Noodle Shop
units.description: Read the end of the trip, do two things at once, and describe distance.

goal.text: 他們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
goal.pinyin: Tāmen yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú.
goal.meaning: They eat noodles while looking at the map.

vocabulary.note: An everyday greeting; the first tone sounds ní before hǎo.
One word written with two characters. Also students, depending on context.
Sounds the same as 他.
An extra everyday form alongside the frequency-list words.
Sounds bú before a fourth tone, as in 不是.
Sounds yí in 一個.
Often light-toned ge in a phrase. Used with 人 and 學生 here.

vocabulary.meaning: do not have; there is not / are no

vocabulary.note: Points to something nearby. Use a measure word before a noun: 這個人.
Points to something farther away: 那個人.
One question word written with two characters. 麼 has a light neutral tone.
An everyday noun to practice counting, ownership, and location.
一本書 = one book. 這本書 = this book.
兩本書 = two books. 兩個人 = two people.

vocabulary.meaning: very; neutral link before an adjective
vocabulary.note: In a plain description, 很 often does not strongly emphasize very.
Place it before the location. No 是 is needed: 我在這裡.
A place word made from 這 and 裡. Learn it as a whole word.
The matching place word for somewhere farther away.
Goes after the group and before the verb: 我們都在這裡.
The destination follows the verb: 去那裡. The u in qù represents the ü vowel, written without dots after q.
Movement toward the speaker or the chosen reference point: 來這裡.
An information question word. Compare 那裡 (nàlǐ), there.
The object determines the English action: 看書 means read books.
Also pronounced hàn for and in Taiwan. Use it between people or things, not to join whole sentences.
A language name written with two characters; it counts as one word.
Shares 文 with 中文. It counts as one word, not two characters.
You know the character from 學生. Now practice it as an independent verb: 學中文.
Put the language directly after the verb: 說英文.
聽中文 names listening to Chinese; it does not by itself mean understanding it.
For want to, follow it with an action: 想學中文.
Can precede a thing you want or an action you intend to do.

vocabulary.meaning: can; know how to (a learned skill)
vocabulary.note: A learned ability here: 會說英文. Its negative is 不會 (bú huì).

vocabulary.meaning: measure word for flat objects / photos
how about it?; how does that sound?

vocabulary.note: Use the familiar 聽: 聽音樂, listen to music. In this word 樂 is yuè.
Use 運動 as an activity by itself; it does not need a following object.
打 means hit/play here; 籃球 is basketball. Learn the sport with its verb.
踢 means kick; 足球 is soccer, also called football.
網球 is tennis; 網 means net. This sport also uses 打.
Put 還是 between the alternatives. Do not add 嗎 to this choice-question pattern.
A time word. Put it before the action or habit it frames.
A time word used before the action or habit it frames.

vocabulary.meaning: how about it?; does that sound good?
vocabulary.note: Place it after a suggestion to ask whether the other person agrees.
Use it after a country name to name a cuisine.
越南菜 means Vietnamese food. Learn the country name as one word.

vocabulary.meaning: cup; measure word for cups of a drink

vocabulary.note: You know the character from 中文. The new meaning here is medium: 中杯.
A complete acknowledgment. The 的 is light; learn 好的 as a fixed reply here.
Names the number two. Keep 兩 before 杯 for two cups.

vocabulary.meaning: may all your wishes come true
vocabulary.note: Fixed four-character auspicious wish.
A person who treats patients. 醫生 yīshēng is “doctor”; use it as a title or a noun.
Put 一直 before the continuing action: 一直流鼻水 means “keep having a runny nose.”
A verb for liquid flowing. In 流鼻水, it describes a runny nose.
The mucus from the nose. Use 流鼻水 for the symptom “have a runny nose.”
The body part “head” here. 頭很痛 means “my/the head hurts.”
Use after the body part that hurts: 頭很痛. It describes pain, not the action of injuring someone.
Appetite, not the stomach itself. 胃口很差 means “have a poor appetite.”
Pronounced chā here: poor or bad in quality, as in 胃口很差.
The two characters form one word, “throat.” Learn hóulóng together.
To become inflamed. 喉嚨發炎 means “the throat is inflamed.”
To fall ill or be sick. 生 and 病 form a separable verb, revisited later in this lesson.
To have a fever. Learn the whole word; it is not translated as “send out burning.”
A common cold; used as a verb for catching or having one.
Medicine. Say 吃藥 chī yào for “take medicine,” even though 吃 usually means “eat.”
A pharmacy or drugstore where you get medicine. 藥 means medicine.
To take, hold, or get something. 拿藥 means to collect or get medicine.
Marks the affected object before the action: 把藥吃了, “take the medicine.” It has no separate English translation in this pattern.
Put before an action to tell someone not to do it. This is the imperative “don’t,” not the “other” sense.
Water as a drink here. 多喝水 means “drink more water.”
To rest or take a break. 多休息 means “get more rest.”
To sleep. It is a separable verb: later you will see material placed between 睡 and 覺.
A little earlier. 早一點睡覺 means “go to sleep a little earlier.”
Ask this when someone seems unwell or something seems wrong: “What’s wrong?”
The color or appearance of someone’s face, especially as a sign of health or emotion.
Not good to look at. Describing 臉色, it means the person looks unwell, not that you are insulting their appearance.
The belly or abdomen; 子 is pronounced with a neutral tone: dùzi.
Pronounced tù (fourth tone) for “vomit; throw up.”
Counts occurrences of an action: 三次 means “three times.” It does not measure how long the action lasts.
Go or stay with someone, often to keep them company or help: 陪你去看病.
To see a doctor as a patient. Learn the phrase together rather than translating 看 as “look at.”
Politely decline an offer: “No need, thanks.” It does not mean that something is broken or unusable.
Health; also healthy in descriptive uses. 健康中心 is a health center.
Insurance. 健康保險 means “health insurance.”
A health center, such as the place on campus where students can seek care.
Go or return home. 回 means return; 家 means home.
Oily or greasy when describing food here; as a noun, 油 also means oil.
Icy or ice-cold when describing food or drinks here; as a noun, 冰 means ice.
Care about or be concerned about someone. 謝謝你關心 means “Thank you for caring.”
Introduce advice: “It would be best to…” or “You should…” This is stronger than merely listing a preference.
A measure word for bags or packets, such as a packet of medicine. 三包 means “three packets.”
The verb “sleep,” also found in 睡覺. Use 睡 when comparing how long people sleep.
An hour as a duration: 三個小時 means “three hours.” It does not state a clock time.
路人 (lùrén) is a passer-by: a person you meet on the street. 路 means road and 人 means person. You can politely ask a passer-by for help; the word does not mean a tour guide.
幫忙 (bāngmáng) means help or do a favor. 你需要我幫忙嗎？ (Nǐ xūyào wǒ bāngmáng ma?) means “Do you need my help?” 需要 means need; 我 is the person offering to help.

迷路 (mílù) means lose your way. 我好像迷路了。 (Wǒ hǎoxiàng mílù le.) means “I seem to have lost my way.” 好像 softens the claim to “seem”; final 了 marks the new situation. 迷路 describes what happened, not a place.
師大 (Shīdà) is the short name for National Taiwan Normal University (NTNU) in Taipei. Treat it as a place name. It is the destination in our directions examples.
走 (zǒu) means walk or go along a route. 到師大怎麼走？ (Dào Shīdà zěnme zǒu?) means “How do I get to NTNU?” 到師大 names the destination; 怎麼走 asks how to go there. 走 alone does not say that you have arrived.

下 (xià) before a number and measure word means next or following. 下一個 (xià yí ge) means “the next one.” This is the “next” sense, not the “down” sense. You will combine it with a place in the next card.
路口 (lùkǒu) is an intersection, where streets meet. 下一個路口 (xià yí ge lùkǒu) means “the next intersection.” 下一個 tells you which one; 路口 names the place.
往前 (wǎng qián) means forward or ahead. 往 gives the direction and 前 means front/ahead. 往前走 (wǎng qián zǒu) means “walk forward.” The movement verb is 走; 往前 tells you its direction.
右轉 (yòu zhuǎn) means turn right: 右 is right and 轉 is turn. 到路口右轉。 (Dào lùkǒu yòu zhuǎn.) means “Turn right at the intersection.”
左轉 (zuǒ zhuǎn) means turn left: 左 is left and 轉 is turn. Compare 右轉 (yòu zhuǎn), turn right. Both tell you to change direction, whereas 往前走 means walk forward.
和平東路 (Hépíng Dōng Lù) is Heping East Road, a road name in Taipei. 和平 (Hépíng) is the name, 東 (dōng) means east, and 路 (lù) means road. Read the whole name as one destination or landmark.
段 (duàn) means a section of a road. 和平東路一段 (Hépíng Dōng Lù yī duàn) is “Section 1 of Heping East Road.” Put the section number after the road name and before 段. Here 一 is a section label, read yī.
紅綠燈 (hónglǜdēng) means traffic light: 紅 is red, 綠 is green, and 燈 is light. A traffic light can serve as a landmark in directions. 一個紅綠燈 (yí ge hónglǜdēng) means one traffic light.

第 (dì) before a number gives its position in a sequence. 第二 (dì èr) means second. 第二個紅綠燈 (dì èr ge hónglǜdēng) means “the second traffic light”; 兩個紅綠燈 means two traffic lights, a quantity rather than a position.
看見 (kànjiàn) means see or catch sight of. 我看見師大了。 (Wǒ kànjiàn Shīdà le.) means “I can see NTNU now.” 看 is looking; 看見 says that something comes into view.

告訴 (gàosù) means tell someone information. 告訴我 (gàosù wǒ) means “tell me.” Put the person after 告訴, then the information or question: 請告訴我師大在哪裡。 (Qǐng gàosù wǒ Shīdà zài nǎlǐ.) means “Please tell me where NTNU is.”
聽起來 (tīng qǐlái) means “sound” when giving an impression from what you hear. 聽起來不遠。 (Tīng qǐlái bù yuǎn.) means “It does not sound far.” Put the judgment after 起來; this is not a movement upward.
提款機 (tíkuǎnjī) means ATM. 提款 (tíkuǎn) means withdraw money and 機 (jī) means machine. 這裡有提款機嗎？ (Zhèlǐ yǒu tíkuǎnjī ma?) means “Is there an ATM here?”

超商 (chāoshāng) means convenience store in Taiwan, another name for 便利商店 (biànlì shāngdiàn). 超商裡有提款機。 (Chāoshāng lǐ yǒu tíkuǎnjī.) means “There is an ATM inside the convenience store.” This is an example, not a claim that every store has one.
郵局 (yóujú) means post office. A post office handles mail and may also offer cash withdrawal. 郵局在哪裡？ (Yóujú zài nǎlǐ?) means “Where is the post office?”
提 (tí) here means withdraw money. 提錢 (tí qián) means withdraw cash; 錢 is money. 郵局也可以提錢。 (Yóujú yě kěyǐ tí qián.) means “You can also withdraw money at the post office.”
那邊 (nàbiān) means over there, away from the speaker. 那邊有一家郵局。 (Nàbiān yǒu yì jiā yóujú.) means “There is a post office over there.” The word points to a location; it does not specify left or right.
下載 (xiàzài) means download: save digital information from a network to your device. 載 is pronounced zài in this word. Use 下載 before the thing being downloaded; 下載了 adds completed-action 了.
地圖 (dìtú) means map. 下載地圖 (xiàzài dìtú) means “download a map.” 一張地圖 (yì zhāng dìtú) means “one map”; 張 is the measure word you already use for flat items.
好用 (hǎoyòng) means easy to use or handy. 這張地圖很好用。 (Zhè zhāng dìtú hěn hǎoyòng.) means “This map is easy to use.” Ask 地圖好用不好用？ (Dìtú hǎoyòng bù hǎoyòng?) to ask whether it is easy to use.
著 (zhe, neutral tone) follows a verb to show a continuing action or state. 看著地圖 (kànzhe dìtú) means “looking at the map,” with the looking continuing. It does not say that the looking has finished.

日用品 (rìyòngpǐn) are articles used in daily life: daily necessities. 這家店賣日用品。 (Zhè jiā diàn mài rìyòngpǐn.) means “This shop sells daily necessities.” 日用 describes everyday use and 品 means articles or goods.
巷子 (xiàngzi) means alley or narrow lane. 這個巷子裡有一家店。 (Zhège xiàngzi lǐ yǒu yì jiā diàn.) means “There is a shop in this alley.” 裡 places the shop inside the alley.
經過 (jīngguò) means pass by or go past. 經過兩個巷子 (jīngguò liǎng ge xiàngzi) means “pass two alleys.” In directions, this tells you to pass those landmarks, without telling you to turn into either alley.
發現 (fāxiàn) means discover or notice something you had not noticed before. 我發現一家店。 (Wǒ fāxiàn yì jiā diàn.) means “I discover a shop.” Put what you discover after 發現.
餓 (è) means hungry. 我有一點餓。 (Wǒ yǒu yìdiǎn è.) means “I am a little hungry.” 有一點 softens the degree; 我餓了 (wǒ è le) says “I am hungry now.”
麵店 (miàn diàn) means noodle shop: 麵 is noodles and 店 is shop. 我們去麵店吃麵。 (Wǒmen qù miàn diàn chī miàn.) means “We go to a noodle shop to eat noodles.”

In this lesson 一邊 (yìbiān) introduces an action happening at the same time as another. Repeat it before both actions: 一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖 (yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú), “eat noodles while looking at the map.” It does not mean first do one, then the other.

離 (lí) marks the reference place when stating distance. 學校離這裡很近。 (Xuéxiào lí zhèlǐ hěn jìn.) means “The school is close to here.” Name the place being located, then 離 + reference place, then 很近 or 很遠.
背包 (bēibāo) means backpack. Read 背 as first-tone bēi in this word. 我想買一個背包。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí ge bēibāo.) means “I want to buy a backpack.” Use 個 to count backpacks.

正好 (zhènghǎo) here means happen to or just at the right time. 我正好想買背包。 (Wǒ zhènghǎo xiǎng mǎi bēibāo.) means “I happen to want to buy a backpack.” 正好 goes before 想買 and connects the wish to the present opportunity.
筆 (bǐ) means pen or writing instrument. 我想買筆。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi bǐ.) means “I want to buy pens.” The next card teaches how to count them.
枝 (zhī) is the measure word for pens here. 一枝筆 (yì zhī bǐ) is one pen; 兩枝筆 (liǎng zhī bǐ) is two pens. The order is number + 枝 + 筆. 枝 counts the items; 筆 names them.
本子 (běnzi) means notebook. 一本本子 (yì běn běnzi) is one notebook. The first 本 is the measure word for books; the 本 in 本子 is part of the noun. Keep both: 一 + 本 + 本子.
最後 (zuìhòu) means finally or in the end. 最後她買了兩枝筆。 (Zuìhòu tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ.) means “Finally she bought two pens.” 最後 puts this event at the end of a sequence.

師大路上 (Shīdà Lù shàng) means on Shida Road. 師大路 is the road name and 上 locates something along it. 師大路上有很多店。 (Shīdà Lù shàng yǒu hěn duō diàn.) means “There are many shops on Shida Road.” It does not mean inside the university.

你.note: 你 addresses one person. This form is used in Traditional Chinese too.
你.memory: Notice the narrow person on the left and the wider shape on the right.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person
parts.description: A side form of 人, meaning person. You will meet this component in many characters connected with people.

parts.label: 尔
parts.name: historical sound part
parts.description: This is a historical sound component. Its connection to nǐ is not transparent in modern Mandarin, so learn the pronunciation with the whole character.

好.note: 好 means good or well here. Together, 你好 is a greeting: hello.
好.memory: Remember the two familiar shapes side by side: woman and child. This is a memory aid for the written form.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman
parts.description: 女 means woman. As a left-hand component it becomes narrower, and its final stroke rises slightly.

parts.label: 子
parts.name: child
parts.description: 子 means child. You will meet this same component at the bottom of 學 later in the unit.

我.note: 我 can mean both I and me. Its form stays the same in either position.
我.memory: Learn the overlapping strokes as a whole. Watch the slanting hook and the final dot.

parts.label: 我
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: The modern pieces do not give a useful meaning equation for I. Learning the stroke sequence is more useful here than inventing a story for each part.

是.note: Use 是 to connect someone with an identity: 我是學生 means I am a student. It is not used before every adjective.
是.memory: Recognize 日 at the top, then give the lower strokes room to stretch.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun / day shape
parts.description: The top four strokes form 日 (sun or day). Here it is a useful shape to recognize; it does not literally explain the meaning am/is/are.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: The lower five strokes finish with a long stroke to the right. Learn this shape in context rather than assigning it a made-up meaning.

學.note: This is the Traditional character 學. The word 學生 means student.
學.memory: Picture a child learning beneath a cover. This is a memory aid; the upper strokes have a more complex historical origin.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper shape
parts.description: Start with the intricate upper group. Notice the two crossed marks and the strokes around them; learn their order slowly.

parts.label: 冖
parts.name: cover
parts.description: These two strokes form the cover-like 冖 shape above 子. It has no dot at the top.

parts.label: 子
parts.name: child
parts.description: The bottom three strokes form 子 (child), the same component you saw on the right of 好.

生.note: 生 has several uses in words. Learn 學生 as one word meaning student, rather than translating each character separately.
生.memory: Keep the central vertical stroke balanced across the three horizontal levels.

parts.label: 生
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: 生 is a basic character and a dictionary radical in its own right. You do not need to split it into smaller meaning parts to learn it.

嗎.note: Put 嗎 at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. In this use, ma has a light neutral tone.
嗎.memory: A small mouth on the left, a large horse on the right. The horse helps with the sound.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 means mouth. It is common in characters connected with speaking and sentence particles.

parts.label: 馬
parts.name: horse · mǎ
parts.description: 馬 is the phonetic component: mǎ points toward the sound ma. Sound components can suggest a syllable even when the tone differs.

他.note: 他 means he or him in this unit. 她 means she or her; both are pronounced tā.
他.memory: Keep the narrow person shape on the left. The three strokes on the right form 也.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person
parts.description: The same person component as in 你. It helps connect this character with a person.

parts.label: 也
parts.name: 也 shape
parts.description: 他 and 她 share 也 on the right. The whole characters are pronounced tā; 也 by itself is yě. Do not read this as a modern sound equation.

她.note: 她 is the written pronoun she or her. It sounds exactly like 他 (he or him). The writing and context tell them apart.
她.memory: Reuse 女 from 好, then add the same right side as 他.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman
parts.description: 女 is the same component you met in 好. Here it helps distinguish the written pronoun she from 他.

parts.label: 也
parts.name: 也 shape
parts.description: This is the same three-stroke component as in 他. Sharing a component is useful for recognition even when it does not explain the modern pronunciation.

們.note: Add the light-toned 們 to a personal pronoun: 我們 = we, 你們 = you (plural), 他們 = they. It is an ending, not an English-style plural for every noun.
們.memory: A narrow person stands beside a wide door. This is a shape memory aid.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person
parts.description: 亻 connects this ending with people. You have already written it in 你 and 他.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: door · mén
parts.description: 門 (mén, door) points toward the sound men. The ending 們 normally has a light neutral tone.

也.note: 也 means also or too. In the sentences here it goes after the person and before 是: 我也是學生 = I am a student too.
也.memory: You have seen this shape inside 他 and 她. Now give it the whole square.

parts.label: 也
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: Learn the three-stroke shape as a whole. Its meaning also is not explained by smaller modern pieces.

不.note: 不 goes before 是 to say am not, is not, or are not. Before the fourth tone of 是, bù changes to bú in speech: 不是, bú shì.
不.memory: Start with the horizontal stroke, then place the falling stroke, vertical, and final dot.

parts.label: 不
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: The four strokes are most useful as one shape. Their modern forms do not give a reliable meaning story for not.

example.meaning: am not; is not; are not

的.note: 的 links a person to a noun: 我的學生 = my student. In this use, de has a light neutral tone.
的.memory: Find the white-shaped block on the left and the spoon-shaped strokes on the right. Remember the written shapes, not a literal meaning equation.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: 白 · white shape
parts.description: 白 means white on its own. Recognize its five strokes here; white does not explain the possessive use of 的.

parts.label: 勺
parts.name: 勺 · spoon shape
parts.description: The right side is 勺, a three-stroke shape. Learn de with the whole character instead of guessing its sound from this part.

一.note: 一 means one. Its dictionary tone is yī. In 一個 it is pronounced yí because 個 (gè) has a fourth tone.
一.memory: One horizontal stroke, drawn from left to right.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: one horizontal stroke
parts.description: 一 is a basic character in its own right. A single horizontal stroke writes the number one.

個.note: When counting people, put 個 between the number and the noun: 一個人 = one person. 個 is often pronounced lightly as ge in a phrase.
個.memory: A person component beside a box with another shape inside. Keep the right side roomy.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person
parts.description: Recognize the person component again. 個 is used to count people and many other things, so its use is wider than just people.

parts.label: 固
parts.name: 固 · gù
parts.description: 固 is a historical phonetic component. Its modern sound gù is only a rough clue to gè. The outer enclosure surrounds 古; close the outer bottom last.

人.note: 人 can mean person or people. Chinese nouns usually do not change shape for singular or plural; the number or context makes it clear.
人.memory: Two spreading strokes. Start the left-falling stroke first, then the right-falling stroke.

parts.label: 人
parts.name: person
parts.description: 人 is the full character person. Its narrow side form is 亻, which you have already seen in 你, 他, 們, and 個.

有.note: 有 means have. Put a person before it to say who has something. Without that subject, 有 + a noun phrase can introduce something that exists: there is or there are.
有.memory: Two strokes above a four-stroke lower block. These visual groups help you remember the shape.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper two strokes
parts.description: Start with the horizontal and the left-falling stroke. Treat them as a visual group rather than inventing a meaning for them.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: 月-shaped lower part
parts.description: This lower group resembles 月. A visible moon shape does not by itself explain the modern word have.

沒.note: Learn 沒 in 沒有 (méiyǒu): do not have, or there is not. 有 is negated with 沒, not 不.
沒.memory: Three water strokes on the left, then the four-stroke right side. Follow the Taiwan form shown in the guide.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water
parts.description: 氵 is a side form of 水 (water). It reflects other historical uses of 沒; it does not give the meaning of modern 沒有.

parts.label: 𠬛
parts.name: four-stroke right side
parts.description: Learn the upper turn and the lower 又-shaped strokes from the guide. This visible group is not a modern meaning equation for negation.

這.note: 這 points to something nearby: this. Put 個 before 人 when naming this person: 這個人. You will practice the pattern next.
這.memory: The speech-shaped block sits inside a long walking component. Watch the order: the inner block comes first.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: 辶 wraps around the left and bottom. In this Taiwan form it has four strokes, written after 言. Its usual movement association does not literally explain this.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech-shaped block
parts.description: 言 means speech on its own. Here, recognize its seven-stroke shape without treating speech as the meaning of 這.

那.note: 那 points to something farther away: that. Compare 這個人 (this person) and 那個人 (that person).
那.memory: Four strokes on the left, then a narrow three-stroke shape on the right.

parts.label: left
parts.name: four-stroke left side
parts.description: Watch the long turn, two short horizontals, and final falling stroke. This shape helps you remember the writing, not a literal meaning equation.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: right-side 阝
parts.description: On the right, 阝 is a form of 邑, a city or settlement component. This does not explain the modern meaning that. You will see it again in 都.

什.note: Learn 什 together with 麼: 什麼 (shénme) means what. In this word, 什 is pronounced shén.
什.memory: A person component next to a simple cross.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person
parts.description: The same two-stroke person component you met in 你 and 他. It does not make 什麼 mean a person.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: 十 · shí
parts.description: 十 is a historical phonetic component. Its sound shí is not the same as shén in 什麼, so learn the complete word’s pronunciation.

麼.note: 麼 is light-toned me in 什麼. The two characters form one question word: what. 麼 is not used by itself for what here.
麼.memory: A large upper frame over a small, three-stroke lower shape. Take the upper strokes slowly.

parts.label: 麻
parts.name: 麻-shaped upper part
parts.description: The upper eleven strokes form 麻. Use the broad top and the two tree-like groups underneath as visual landmarks; they do not explain the meaning what.

parts.label: 幺
parts.name: 幺 · small lower shape
parts.description: 幺 is the three-stroke shape at the bottom. Keep it centered beneath the large upper part.

書.note: 書 means book or books, depending on context. As with 學生, you do not need a plural ending. We will introduce its measure word before counting books.
書.memory: A tall brush-shaped top over a broad lower block.

parts.label: 聿
parts.name: writing brush shape
parts.description: 聿 is associated with a writing brush. That connection is useful for remembering a character used for books and writing.

parts.label: 曰
parts.name: 曰-shaped lower block
parts.description: The lower four strokes form a wide 曰 shape. Recognize its proportions and stroke order instead of making a literal meaning story.

本.note: 本 is the measure word used with books: 一本書 = one book. It has other meanings, including root or origin; here we practice its counting use.
本.memory: Write 木, then add a short horizontal mark near the bottom.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: tree shape
parts.description: The first four strokes form 木 (tree). The extra mark near the base helps distinguish 本 from 木.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: short lower mark
parts.description: The final horizontal marks the lower part of the tree shape. Learn the book-counting use as the pattern 一本書, not as a literal sum of tree and one.

兩.note: Use 兩 before a measure word when counting two things: 兩個人 (two people), 兩本書 (two books).
兩.memory: Find the frame and central line, then the two small paired shapes inside.

parts.label: frame
parts.name: frame and central line
parts.description: The first four strokes make the top, outer frame, and central vertical. Watch these before adding the paired shapes.

parts.label: pair
parts.name: two inner shapes
parts.description: The last four strokes form two small 入-shaped groups, one on each side. Their pairing is a useful memory aid for two.

很.note: 很 can mean very. In a simple description it often just links the subject to an adjective, without emphasizing very. You will use it with big and small.
很.memory: Three narrow strokes on the left and a six-stroke shape on the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: three-stroke step component
parts.description: 彳 is often associated with steps or movement. It has three strokes, unlike the two-stroke person component 亻. Here it does not give the modern meaning very.

parts.label: 艮
parts.name: 艮 · gèn
parts.description: 艮 is the phonetic component. Its modern sound gèn is only a rough historical clue to hěn, not an exact pronunciation rule.

大.note: 大 describes size: big or large. A basic description uses 很大, without 是 before the adjective.
大.memory: Picture a person stretching both arms out wide. This is a memory aid for the shape.

parts.label: 大
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: A horizontal stroke crosses the two spreading strokes. Learn the three strokes together as one basic character.

小.note: 小 is the opposite of 大: small rather than big. 不大 means not big; it does not necessarily mean small.
小.memory: A central hook with a short stroke on either side.

parts.label: 小
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: Write the central stroke first, then the left stroke, then the right dot. Learn the shape as a whole.

在.note: 在 says where someone or something is. Put a place after it. It serves as the verb in these location sentences, so do not put 是 before it.
在.memory: Three upper strokes lead into a small 土 shape below.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper three strokes
parts.description: Follow the horizontal, falling stroke, and vertical shown by the guide. Recognize this upper group without inventing a modern meaning for each stroke.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth · 土
parts.description: The lower three strokes form 土 (earth or ground), a familiar component to notice in this character about location.

裡.note: Learn the place words 這裡 (zhèlǐ, here) and 那裡 (nàlǐ, there). 裡 can mean inside in other combinations, but these two words name places.
裡.memory: Five clothing strokes on the left, and a balanced 里 shape on the right.

parts.label: 衤
parts.name: clothing component
parts.description: 衤 is a side form of 衣 (clothing). Notice its five strokes; it is not the four-stroke component 礻. This spelling 裡 is standard in Taiwan.

parts.label: 里
parts.name: 里 · lǐ
parts.description: 里 is pronounced lǐ, the same sound and tone as 裡. It is a useful phonetic clue here.

都.note: 都 means all, or both for a group of two. Put it after the group and before the verb. In this use, it is pronounced dōu.
都.memory: An eight-stroke left side beside the same narrow right side as 那.

parts.label: 者
parts.name: 者-shaped left side
parts.description: The left eight strokes form 者. Recognize the upper crossing strokes and the 日-shaped block below; learn dōu with the whole character.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: right-side 阝
parts.description: This is the same three-stroke component as in 那. It is a form of 邑 (city or settlement), but it does not explain the meaning all in this use of 都.

去.note: 去 means go. Put the destination after it: 去那裡 = go there. Unlike 在 (be at), 去 describes movement.
去.memory: A 土-shaped top above a small, two-stroke lower shape.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth-shaped top
parts.description: The upper three strokes form 土, a shape you saw in 在. Recognize the shared shape without treating earth as a literal explanation of go.

parts.label: 厶
parts.name: two-stroke lower shape
parts.description: Write the angular turning stroke and then the dot. This 厶-shaped group helps distinguish 去 from other characters with 土.

來.note: 來 means come, toward the speaker or a place treated as the reference point. 來這裡 means come here. Learn 來 and 去 as a useful pair.
來.memory: A tall central shape with two smaller 人-like shapes tucked inside.

parts.label: 來
parts.name: overlapping whole shape
parts.description: The central 木-like strokes surround two small 人-like groups. Their strokes are interleaved, so follow the whole eight-stroke sequence rather than writing each visible part separately.

哪.note: 哪 appears in 哪裡 (nǎlǐ), meaning where. Notice the mouth component and third tone: 哪裡 asks where; 那裡 (nàlǐ) means there.
哪.memory: Add a small mouth to the left of the 那 you already know.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 is the same three-stroke component as in 嗎. It is a useful visible clue for distinguishing 哪 from 那.

parts.label: 那
parts.name: 那 · nà
parts.description: 那 suggests the syllable na, but the tone changes: 那 is nà (that), while 哪 in 哪裡 is nǎ. The right side reuses all seven strokes of 那.

看.note: 看 covers several English actions, depending on what follows it. 看書 means read a book or read books. In these uses it is pronounced kàn.
看.memory: Imagine a hand shading an eye so it can look into the distance.

parts.label: 龵
parts.name: hand-shaped upper part
parts.description: The upper four strokes are a changed form of 手 (hand). The hand above the eye is a useful connection with looking.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye
parts.description: 目 means eye. Its five strokes form the lower block, connecting this character with seeing.

和.note: 和 joins people or things: 我和你 = I and you. We write hé in the pinyin; you may also hear hàn for this use in Taiwan. The meaning and word order stay the same.
和.memory: A grain-shaped left side beside a small mouth.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain · hé
parts.description: 禾 is pronounced hé and helps with the hé reading of 和. The hàn reading used for and in Taiwan is a pronunciation to learn with the word, not from this sound clue.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: Recognize the three-stroke 口 shape on the right. It does not make grain plus mouth a literal meaning equation for and.

中.note: 中 can mean middle. In this unit it is the first character of 中文, Chinese. Learn the language name as a whole word, not as middle plus writing.
中.memory: A central vertical stroke passes through a small box.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: box shape
parts.description: The first three strokes make the box. Here it is a shape to recognize, not the word mouth in the meaning of 中文.

parts.label: 丨
parts.name: central vertical
parts.description: The final stroke passes down through the center and extends above and below the box.

文.note: 文 is connected with writing and language. It is the shared ending in 中文 (Chinese) and 英文 (English). Each language name counts as one word.
文.memory: A dot and horizontal at the top, then two long crossing strokes.

parts.label: 文
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: Learn the four strokes as one basic character. The lower crossing strokes should have room to spread; they are not two separate words.

英.note: 英 is the first character of 英文 (Yīngwén), English. This Taiwan stroke form has nine strokes, including four in the top component.
英.memory: A four-stroke plant component sits above a wider five-stroke lower shape.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: plant component
parts.description: The top is the plant or grass component, written with four strokes in this Taiwan form. It reflects other uses of 英, not the meaning English.

parts.label: 央
parts.name: 央 · yāng
parts.description: 央 is a historical phonetic component. Modern yāng is only a rough clue to yīng, so learn the pronunciation with the whole word 英文.

說.note: 說 means speak or say. Put a language after it to say which language someone speaks. Keep the Traditional 言 component and the Taiwan 兌 shape on the right.
說.memory: The speech component you saw in 這 now stands on the left.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech
parts.description: 言 is associated with speech and language. Its seven strokes give a useful meaning connection in 說, speak or say.

parts.label: 兌
parts.name: 兌-shaped right side
parts.description: 兌 is a historical phonetic component, but its modern reading duì does not directly give shuō. Notice the two upper strokes, the small box, and the spreading legs.

聽.note: 聽 means listen or listen to. English needs to in listen to English; Mandarin can put the language directly after 聽. This longer character is worth learning slowly, one group at a time.
聽.memory: Find the ear on the upper left and the heart shape at the bottom right.

parts.label: left
parts.name: ear and lower left strokes
parts.description: The first six strokes form 耳 (ear), a clear connection with listening. Four more strokes finish the lower left group. Complete this whole side before moving right.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right-hand group with 心
parts.description: Work down through the upper marks and box-like shape, then the horizontal and the bottom 心 (heart) shape. These landmarks help memory; they are not a literal formula for how the character was created.

想.note: 想 can mean think. Before an action, it can express want to or would like to: 想看書 = want to read. The lesson will show where it goes in a sentence.
想.memory: A tree-and-eye shape sits above a heart.

parts.label: 相
parts.name: 相 · xiāng
parts.description: The upper nine strokes form 相, with 木 on the left and 目 on the right. Its reading xiāng points to the syllable xiang; 想 has a third tone instead.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart; mind
parts.description: 心 is connected with thoughts and feelings, a useful meaning clue for think or want. Keep its four strokes spread beneath the upper block.

要.note: 要 can name something you want or an action you intend to do. It often sounds more definite than 想. We will practice this wanting and intention use, not every meaning of 要.
要.memory: A wide upper block over the 女 shape you already know.

parts.label: 覀
parts.name: wide upper block
parts.description: The top six strokes form a 覀-shaped block. Notice its short inner verticals and wide base; the shape does not literally explain want.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman-shaped lower part
parts.description: Reuse 女 from 好 and 她, now underneath the upper block. Recognize the component without inventing a woman-related meaning for modern 要.

會.meaning: can; know how to (a learned skill)
會.note: 會 before an action can mean know how to do it. 我會說英文 means I can speak English. This is learned ability, not a general word for permission.
會.memory: A broad, roof-like upper group above a small lower block.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper nine-stroke group
parts.description: Start with the two spreading top strokes, then build the enclosed shapes below. Follow the guide carefully; the visible pieces do not give a simple meaning equation for can.

parts.label: 曰
parts.name: wide lower block
parts.description: The last four strokes form a wide 曰-shaped block. You saw a similar lower shape in 書. Keep it centered under the larger top.

喝.note: 喝 is the action drink. The drink follows it directly: 喝茶.
喝.memory: Keep the mouth narrow and leave room for the right side.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 relates to using the mouth. Here the action is drinking.

parts.label: 曷
parts.name: historical sound part
parts.description: 曷 is the historical phonetic component. Learn hē with the whole character; modern sounds are not identical.

茶.note: 茶 names tea. In this Taiwan stroke form, the grass top takes four strokes.
茶.memory: Start with the grass, then the spreading middle and lower strokes.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass top
parts.description: This plant-related component helps connect the character with tea leaves.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: Learn the remaining strokes as one visual group. Their shapes are not a literal formula for tea.

請.note: Put 請 before an action to make a polite invitation or request.
請.memory: Recognize the speech component on the left, with 青 on the right.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech
parts.description: 言 is the speech component, a useful clue for this polite expression.

parts.label: 青
parts.name: qīng sound part
parts.description: 青 (qīng) suggests the qing syllable. 請 has the third tone.

喜.note: Use 喜 with 歡 as the everyday word 喜歡, to like.
喜.memory: Build the upper group, then finish with the lower mouth.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The first nine strokes form the upper group. Use its stacked shapes as a memory aid.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth shape
parts.description: The last three strokes form a separate 口 at the bottom.

歡.note: 歡 completes 喜歡. Learn the two characters as one word for like.
歡.memory: Give the dense left side most of the space and keep 欠 slim.

parts.label: 雚
parts.name: guàn sound part
parts.description: 雚 is a historical phonetic component. The modern sound differs, so learn huān with the whole word.

parts.label: 欠
parts.name: qiàn component
parts.description: 欠 is the four-stroke component on the right. Recognizing it helps organize this dense character.

咖.note: 咖啡 is a borrowed word for coffee. Here 咖 is pronounced kā.
咖.memory: Spot the mouth next to 加.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 appears in many characters used for sounds and spoken words.

parts.label: 加
parts.name: jiā sound-related part
parts.description: 加 is the phonetic component historically. In the borrowed word 咖啡, learn the pronunciation kā.

啡.note: 啡 completes 咖啡. The two characters form one word.
啡.memory: A small mouth sits beside the balanced rows of 非.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: This is the same left component as in 咖 and 喝.

parts.label: 非
parts.name: fēi sound part
parts.description: 非 (fēi) points directly to the pronunciation of 啡.

呢.note: Here 呢 asks the same question about another person: 你呢？ means And you?
呢.memory: A mouth on the left and 尼 on the right.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 is common in spoken sentence particles, including 嗎 and 呢.

parts.label: 尼
parts.name: ní sound part
parts.description: 尼 is the historical phonetic component. In this particle, use neutral-tone ne.

謝.note: The everyday expression is 謝謝. The second syllable is often light: xièxie.
謝.memory: Keep 言 narrow; let 射 fill the right side.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech
parts.description: The same speech component appears in 請 and 說. Thanking is expressed in words.

parts.label: 射
parts.name: shè sound part
parts.description: 射 is a historical sound component. Its modern pronunciation differs from xiè.

家.note: 家 can mean home or family. The next word combines it with 人, which you already know.
家.memory: Picture 宀 as a roof over 豕: a wide lower shape sheltered beneath a small roof.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: 宀 forms the three-stroke roof at the top of 家.

parts.label: 豕
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: 豕 fills the space below the roof, with a curved central stroke and strokes spreading to both sides.

爸.note: 爸爸 means dad. Repeat the character; the second syllable is light-toned ba.
爸.memory: Remember 爸 as 父 above 巴: the crossed upper strokes sit over a hooked lower shape.

parts.label: 父
parts.name: father component
parts.description: 父 forms the upper four strokes, including the crossing diagonals.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: 巴 forms the lower four strokes; notice its enclosed upper space and curved hook below.

媽.note: 媽媽 means mom. Repeat the character; the second syllable is light-toned ma.
媽.memory: Remember 媽 as 女 + 馬: a narrow 女 on the left and a larger 馬 on the right.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: 女 is the left component, also seen in 姐 and 妹.

parts.label: 馬
parts.name: horse-shaped sound component
parts.description: 馬 occupies the right side. Its four dots along the bottom make it easy to recognize.

哥.note: 哥哥 means an older brother. The second syllable is light-toned ge.
哥.memory: Look for two 可-shaped groups stacked in 哥, each with a small 口.

parts.label: 可
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper group has a horizontal top, a small 口 and a vertical stroke on the right.

parts.label: 可
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: The lower 可-shaped group repeats the small 口 and ends with the long hooked stroke.

姐.note: 姐姐 means an older sister. The second syllable is light-toned jie.
姐.memory: Remember 姐 as 女 + 且: the right side is a tall frame with horizontal lines.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: 女 sits on the left, as it does in 媽 and 妹.

parts.label: 且
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: 且 has two horizontal lines inside its tall frame and a longer horizontal base.

妹.note: 妹妹 means a younger sister. The second syllable is light-toned mei.
妹.memory: Remember 妹 as 女 + 未. In 未, the lower of the two horizontal lines is longer.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: 女 forms the narrow left side, shared with 媽 and 姐.

parts.label: 未
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: 未 has two horizontal lines crossed by a vertical, with two strokes spreading below.

誰.note: 誰 asks who a person is. Learn the rising second tone: shéi.
誰.memory: Remember 誰 as 言 + 隹: speech on the left, a tightly lined shape on the right.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: 言 forms the left side; look for its small 口 at the bottom.

parts.label: 隹
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: 隹 has a narrow left edge beside a vertical stem crossed by several horizontal strokes.

照.note: 照 is the first character of the two-character word for photo. Learn its partner next; do not translate this character as photo by itself.
照.memory: See 照 as 昭 over four dots: 日 is beside 刀 above 口, with 灬 underneath.

parts.label: 昭
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: 昭 combines 日 on the left with 刀 above 口 on the right.

parts.label: 灬
parts.name: four-dot fire component
parts.description: 灬 is the row of four dots across the bottom of 照.

片.note: 照片 means photo. Both syllables have the falling fourth tone: zhàopiàn. Learn it as one word.
片.memory: Remember 片 by its open shape: a tall left stroke, a short upper vertical and a bent stroke at the lower right.

parts.label: 片
parts.name: whole shape
parts.description: 片 is one four-stroke shape. Notice the open top and the corner formed at the lower right.

張.meaning: measure word for flat objects / photos
張.note: 張 is the measure word used with photos. The next explanation shows where to put it.
張.memory: Remember 張 as 弓 + 長: the small bow shape stands beside the taller, wider right side.

parts.label: 弓
parts.name: bow-shaped component
parts.description: 弓 is the narrow three-stroke shape on the left, with two bends and a final hook.

parts.label: 長
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 長 fills the right side, with horizontal lines above and spreading strokes below.

幾.note: 幾 asks for a number. In 幾個, it takes the place of the number before the classifier.
幾.memory: Two small 幺 shapes sit side by side at the top of 幾. Below them, notice the crossing diagonals and the long hooked stroke.

parts.label: 幺幺
parts.name: paired upper shapes
parts.description: The first six strokes make two compact 幺 shapes: keep each small enough to fit beside the other.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: crossing lower strokes
parts.description: The last six strokes include the lower crossing slants and a long hooked stroke that starts between the upper shapes. Follow their order in the animation.

老.meaning: old; first syllable of 老師
老.note: 老師 (lǎoshī) means teacher. 老 places 耂 above 匕. A long slant cuts down through the upper horizontal strokes; the hooked lower shape tucks underneath.
老.memory: 老 places 耂 above 匕. A long slant cuts down through the upper horizontal strokes; the hooked lower shape tucks underneath.

parts.label: 耂
parts.name: 耂 component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the upper group: horizontal, vertical, another horizontal, then the long downward-left slant.

parts.label: 匕
parts.name: 匕 component
parts.description: The final two strokes form the compact hooked shape below. Keep it tucked under the spreading upper group.

師.note: 師 first appears in 老師 (lǎoshī), teacher. Recognize its shape while learning 老師 as one word.
師.memory: Remember 師 by its two stacked spaces on the left and a hanging 巾 shape under a bar on the right.

parts.label: 𠂤
parts.name: left group
parts.description: 𠂤 forms the left side, with a short top slant and two stacked, box-like spaces.

parts.label: 帀
parts.name: right group
parts.description: 帀 is a horizontal bar above 巾; its central vertical extends down through the hanging frame.

相.note: In 照相, read 相 as xiàng, with a fourth tone. Learn 照相 as the whole activity: taking photos.
相.memory: 相 places 木 beside 目. Recognize a tree-shaped left side and an eye-shaped rectangle with two inner lines.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: tree-shaped left side
parts.description: 木 takes the first four strokes on the left. Its final stroke becomes compact to make room for 目.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye-shaped right side
parts.description: 目 is the tall rectangle on the right with two short horizontal lines inside it.

電.note: 電影 (diànyǐng) means movie. 電 stacks the rain component 雨 over a lower box with a long hooked stroke. The final hook reaches down and curls to the right.
電.memory: 電 stacks the rain component 雨 over a lower box with a long hooked stroke. The final hook reaches down and curls to the right.

parts.label: 雨
parts.name: 雨 component
parts.description: The eight upper strokes form the rain component, including its small internal marks beneath the cover.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: The lower five strokes include the box-like middle and the long final hook. Keep the hook free to extend below the upper part.

影.note: 電影 (diànyǐng) means movie. 影 places 景 beside three slanting strokes 彡. On the left, 景 stacks 日 over 京; on the right, keep the three slants clearly separated.
影.memory: 影 places 景 beside three slanting strokes 彡. On the left, 景 stacks 日 over 京; on the right, keep the three slants clearly separated.

parts.label: 景
parts.name: 景 component
parts.description: The twelve strokes of 景 occupy the left side. Look for the upper 日 and the smaller stacked shapes below it.

parts.label: 彡
parts.name: 彡 component
parts.description: Three separate downward-left slants run along the right edge, with the lowest stroke reaching furthest down.

週.note: 週末 (zhōumò) means weekend. 週 wraps the movement component 辶 around 周. Write the inner 周 first, then finish the path that runs along its left and underneath it.
週.memory: 週 wraps the movement component 辶 around 周. Write the inner 周 first, then finish the path that runs along its left and underneath it.

parts.label: 周
parts.name: 周 component
parts.description: 周 is the enclosed inner component. Its upper and lower internal strokes fit inside the surrounding outline.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: 辶 component
parts.description: The Taiwan form here has four strokes in the movement component. Its final long stroke sweeps beneath 周.

末.note: 末 means end in 週末: the end of the week, or weekend.
末.memory: For 末, the TOP horizontal is longer than the horizontal below it. A vertical runs through both, with two sloping strokes spreading below.

parts.label: 末
parts.name: long top bar and spreading base
parts.description: Notice the long first horizontal, shorter second horizontal, central vertical, and two spreading final strokes. The long top bar identifies 末.

做.note: 做什麼 (zuò shénme) means do what. 做 has three visible columns: the person component 亻, 古 in the middle, and 攵 on the right. 古 itself is 十 above 口.
做.memory: 做 has three visible columns: the person component 亻, 古 in the middle, and 攵 on the right. 古 itself is 十 above 口.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: 亻 component
parts.description: The narrow two-stroke person component sits at the left. Keep it compact so the two groups to its right have room.

parts.label: 古
parts.name: 古 component
parts.description: 古 forms the middle column: a cross above a small mouth-shaped box. These five strokes come before the right component.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: 攵 component
parts.description: The final four strokes make the right-hand component. Its two longer diagonal strokes cross and spread outward.

游.note: 游泳 (yóuyǒng) means swim. 游 has 氵 at the left, 方 in the middle, and a small two-stroke top above 子 on the right. Do not confuse its right side with 永 in 泳.
游.memory: 游 has 氵 at the left, 方 in the middle, and a small two-stroke top above 子 on the right. Do not confuse its right side with 永 in 泳.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: 氵 component
parts.description: The first three strokes make the water component, a useful meaning clue for swimming.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: 方 component
parts.description: 方 occupies the middle column. Leave space to its right for the small top strokes and 子.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right-hand group
parts.description: The final five strokes form a two-stroke cap above 子. Notice the separate child-shaped group at the lower right.

泳.note: 泳 completes 游泳, to swim. Its water component helps you remember the activity.
泳.memory: 泳 is 氵 + 永. Put three water strokes on the left and the branching 永 shape on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The three strokes of 氵 sit along the left edge. Water is a useful meaning clue for swimming.

parts.label: 永
parts.name: right-hand sound component
parts.description: 永 suggests the yong syllable. Its central hooked stroke is surrounded by spreading side strokes; 泳 has a third tone.

常.note: 常 means often. Put it before the activity, as in 常看電影.
常.memory: 常 stacks a small spreading top, a cover and 口 above 巾. The final vertical descends through the lower hanging shape.

parts.label: 尚
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper eight strokes contain three small top strokes, a cover, and a 口 underneath that cover.

parts.label: 巾
parts.name: lower hanging shape
parts.description: 巾 forms the lower three strokes. Its final vertical runs down through the middle of the hanging outline.

吧.note: At the end of 我們去看電影吧, 吧 makes a friendly suggestion. Say ba lightly, without a tone mark.
吧.memory: 吧 is 口 + 巴. The small mouth on the left sits beside the hooked 巴 shape you saw under 爸.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: 口 occupies the first three strokes on the left, a useful clue for a particle used in speech.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 巴 occupies the right side. Notice its upper enclosed space and the rounded hook below, also seen in 爸.

今.note: 今 begins 今天, today. Learn the time word as a whole.
今.memory: 今 has a spreading roof, a dot beneath it, and a bent final stroke. Keep that dot separate from the lower bend; do not add the extra dot of 令.

parts.label: top
parts.name: spreading roof
parts.description: The first two sloping strokes meet at the top and open outward, making space beneath their meeting point.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: dot and bend
parts.description: Place a small dot under the roof, then the single bent final stroke below it. These are two separate strokes.

天.meaning: day; sky (in 今天 and 明天)
天.note: 明天 (míngtiān) means tomorrow. 天 has two horizontal strokes above two spreading slants. Compare it with 大: 天 has an extra horizontal across the top.
天.memory: 天 has two horizontal strokes above two spreading slants. Compare it with 大: 天 has an extra horizontal across the top.

parts.label: 天
parts.name: 天 component
parts.description: Write the short top horizontal, the longer horizontal below, then the two sloping strokes that spread into a broad base.

明.note: 明 begins 明天, tomorrow. Its shapes are 日 and 月.
明.memory: 明 places 日 on the left and the taller 月 on the right. Compare the closed bottom of 日 with the longer downward strokes of 月.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun-shaped left side
parts.description: Make the four strokes of 日 on the left, including its short inner horizontal. Keep it narrower than the whole character.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: moon-shaped right side
parts.description: 月 uses four strokes on the right. Its long outer strokes surround two short horizontal strokes.

覺.note: 覺得 (juéde) means think; feel (an opinion). 覺 has the same complex upper group you saw in 學, but 見 underneath instead of 子. The lower 見 contains 目 above two spreading legs.
覺.memory: 覺 has the same complex upper group you saw in 學, but 見 underneath instead of 子. The lower 見 contains 目 above two spreading legs.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper thirteen strokes form the covered group shared with 學. Keep its small inner crossing strokes compact.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: 見 component
parts.description: The lower seven strokes form 見: a tall eye-shaped 目 with two legs below. This lower group distinguishes 覺 from 學.

得.meaning: light final syllable in 覺得
得.note: 覺得 (juéde) means think; feel (an opinion). 得 has 彳 on the left and a stacked right side: 日, a horizontal, and 寸. In 覺得, say the final de lightly; other words can use dé or děi.
得.memory: 得 has 彳 on the left and a stacked right side: 日, a horizontal, and 寸. In 覺得, say the final de lightly; other words can use dé or děi.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: 彳 component
parts.description: The left component has two short slants and a vertical. Keep its three strokes narrow alongside the taller right-hand stack.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right-hand group
parts.description: The eight strokes on the right stack 日 over a horizontal and 寸. Notice the small dot beside the lower hooked vertical.

玩.note: 玩 has a second tone in 好玩, fun. 好玩 describes an activity as enjoyable.
玩.memory: 玩 puts the narrow jade component 王 beside 元. On the right, notice two horizontal bars above two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: jade component
parts.description: The left side looks like a narrow 王. As a component here it represents jade; its final stroke rises toward the right.

parts.label: 元
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 元 has two horizontal strokes above two legs, the right one ending in a hook. Leave space between those lower strokes.

起.note: 起 completes 一起, together. 一起 goes before the shared action.
起.memory: 起 combines 走 with 巳 tucked at the right. The long final stroke of 走 sweeps beneath the right-hand component.

parts.label: 走
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: The seven strokes of 走 occupy the left and lower part. Its sweeping base extends under the whole character.

parts.label: 巳
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The three strokes of 巳 fit on the right above the sweeping base. In this Taiwan form, notice the closed upper space.

怎.note: 怎 first appears in 怎麼樣 (zěnmeyàng), how does that sound? Learn the whole expression together.
怎.memory: Remember 怎 as 乍 above 心: a compact top with a wider heart shape below.

parts.label: 乍
parts.name: upper part
parts.description: 乍 has a short slant at the top and horizontal strokes extending right from a vertical.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: 心 sits below 乍, with dots around a curved hook.

樣.note: 怎麼樣 (zěnmeyàng) means how does that sound?. 樣 puts 木 beside 羕. The right side has a sheep-shaped upper group over a branching, water-like lower group with a central hook.
樣.memory: 樣 puts 木 beside 羕. The right side has a sheep-shaped upper group over a branching, water-like lower group with a central hook.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: 木 component
parts.description: 木 is the four-stroke tree component on the left. Its final stroke becomes compact beside the wider right component.

parts.label: 羕
parts.name: 羕 component
parts.description: The eleven right-hand strokes form 羕. Keep the upper horizontal bars orderly and leave room for the branching lower strokes.

啊.note: 好啊 (hǎo a) means sure!; OK!. 啊 has a small mouth 口 on the left and 阿 on the right. Inside 阿, notice the narrow ear-shaped component beside 可.
啊.memory: 啊 has a small mouth 口 on the left and 阿 on the right. Inside 阿, notice the narrow ear-shaped component beside 可.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: 口 component
parts.description: The first three strokes make a small mouth component, a useful clue for a particle used in speech.

parts.label: 阿
parts.name: 阿 component
parts.description: The right eight strokes form 阿: a narrow left-side 阝 followed by 可. Keep the small inner box of 可 distinct.

可.note: 可 begins 可以. Here 可以 describes a possibility, not a learned skill.
可.memory: 可 has a long top bar, a small 口 beneath it, and a final vertical hook on the right. Keep the small box inside the space under the bar.

parts.label: 可
parts.name: bar, box, and right hook
parts.description: Write the top horizontal, then the three strokes of the small 口, and finish with the long right-side vertical hook.

以.note: 可以 (kěyǐ) means can (possibility). 以 has a short vertical and a rising stroke on the left, a separate dot in the middle, and two longer sloping strokes on the right. In this Taiwan form, the left side takes two strokes.
以.memory: 以 has a short vertical and a rising stroke on the left, a separate dot in the middle, and two longer sloping strokes on the right. In this Taiwan form, the left side takes two strokes.

parts.label: 以
parts.name: 以 component
parts.description: Write the short left vertical, then the rising stroke, then the central dot. Finish with the two longer right-hand strokes. This source Taiwan form has five strokes, not four.

音.note: 音 is the first character of 音樂 (yīnyuè), music. It has 立 above 日. Keep the lower box narrower than the long horizontal above it.
音.memory: For 音, place the five-stroke 立 over a four-stroke 日. The top and bottom share one vertical centre.

parts.label: 立
parts.name: upper standing shape
parts.description: Write the dot, horizontal, two inward strokes, and long horizontal of 立 before the lower box.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: lower sun-shaped box
