parts.description: Under 立, write the upright 日 box with one horizontal line inside. This is a visible shape cue.

樂.note: In 音樂 (yīnyuè), 樂 is pronounced yuè. The Taiwan stroke sequence starts with the central 白, then the two small 幺 groups, and finishes with 木 below.
樂.memory: Find the central 白, one curled 幺 on each side, and a wide 木 base. Three upper groups balance over the lower wood shape.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: central white-shaped box
parts.description: Begin with the five strokes of 白 in the upper centre; do not begin with the far-left curl.

parts.label: 幺
parts.name: left curled group
parts.description: Three compact strokes curl down the left of 白. Leave space between the curl and the centre.

parts.label: 幺
parts.name: right curled group
parts.description: Write the matching three-stroke curl to the right of 白 after completing the left one.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood base
parts.description: Finish with four strokes below: a horizontal, central vertical, and two spreading lower strokes.

運.note: 運 begins 運動 (yùndòng), to exercise. Write the inner 軍 first, then the four-stroke Taiwan movement component 辶 around its left and bottom.
運.memory: 運 has a covered 車 inside 軍, resting above the long sweeping path of 辶. Finish the outside path last.

parts.label: 軍
parts.name: inner covered vehicle shape
parts.description: The nine inner strokes form 軍: a two-stroke cover above 車. Keep the inner group high enough for the path below.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement surround
parts.description: Four strokes form the Taiwan movement component. Its final long sweep supports the entire inner 軍.

動.meaning: move; second syllable of 運動
動.note: 動 is the second character of 運動 (yùndòng). The left component is 重; the two strokes of 力 sit on the right.
動.memory: Keep the layered 重 tall and compact, then add the hooked 力 and its slant on the right.

parts.label: 重
parts.name: layered left component
parts.description: The nine strokes of 重 include a central vertical and stacked horizontal lines. Finish this entire left component first.

parts.label: 力
parts.name: strength component
parts.description: A bent hook and a falling leftward stroke form 力 on the right. The hook leaves room for the final slant.

打.note: 打 is used in 打籃球, play basketball. Learn each sport with its own action verb.
打.memory: 打 is 扌 + 丁: the narrow hand component stands beside a horizontal bar with a vertical hook.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: 扌 forms the three strokes on the left. The hand component suits an activity done with the hands.

parts.label: 丁
parts.name: right-hand bar and hook
parts.description: 丁 has just two strokes: a horizontal above a vertical hook. Keep that simple right side open.

籃.note: 籃球 (lánqiú) means basketball. 籃 has the bamboo component 竹 at the top and 監 below. At the bottom of 監, a wide 皿 forms a stable base.
籃.memory: 籃 has the bamboo component 竹 at the top and 監 below. At the bottom of 監, a wide 皿 forms a stable base.

parts.label: 竹
parts.name: 竹 component
parts.description: The six top strokes form the compact bamboo component. Its two small groups sit side by side above the larger lower part.

parts.label: 監
parts.name: 監 component
parts.description: The fourteen strokes below the bamboo form 監. Notice its upper clusters above the long, shallow 皿 at the bottom.

球.note: 足球 (zúqiú) means soccer; football. 球 is 王 beside 求. The left jade component is narrow; 求 spreads out around a central hooked vertical on the right.
球.memory: 球 is 王 beside 求. The left jade component is narrow; 求 spreads out around a central hooked vertical on the right.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: 王 component
parts.description: The four-stroke jade component looks like a narrow 王. Its final stroke rises toward the right in this side form.

parts.label: 求
parts.name: 求 component
parts.description: 求 includes a central hooked stroke and spreading marks on both sides. Remember the small dot near its upper right.

踢.note: 踢足球 (tī zúqiú) means play soccer; football. 踢 places the foot component 足 beside 易. The foot is a useful clue for kicking; 易 has 日 above two slants inside a hooked outline.
踢.memory: 踢 places the foot component 足 beside 易. The foot is a useful clue for kicking; 易 has 日 above two slants inside a hooked outline.

parts.label: 足
parts.name: 足 component
parts.description: The left foot component begins with 口, then narrows beneath it. Its final rising stroke makes room for the right side.

parts.label: 易
parts.name: 易 component
parts.description: The eight strokes on the right make 易: 日 above a hooked lower group with two inner slants.

足.note: 足 means foot. It begins 足球, soccer/football, the sport played by kicking the ball.
足.memory: 足 has 口 above a lower group that stretches down and then across to the right, like a planted foot.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: upper mouth-shaped box
parts.description: The first three strokes form a small 口 at the top of 足. This is a shape cue, not a literal explanation of the meaning.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower leg and foot shape
parts.description: Below 口, a central vertical and short bar lead into two spreading strokes. The final stroke makes a long base to the right.

網.note: 網球 (wǎngqiú) means tennis. 網 has the thread component 糹 on the left and 罔 on the right; the thread shape is a useful memory cue for a net.
網.memory: A narrow 糹 stands beside the wider frame of 罔. Keep the three final dots of 糹 distinct before moving to the right side.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: Six strokes make the narrow thread component, including three small finishing dots. Complete all six before the right frame.

parts.label: 罔
parts.name: right framed component
parts.description: Eight strokes form 罔. Start with the outer left and hooked top-right frame, then write the small shapes inside it.

還.note: 還是 (háishì) means or (in a choice question). 還 places 睘 inside the movement component 辶. Look for the wide net-shaped top inside, and the long path sweeping underneath.
還.memory: 還 places 睘 inside the movement component 辶. Look for the wide net-shaped top inside, and the long path sweeping underneath.

parts.label: 睘
parts.name: 睘 component
parts.description: The thirteen inner strokes form 睘, beginning with a wide net-shaped box. Keep the smaller shapes below it centered.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: 辶 component
parts.description: Write the four-stroke Taiwan movement component last, down the left and across the base. In 還是, read 還 as hái, not huán.

早.note: 早 begins 早上, morning. Notice 日 above 十.
早.memory: 早 stacks a compact 日 over 十. The last vertical passes through the lower horizontal, not through the box above it.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: upper box
parts.description: The first four strokes form 日. Keep this box centered above the lower crossing strokes.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: lower cross
parts.description: Write the broad horizontal below 日, then the vertical through that horizontal to complete 十.

上.meaning: final syllable in 早上 and 晚上
上.note: 早上 (zǎoshàng) means morning. 上 has a vertical, a short horizontal to its right, and a long base line. The small bar sits above the base, which helps distinguish 上 from 下.
上.memory: 上 has a vertical, a short horizontal to its right, and a long base line. The small bar sits above the base, which helps distinguish 上 from 下.

parts.label: 上
parts.name: 上 component
parts.description: Begin with the vertical, add the short bar to its right, and finish with the long horizontal base. Keep the short bar above that base.

晚.note: 晚 appears in 晚上, evening, and 晚飯, dinner.
晚.memory: 晚 has 日 on the left and 免 on the right. The right side begins with a small slant and bend above a box, then spreads into two lower strokes.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun-shaped left side
parts.description: The four strokes of 日 make a compact box at the left. Keep enough space for the wider 免 on the right.

parts.label: 免
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The seven strokes of 免 include an upper slant and bend, a box-like middle, and two spreading lower strokes.

吃.note: 吃晚飯 (chī wǎnfàn) means eat dinner. 吃 puts 口 beside 乞. The right side has a short slant and horizontal above a bent hook; do not add an extra horizontal to 乞.
吃.memory: 吃 puts 口 beside 乞. The right side has a short slant and horizontal above a bent hook; keep 乞 to three clear strokes without an extra horizontal.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: 口 component
parts.description: The first three strokes make the mouth-shaped box on the left. A mouth is a useful meaning clue for eating.

parts.label: 乞
parts.name: 乞 component
parts.description: The right side has three strokes: a short slant, a short horizontal, then a long bent hook below them.

飯.note: 飯 completes 晚飯, dinner. The food component is the Traditional form 飠.
飯.memory: 飯 places the narrow food component 飠 beside 反. The right side starts with a sloping cover above two crossing lower strokes.

parts.label: 飠
parts.name: food component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the food component on the left, a useful meaning clue for a meal.

parts.label: 反
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 反 uses four strokes on the right: two upper sloping strokes above the crossing lower strokes of 又.

菜.note: 菜 can refer to dishes or a style of cooking. Here it names a cuisine after a country name.
菜.memory: 菜 has the grass top 艹 above 采. In this Taiwan form, the grass top uses four strokes; below it, a claw-like top sits over 木.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass top
parts.description: Write the four short strokes across the top in two groups. This plant-related component gives a useful clue to the food meaning.

parts.label: 采
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The next four strokes form the claw-like top of 采, and the last four form 木 below. Keep 采 centered under 艹.

越.meaning: first syllable of 越南, Vietnam
越.note: In this unit, learn 越 as part of the country name 越南. It is not a new comparison pattern.
越.memory: 走 runs down the left and stretches underneath 戉 on the right. The long lower stroke supports the right-hand component.

parts.label: 走
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: These seven strokes form 走, with 土 above the lower strokes. Its long final stroke extends under the right side.

parts.label: 戉
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: Five strokes form 戉. Notice its bent strokes, long diagonal hook, and final small mark at the upper right.

南.meaning: final syllable of 越南, Vietnam
南.note: 南 completes 越南, Vietnam. The country name is pronounced Yuènán, with fourth tone then second tone.
南.memory: 南 begins with 十. Beneath it, an open-bottom frame surrounds two short marks and the lower crossing strokes.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: top cross
parts.description: The horizontal and vertical form a cross above the wide lower frame.

parts.label: 冂
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The left vertical and the top-right hooked stroke make the frame, open at its base.

parts.label: 𢆉
parts.name: inner strokes
parts.description: Two short inward marks sit above two horizontal strokes. Finish with the central vertical through those horizontals.

杯.meaning: cup; measure word for cups of a drink
杯.note: 杯 counts cups of a drink: 一杯茶. Use it in place of the general measure word 個 for this meaning.
杯.memory: 杯 places 木 on the left and the familiar 不 on the right. Keep the left 木 narrow so the two sides stay distinct.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood component
parts.description: Write the horizontal, vertical, left-falling stroke, then the small right-hand stroke of the narrow 木.

parts.label: 不
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The four strokes form 不. Recognize the shape, but do not read this component as a negative inside 杯.

熱.note: 熱 describes temperature: 熱咖啡 is hot coffee. It does not mean that the coffee tastes good.
熱.memory: 熱 has a broad upper 埶 and four separate fire dots 灬 below. Keep the bottom dots distinct from the small upper marks.

parts.label: 埶
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: These eleven strokes form the broad upper structure. Its left side is built from short crossing strokes; its right side has a curved hook and a dot.

parts.label: 灬
parts.name: fire dots
parts.description: Finish with four separate dots spread across the base. This fire component helps recall the meaning hot.

買.note: 買 means to buy. 想買 means would like to buy; the verb 買 comes before the thing being bought.
買.memory: 買 stacks a wide 罒 over 貝. The lower 貝 has a tall box and two spreading strokes at its feet.

parts.label: 罒
parts.name: top frame
parts.description: These five strokes make the wide top frame with internal vertical divisions.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: shell component
parts.description: Seven strokes form 貝 below. Keep its inner horizontals inside the tall box, then add the two lower strokes. 貝 is a useful clue to money-related meanings.

外.meaning: outside; first syllable of 外帶
外.note: 外 begins 外帶, to go. Learn the complete expression for taking an order away.
外.memory: 外 puts 夕 on the left and 卜 on the right. The small inner mark of 夕 stays inside the left shape.

parts.label: 夕
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write the short left-falling stroke, the longer bent stroke, then the small inner mark.

parts.label: 卜
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the tall vertical and then the short mark to its right. Leave a clear gap from 夕.

帶.meaning: carry; final syllable of 外帶
帶.note: 帶 completes 外帶, to go. Both syllables have fourth tone: wàidài.
帶.memory: 帶 has an interlocking top, a broad cover 冖, and a hanging 巾 below. The final vertical runs through the lower cloth-shaped part.

parts.label: 廿 + 儿
parts.name: upper structure
parts.description: The first six strokes form the interlocking top and its two lower turns. Keep this structure above the separate cover.

parts.label: 冖
parts.name: middle cover
parts.description: The next two strokes make a wide cover over the lower 巾.

parts.label: 巾
parts.name: cloth component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 巾. Its long central vertical drops below the side strokes.

內.meaning: inside; first syllable of 內用
內.note: 內 begins 內用, for here. Notice the Traditional form: the shape inside is 入.
內.memory: 內 surrounds 入 with an open-bottom frame 冂. The two inner slanting strokes stay within the frame.

parts.label: 冂
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: Write the left side, then the top-and-right hooked stroke to make an open-bottom frame.

parts.label: 入
parts.name: inside component
parts.description: The last two strokes form 入 inside the frame. Watch where the two slanting strokes meet near the top.

用.meaning: use; final syllable of 內用
用.note: 用 completes 內用, for here. At a drink counter, this means you will have your drink on the premises.
用.memory: 用 has a tall outer frame, two inner horizontal bars, and one long central vertical through them.

parts.label: 用
parts.name: use component
parts.description: Begin with the left side and the hooked top-right side. Add the two inner horizontals, then finish with the central vertical.

二.note: 二 names the number two. When counting two cups, keep the familiar 兩杯. Learn 二 for naming the number itself.
二.memory: Two separate horizontal lines: the upper line is shorter, the lower line wider.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: upper horizontal
parts.description: Write the shorter upper line first, leaving space beneath it.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: lower horizontal
parts.description: Write the longer lower line underneath; the two lines never touch.

三.note: 三 names the number three. 三杯茶 is three cups of tea.
三.memory: Three separate horizontal lines: the middle is shortest and the bottom is widest.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top horizontal
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal first. Keep it separate from the middle line.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: middle horizontal
parts.description: The second horizontal is shorter. Leave a clear gap above and below it.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: bottom horizontal
parts.description: Finish with the longest horizontal to give 三 a broad base.

四.note: 四 names the number four. Its pronunciation sì has a falling fourth tone.
四.memory: 四 has an outer box around two inner strokes. Close the bottom of the box last.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: Start with the left side and the hooked top-right side. The bottom horizontal closes the enclosure after the inside is written.

parts.label: 儿
parts.name: inner strokes
parts.description: Inside the box, write a left-falling stroke and a bent stroke. Keep them clear of the outer sides.

五.note: 五 names the number five. 五杯茶 is five cups of tea.
五.memory: 五 has a short upper bar, a descending inner stroke, a bent middle stroke, and a broad bottom bar.

parts.label: 五
parts.name: 五 strokes
parts.description: Write the top horizontal, the descending stroke, the horizontal-turn stroke, then the long bottom horizontal. The third stroke turns downward on the right.

六.note: 六 names the number six. Keep its falling fourth tone: liù.
六.memory: 六 has a dot and a long horizontal above two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top dot and bar
parts.description: Write the top dot, then the horizontal underneath it.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: lower strokes
parts.description: Finish with the left-falling stroke and the short right-hand dot. They spread apart below the bar.

七.note: 七 names the number seven. Its high first tone is qī.
七.memory: 七 crosses a rising horizontal with a vertical that bends right into a hook.

parts.label: 七
parts.name: 七 strokes
parts.description: Write the slightly rising horizontal first. The second stroke drops through it, turns right, and finishes with a small hook.

八.note: 八 names the number eight. The two strokes separate rather than meeting at the top.
八.memory: 八 opens outward: a shorter left-falling stroke and a longer right-falling stroke.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: 八 strokes
parts.description: Write the left-falling stroke first and the right-falling stroke second. Leave a gap between their upper ends.

九.note: 九 names the number nine. Pronounce it jiǔ, with third tone.
九.memory: 九 starts with a curved left-falling stroke. Its second stroke crosses it, turns down, and hooks up at the lower right.

parts.label: 九
parts.name: 九 strokes
parts.description: Write the left-falling stroke first. Then draw the short horizontal into a downward curve and finish the hooked turn.

十.note: 十 names ten. Its rising tone shí is different from the falling sì of 四.
十.memory: 十 is a simple cross. The vertical passes through the horizontal and extends above and below it.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: 十 strokes
parts.description: Write the horizontal first. Write one vertical through it, keeping the crossing near the middle.

錢.note: 錢 means money. After a price such as 三十五塊, it is optional: 三十五塊錢 gives the same price.
錢.memory: 錢 places the metal component 金 on the left and two stacked 戈 shapes on the right.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: metal component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the narrow metal component. Its top opens into a cover above the lower bars and dots.

parts.label: 戔
parts.name: stacked right-hand component
parts.description: Two four-stroke 戈 shapes are stacked on the right. Keep their long slanting hooks and small dots distinct.

塊.note: 塊 follows an amount in everyday prices. In these Taiwan drink-shop examples, 三十塊 means NT$30.
塊.memory: 塊 has 土 on the left and 鬼 on the right. The right side is much wider than the three-stroke 土.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth component
parts.description: Write the small horizontal, vertical, and rising lower stroke on the left.

parts.label: 鬼
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The ten strokes of 鬼 begin with a short slant over a box, then continue into the curved lower strokes and small inner mark.

多.meaning: first syllable of 多少, how much/how many
多.note: 多 begins 多少. Learn 多少 as one question word here; do not translate the characters separately.
多.memory: 多 stacks two 夕 shapes. The lower one sits slightly farther to the right.

parts.label: 夕
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the upper 夕: a short slant, a longer bent stroke, and an inner mark.

parts.label: 夕
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Repeat the three-stroke 夕 below, leaving room between the two components.

少.meaning: final syllable of 多少, how much/how many
少.note: 少 completes 多少. Keep the third tone in duōshǎo.
少.memory: 少 resembles 小 with an extra long left-falling stroke below. That last stroke sweeps under the upper marks.

parts.label: 小
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: Write the short central vertical and the two side marks at the top.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: long final stroke
parts.description: Finish with a long left-falling stroke that begins on the right and sweeps underneath the upper strokes.

共.note: 共 completes 一共, altogether. In this expression 一 is pronounced yí before the fourth-tone gòng.
共.memory: 共 has two upright strokes through two horizontal bars, with two short spreading strokes below.

parts.label: 龷
parts.name: upper structure
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal, the two verticals, then the wider lower horizontal across them.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: lower strokes
parts.description: Finish with the two spreading lower strokes, leaving a gap below the upper structure.

闆.note: 闆 completes 老闆, a shop owner or boss. The spoken word has two third tones; keep the dictionary spelling lǎobǎn.
闆.memory: Three small mouths sit inside the 門 frame. Keep space between all three boxes.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: outer door frame
parts.description: The eight-stroke 門 encloses the inside on the top and both sides.

parts.label: 品
parts.name: three inner mouths
parts.description: Write the upper 口, then the lower left and lower right 口 inside the frame.

問.note: In 請問, 問 introduces a question politely.
問.memory: Picture 口 inside 門: a small mouth enclosed by a tall doorway.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: door frame
parts.description: 門 makes the outer frame and stays open at the bottom.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth inside
parts.description: 口 is the small three-stroke box inside the lower part of 門.

包.meaning: first syllable of 包子, a filled steamed bun
包.note: 包 begins 包子. Learn the food name as a whole word; this card is not teaching a separate order for a bag.
包.memory: The curved outer 勹 wraps around the small 巳 shape, like a wrapper around a filling.

parts.label: 勹
parts.name: outer wrapping shape
parts.description: Begin with a short left-falling stroke and the long bent hook around the top and right.

parts.label: 巳
parts.name: inner curled shape
parts.description: The three inner strokes make 巳, finishing with the curved stroke at the bottom.

子.note: The dictionary reading is zǐ. In 包子 the suffix is neutral-tone zi: bāozi.
子.memory: 子 has a bent top, a central hooked stroke, and a horizontal stroke through the middle.

parts.label: 子
parts.name: three-stroke 子
parts.description: Write the bent top, central hooked stroke, then the horizontal crossing through it.

幫.meaning: for; on behalf of (in 幫我…)
幫.note: In 請幫我買茶, 幫 introduces the person benefiting from the action: please buy tea for me.
幫.memory: 封 sits above 帛. Keep the lower white box and hanging cloth shape centered under the wide top.

parts.label: 封
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Write the upper 封 structure, with its stacked 土 shapes and 寸 on the right.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: middle box
parts.description: Write 白 beneath the top, including the short slant above its box.

parts.label: 巾
parts.name: lower cloth shape
parts.description: Finish with 巾 below 白; the central vertical extends downward.

微.meaning: first syllable of 微波, to microwave
微.note: Use second-tone wéi in 微波 wéibō.
微.memory: A narrow 彳 stands left of a mountain-and-legs middle; the four-stroke 攵 finishes at the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: left stepping component
parts.description: Two short slants and a vertical make the narrow left component.

parts.label: 山兀
parts.name: middle structure
parts.description: Write the three-stroke 山, the horizontal below it, then the two lower leg strokes.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Finish the right side with a short slant, horizontal, longer left-falling stroke and right-falling stroke.

波.note: 波 means wave; 微波 literally refers to microwaves and is used as the verb to microwave here.
波.memory: The three water strokes 氵 are on the left, with 皮 on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: Place the three water strokes down the left, with the last one rising.

parts.label: 皮
parts.name: right component
parts.description: In the Taiwan sequence, start 皮 with the long left-falling stroke, then the bent top, vertical, and two lower crossing strokes.

百.note: 百 names the hundreds place. 一百 is one hundred, pronounced yìbǎi in these examples.
百.memory: A single horizontal roof sits above 白. Unlike 白 alone, 百 has that extra top line.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top horizontal
parts.description: Begin with the long horizontal line above the rest of the character.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the slant into the lower 白 and its box with the inner horizontal.

零.note: 零 names zero. Inside a number such as 一百零五, it marks the missing tens place.
零.memory: Rain 雨 sits over 令: keep the rain dots above the pointed lower component.

parts.label: 雨
parts.name: rain component
parts.description: Write the rain roof and frame, central vertical, and the four small rain marks.

parts.label: 令
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the two slanting top strokes of 令, then its central mark and lower bent strokes.

千.note: 千 is one thousand, ten times 百. 一千 is pronounced yìqiān.
千.memory: 千 looks like 十 with a short slant added above. Do not mistake it for the straight-topped 干.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: top slant
parts.description: Start with the short left-falling stroke across the top.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: cross below
parts.description: Write the horizontal and then the vertical crossing through it.

萬.note: 萬 groups ten thousands. 一萬 is 10,000, not 1,000. Use the Traditional form 萬.
萬.memory: The four-stroke grass top covers 禺, whose lower tail reaches down on the right.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: Taiwan grass top
parts.description: The Taiwan glyph writes the grass top with four strokes, as two separated crosses.

parts.label: 禺
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the box and crossing strokes of 禺, then the lower enclosure, hook and final inner mark.

賣.note: 賣 mài, fourth tone, means sell. Compare the earlier 買 mǎi, third tone, meaning buy.
賣.memory: 賣 adds a three-stroke 士 above 買. That extra top distinguishes selling from buying.

parts.label: 士
parts.name: top component
parts.description: Write the top horizontal, vertical and shorter lower horizontal of 士.

parts.label: 罒
parts.name: middle net
parts.description: Write the wide five-stroke net shape in the middle.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: lower shell component
parts.description: Write 貝 with its stacked box lines and the two short lower strokes.

手.note: 手 is hand. Together with 機 it forms 手機, mobile phone; learn the complete device name.
手.memory: Two horizontal levels and a short top slant are crossed by the long central hook.

parts.label: 手
parts.name: four-stroke hand
parts.description: Write the short top slant, the two horizontal strokes, then the central vertical hook.

機.note: 機 completes 手機. Keep the Traditional 木 + 幾 structure; the small side dots are part of the character.
機.memory: Wood 木 stands to the left of the familiar 幾 shape from 幾個.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: left wood component
parts.description: Keep 木 narrow, with a short final dot to leave room for the right half.

parts.label: 幾
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The twelve-stroke 幾 has two small thread shapes at the top and crossed strokes below.

支.note: Use 支 to count phones: 一支手機, one phone. Use 兩支 for two.
支.memory: A small 十 sits above the spreading 又 shape.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: upper cross
parts.description: Write the horizontal and vertical in the upper part.

parts.label: 又
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the bent left-falling stroke and the long right-falling stroke below.

新.note: 新 describes a new item. Put it before 手機 for a new phone, or use 很新 to describe the phone.
新.memory: A dense 亲 shape sits beside the open strokes of 斤 on the right.

parts.label: 亲
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write the upper 立-like strokes and the lower wood-like strokes on the left.

parts.label: 斤
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Finish with the two slants, horizontal and vertical of 斤.

舊.note: 舊 means old or not new for an item such as a phone. Do not use it to state a person’s age.
舊.memory: The grass top and 隹 bird shape sit over the mortar-shaped 臼 at the bottom.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: Taiwan grass top
parts.description: Write the four-stroke grass top with two separated crosses.

parts.label: 隹
parts.name: middle bird component
parts.description: Write the compact 隹 below the grass top, keeping its horizontal lines distinct.

parts.label: 臼
parts.name: lower mortar shape
parts.description: Finish 臼 with inward-facing short lines and a connected lower edge.

貴.note: 貴 describes a high price. 很貴 means expensive; 不貴 means not expensive.
貴.memory: A compact crossed top rests on 貝, the shell component also visible in money-related characters.

parts.label: 𠀐
parts.name: upper structure
parts.description: Write the upper box with its central crossing vertical and the horizontal beneath it.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: lower shell
parts.description: Write the lower 貝 box, its inner lines and two short spreading strokes.

便.meaning: first syllable of 便宜, inexpensive
便.note: In 便宜, read 便 as pián, second tone. The reading biàn belongs to other words.
便.memory: A narrow person 亻 stands left of the crossed box of 更.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: Write the short slant and vertical on the left.

parts.label: 更
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the top horizontal and box-like center of 更, then the long crossing lower strokes.

宜.meaning: final syllable of 便宜, inexpensive
宜.note: Here 便宜 is piányí, with second-tone yí.
宜.memory: A roof 宀 covers the tiered lines of 且.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof component
parts.description: Write the top dot, left roof mark and bent roof stroke.

parts.label: 且
parts.name: lower tiers
parts.description: Write 且 under the roof: the upright frame, internal horizontal lines and long base.

種.note: 種 is zhǒng, third tone, when it means kind or type. 一種手機 is one kind of phone.
種.memory: 禾 stands next to the dense stacked lines of 重.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: left grain component
parts.description: Write the top slant, horizontal, vertical and two lower marks of 禾.

parts.label: 重
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the layered 重 with its central vertical and horizontal base lines.

太.note: 太 before a description means too or overly. In 太貴了 it expresses that the price is too high.
太.memory: 太 is 大 with an extra dot underneath its crossing strokes.

parts.label: 大
parts.name: large spreading strokes
parts.description: Write the horizontal, left-falling and right-falling strokes of 大.

parts.label: 丶
parts.name: lower dot
parts.description: Add the dot below the center; it distinguishes 太 from 大.

了.note: Here 了 ends 太…了 and adds emphasis to the speaker’s reaction. It does not make this sentence past tense.
了.memory: 了 has only a bent top and a curved vertical hook. It has no crossing horizontal like 子.

parts.label: 乛
parts.name: bent top
parts.description: Write the top horizontal with its short downward bend.

parts.label: 亅
parts.name: lower hook
parts.description: Write the longer curved vertical hook below.

為.meaning: first syllable of 為什麼, why
為.note: Use fourth-tone wèi in 為什麼 wèishénme, why. Other uses of 為 can have a different tone.
為.memory: Follow the descending bends in the upper structure, then place four dots along the bottom.

parts.label: 為
parts.name: upper bent structure
parts.description: Write the top dot and slant, followed by the three descending bent strokes.

parts.label: 灬
parts.name: four lower dots
parts.description: Finish with four separate dots along the bottom, from left to right.

能.note: 能 describes capability here: a phone can take pictures or go online. 不能 places 不 before 能.
能.memory: 厶 and a month-like box fill the left; two spoon-like 匕 shapes sit on the right.

parts.label: 厶
parts.name: upper left component
parts.description: Write the bent stroke and small dot at the upper left.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: lower left component
parts.description: Write the narrow box under 厶 and its two inner horizontals.

parts.label: 匕匕
parts.name: two right components
parts.description: Write the upper two-stroke 匕, then repeat the shape below.

牛.note: 牛 names cattle. In 牛肉, the whole word means beef; do not mistake it for pork.
牛.memory: A short slant sits over two horizontal levels, with a central vertical passing through them.

parts.label: 牛
parts.name: four-stroke structure
parts.description: Write the top slant, the short upper horizontal, the longer lower horizontal, then the central vertical.

肉.note: 肉 means meat. 牛肉 specifies beef; the animal name 牛 tells you which meat it is.
肉.memory: Two small person-like shapes sit one above the other inside a broad open-bottom frame.

parts.label: 冂
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: Write the left vertical, then the top-and-right bent hook, leaving the bottom open.

parts.label: 仌
parts.name: two inner shapes
parts.description: Write the upper pair of inward slants, then the lower pair, inside the frame.

麵.note: Use the Traditional character 麵 for noodles. 牛肉麵 combines beef with noodles.
麵.memory: The grain component 麥 is on the left; the box-like 面 fills the right.

parts.label: 麥
parts.name: left grain component
parts.description: Write the compact 麥 structure on the left, including its descending lower strokes.

parts.label: 面
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the top line and slant of 面, then its outer frame, inner strokes and closing lower horizontal.

湯.note: 湯 is soup or broth. In this food context, describe pleasant broth with the familiar 好喝.
湯.memory: Water 氵 stands beside 昜, whose lower strokes descend below the small sun shape.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: Place the three water strokes down the left side, with a rising final stroke.

parts.label: 昜
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper 日, the horizontal below it, and the bent stroke and descending slants underneath.

真.note: 真 before a description means really here: 真好吃, really delicious. It is an adverb in this sentence, not a noun naming food.
真.memory: A small 十 sits above a tall box, a broad base line, and two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: upper cross
parts.description: Start with the short horizontal and the vertical crossing it.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: middle box
parts.description: Write the upright box with its three inner or closing horizontal lines.

parts.label: 一八
parts.name: base and feet
parts.description: Write the broad horizontal base, then the two short strokes spreading below it.

名.note: 有名 means famous or well-known. Learn that meaning as the complete word rather than translating it as have a name.
名.memory: 夕 sits above 口; keep the lower box centered under the top shape.

parts.label: 夕
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Write the short left-falling stroke, the longer bent stroke and the inner mark of 夕.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower box
parts.description: Finish with the three-stroke 口 below.

店.note: 店 is a shop or store. 牛肉麵店 is a shop specializing in beef noodles.
店.memory: The sloping roof 广 shelters 占, with its small box at the bottom.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: outer roof
parts.description: Write the top dot, horizontal roof and long left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 占
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: Write the short vertical and horizontal above the three-stroke 口.

最.note: 最 before 喜歡 marks your strongest preference: 最喜歡, like most. It does not mean often.
最.memory: The flat top box covers 取; the lower right 又 spreads away from the ear-like left shape.

parts.label: 冃
parts.name: upper box
parts.description: Write the low rectangular top with its two horizontal interior or closing strokes.

parts.label: 取
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the six-stroke 耳 on the lower left, then the two crossing strokes of 又 on the right.

點.note: 點 is used here to order food. 點一碗麵 means order one bowl of noodles; other meanings of 點 are for later lessons.
點.memory: 黑 fills the left side with four dots at the bottom; 占 makes a narrower right-hand block.

parts.label: 黑
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write 黑 on the left, keeping its internal horizontals and four bottom dots distinct.

parts.label: 占
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the short vertical, horizontal and three-stroke 口 on the right.

碗.meaning: bowl; measure for bowls of food
碗.note: 碗 counts bowls of noodles or soup. 兩碗 means two bowls; 大碗 means a large bowl.
碗.memory: The stone component 石 is on the left; 宛, with a roof and curved lower strokes, is on the right.

parts.label: 石
parts.name: left stone component
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal and left-falling stroke, then the three-stroke 口 below.

parts.label: 宛
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the roof 宀, the three strokes below on the left and the two bent strokes on the lower right.

昨.note: 昨 combines with the familiar 天 to make 昨天, yesterday. Keep its rising second tone distinct from 做 zuò.
昨.memory: The narrow 日 stands beside 乍, whose two short inner lines sit below the top cross.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: left sun component
parts.description: Write the narrow four-stroke 日 on the left.

parts.label: 乍
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Start with the short slant and upper horizontal, then the vertical and two shorter horizontals beneath it.

餐.note: 餐 begins 餐廳, restaurant. Read cān with a level first tone; the word names a place to eat.
餐.memory: The seven strokes at the top sit over a broad 食, the food component.

parts.label: 𣦼
parts.name: upper seven-stroke group
parts.description: Write the small upper-left group first, followed by the two crossing strokes of 又 on its right.

parts.label: 食
parts.name: lower food component
parts.description: Begin 食 with its spreading roof, then build the box and finish its descending lower strokes. Keep this nine-stroke component centered below the top group.

廳.meaning: hall; final syllable of 餐廳
廳.note: 廳 completes 餐廳, restaurant. Its tīng sounds like the familiar 聽; the enclosing roof distinguishes this written character.
廳.memory: A wide 广 roof shelters an ear on the left and a heart at the lower right.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: outer roof
parts.description: Write the dot, broad roof line and long left-falling stroke first.

parts.label: 耳
parts.name: inner upper-left ear
parts.description: Inside the roof, write the top horizontal, left vertical and long right vertical before the inner horizontals and lower rising line.

parts.label: 壬
parts.name: inner lower-left group
parts.description: Below the ear, write the short slanting top line, central vertical, middle horizontal and lower rising line.

parts.label: 十罒一心
parts.name: right-hand stack
parts.description: Work downward through the cross, five-stroke flat eye shape and horizontal line, then finish 心 with its left dot, bent hook and two remaining dots.

辣.note: 辣 describes the peppery heat of food. 熱 describes temperature, so food can be 熱 without being 辣.
辣.memory: 辛 has a long descending last stroke on the left; 束 keeps a box around its central line on the right.

parts.label: 辛
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write the dot, horizontal and two small inward strokes, then two horizontals and the long descending left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 束
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the top horizontal and central box, then the long central vertical and the two spreading lower strokes.

怕.meaning: fear; dislike or be sensitive to
怕.note: 怕 means fear or be afraid of. In 怕辣 it describes someone who dislikes or cannot comfortably tolerate spicy food.
怕.memory: The slim heart component 忄 stands beside a compact white 白.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: left heart component
parts.description: Write the left dot and right dot, then the longer vertical between them.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Start with the short top slant, then write the upright box with its inner horizontal and closing base.

example.meaning: dislike or be sensitive to spicy food

所.meaning: first syllable of 所以, so
所.note: Learn 所以 as the complete connector meaning so or therefore. 所 by itself is not the connector in this lesson.
所.memory: A small 戶 sits to the left of 斤, with two long downward strokes keeping the halves apart.

parts.label: 戶
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Start with the slanted top stroke, the bent upper shape and its horizontal, then the long left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 斤
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper slant and longer left-falling stroke, then the horizontal and final vertical.

自.note: 自 begins 自己, oneself. In 我自己做飯, the person doing the cooking is me.
自.memory: A small top slant rests on a tall box with two inner horizontal lines.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: top slant
parts.description: Write the short left-falling stroke above the box.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: lower box
parts.description: Write the left side, top-and-right bend, two inner horizontals and closing bottom horizontal.

己.note: 己 completes 自己. Its third-tone jǐ differs from the familiar 幾 jǐ in writing even though they sound alike.
己.memory: The upper corner bends down to a middle shelf; the last stroke curls underneath without closing the upper opening.

parts.label: 己
parts.name: three-stroke curled structure
parts.description: Write the top horizontal-and-downward bend, then the middle horizontal. Finish with the long curved stroke below, keeping its upper end below the top edge.

甜.note: 甜 gives 甜點 its sweet-food meaning. The familiar 點 has a new role inside this whole word; it is not the ordering verb here.
甜.memory: 舌 fills the left half; the compact 甘 on the right has an extra horizontal inside its open-topped shape.

parts.label: 舌
parts.name: left tongue component
parts.description: Write the top slant, horizontal and vertical, then the three-stroke 口 beneath.

parts.label: 甘
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal, left and right verticals, inner horizontal and bottom horizontal.

錯.meaning: wrong; in 不錯, not bad
錯.note: 錯 can mean wrong. The complete expression 不錯 means not bad or pretty good; do not translate every use as not mistaken.
錯.memory: The metal component 金 is on the left; 昔 puts a wide cross-shaped top above 日 on the right.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: left metal component
parts.description: Write the spreading top, two horizontals and central vertical, then its two small lower marks and final rising base.

parts.label: 昔
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal, two verticals and lower horizontal, then the four-stroke 日 underneath.

教.note: For the verb teach in 教我, use first-tone jiāo. The character also has a jiào reading in other words; those uses are outside this lesson.
教.memory: 孝 fills the left side, with a small 子 beneath its crossed top; 攵 sends two long strokes across the right.

parts.label: 孝
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write the horizontal, vertical, second horizontal and descending slant, then the three strokes of 子 below.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: right action component
parts.description: Write the short slant and horizontal, followed by the longer left-falling and right-falling strokes.

籠.meaning: steamer basket; lóng in 小籠包
籠.note: In 小籠包, 籠 refers to the small steaming basket. Read this syllable lóng, with a rising tone.
籠.memory: Think of bamboo above a detailed lower block: a bamboo steamer for the buns. This is a memory aid.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The six-stroke bamboo top is written as two small three-stroke groups.

parts.label: 龍
parts.name: dragon-shaped lower block
parts.description: The sixteen-stroke 龍 block fills the lower area. Keep its left upright block separate from the long shape on the right.

臭.note: Read 臭 as chòu in 臭豆腐. The name refers to the strong smell of fermented tofu.
臭.memory: The familiar 自 sits above 犬. Remember the small dot of 犬: the bottom is not just 大.

parts.label: 自
parts.name: self-shaped top
parts.description: The upper 自 has a short slant, an outer frame and two inner horizontal lines.

parts.label: 犬
parts.name: dog-shaped bottom
parts.description: The lower 犬 has four strokes, including the small dot beside the spreading strokes.

豆.note: 豆 is the bean character in the tofu name 臭豆腐. Its seven strokes make a compact, balanced shape.
豆.memory: Picture a covered vessel standing on two short supports and a wide base.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top line
parts.description: Start with one horizontal line, separate from the box below.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: central box
parts.description: The middle box takes three strokes; close its bottom before adding the base.

parts.label: 䒑
parts.name: lower support
parts.description: Two short strokes open above a final broad horizontal baseline.

腐.note: 腐 is the last character of 臭豆腐. Learn the complete food name; translating each character literally does not give its usual food meaning.
腐.memory: A shelter surrounds a compact person-and-hand block, with the meat-shaped block at the bottom.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: shelter
parts.description: A dot and roof line lead into a long left-falling stroke around the upper part.

parts.label: 付
parts.name: upper inner block
parts.description: Inside the shelter, the two-stroke person shape stands beside the three-stroke 寸 shape.

parts.label: 肉
parts.name: meat-shaped lower block
parts.description: Write the outer frame then the two small person-like forms inside, six strokes altogether.

知.meaning: know; first syllable of 知道
知.note: 知 begins 知道, to know a fact or know of something. It is not the learned-skill word 會.
知.memory: The five-stroke arrow shape stands next to a small mouth-shaped box.

parts.label: 矢
parts.name: arrow-shaped left
parts.description: The five strokes on the left include two horizontals and two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth-shaped right
parts.description: The right-hand box is three strokes, with its bottom closed last.

道.meaning: dào in 知道; way or path
道.note: 道 is the second character of 知道. It has 13 strokes in this Taiwan handwriting form.
道.memory: Write the upright head-shaped block first, then let the walking component carry it from the left and below.

parts.label: 首
parts.name: head-shaped inner block
parts.description: The inner 首 has two short top strokes above a horizontal and a framed lower section.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: The Taiwan form here uses four strokes on the left and along the bottom. Follow the guide instead of merging the small strokes.

定.note: 定 forms the second syllable of 一定, definitely. In 一定要, the whole expression makes a firm recommendation.
定.memory: A three-stroke roof sits over a steady lower support.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: Write the dot, left roof stroke and hooked roof stroke first.

parts.label: 𤴓
parts.name: lower support
parts.description: Five strokes form the lower block: its central upright connects to two spreading lower strokes.

校.note: 學校 (xuéxiào) means school. 學 was already taught; 校 is the new second character.
校.memory: A wood-shaped block on the left stands beside crossed lower strokes on the right.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood-shaped left
parts.description: The left 木 has four strokes; its final stroke is shortened to fit the right-hand block.

parts.label: 交
parts.name: right-hand block
parts.description: The six strokes of 交 begin with a dot and horizontal, then spread into crossed lower strokes.

現.note: 現在 (xiànzài) means now. The familiar 在 is the second character; 現 is new.
現.memory: A narrow king-shaped block stands beside an eye with two legs.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: jade-side shape
parts.description: This four-stroke side form is written like a narrow 王; the lower stroke rises slightly.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: see-shaped right
parts.description: 見 has an eye-shaped upper frame and two spreading strokes below it, seven strokes total.

山.note: 山 names a mountain. In 山上 it combines with the familiar 上 to make a location: on a mountain or in the mountains.
山.memory: Think of three peaks joined along the base. Start with the middle peak.

parts.label: 丨
parts.name: middle upright
parts.description: The first stroke is the tall central upright.

parts.label: 凵
parts.name: outer sides and base
parts.description: The second stroke bends from the left side along the base; the third forms the right side.

海.note: 海 means sea or ocean. Its water-side component helps distinguish it from other new scenery characters.
海.memory: Three water marks sit to the left of a compact, divided block.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water side
parts.description: The three water strokes descend along the left, with the last one rising.

parts.label: 每
parts.name: right-hand block
parts.description: The seven-stroke 每 begins with a short slant and horizontal above the divided lower enclosure.

風.meaning: wind; first syllable of 風景
風.note: 風 is the first syllable of 風景, scenery. Use the full word 風景 for scenery, rather than 風 by itself.
風.memory: A tall curved frame shelters a compact insect-like shape.

parts.label: 𠘨
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The first two strokes form the left side and the broad hooked outer frame.

parts.label: 䖝
parts.name: inner strokes
parts.description: A short top slant and the insect-shaped lower section fill the frame; the final small dot stays inside.

景.note: 景 completes 風景. The top 日 is separate from the larger 京-shaped block below.
景.memory: Picture a small sun above a tall lower block with a box and three spreading strokes.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun-shaped top
parts.description: Four strokes make the upper box with its interior horizontal line.

parts.label: 京
parts.name: lower block
parts.description: The eight-stroke 京 begins with a dot and horizontal, then a box, then the three strokes of 小.

美.note: 美 describes beauty, especially in scenery here. Say 風景很美, the scenery is beautiful.
美.memory: A six-stroke upper group balances on the three spreading strokes of 大.

parts.label: 𦍌
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper six strokes include the two short top strokes, three horizontals and a central upright.

parts.label: 大
parts.name: large-shaped bottom
parts.description: Three lower strokes form 大; keep the final two strokes wide and balanced.

地.note: 地 is dì in 地方, place. Learn the sound in this word; 地 can have a different grammatical reading in later material.
地.memory: The earth-shaped left stands beside the familiar shape 也.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth side
parts.description: Three strokes form a narrow 土 on the left; its final line rises slightly.

parts.label: 也
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: The three-stroke 也 stretches to the right with its final bent hook.

方.note: 方 is fāng in 地方. Read 地方 as dìfāng here, with first tone on 方.
方.memory: Keep the top dot separate, then place a bending stroke and a long slant below the horizontal.

parts.label: 丶
parts.name: top dot
parts.description: The first stroke is a small dot above the main horizontal.

parts.label: 万
parts.name: lower outline
parts.description: The next strokes are the horizontal, the turning hooked stroke, and the final left-falling stroke.

面.meaning: side; miàn in 裡面 and 外面
面.note: 面 appears in 裡面 and 外面. It sounds like 麵, noodles, but is a different character; do not add the wheat-side strokes of 麵.
面.memory: A top line and short slant lead down into a framed, divided face.

parts.label: 丆
parts.name: top strokes
parts.description: Begin with the horizontal and the short left-falling stroke beneath it.

parts.label: 囬
parts.name: framed lower block
parts.description: The lower seven strokes form the outer frame and its internal divisions. Close the outer bottom last.

圖.note: 圖 starts 圖書館, library. In this Traditional form the outer frame encloses a detailed inner block.
圖.memory: Build the large frame around the small inner forms; save its bottom line for last.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: Begin the frame with two strokes, write the eleven inner strokes, then close the bottom with the last stroke.

parts.label: 啚
parts.name: inner block
parts.description: Eleven inner strokes make a small top box and a larger divided structure beneath it.

館.note: 館 completes 圖書館. 書 in the middle is already familiar, so 圖 and 館 are the new writing targets.
館.memory: A food-shaped side stands next to a roof sheltering stacked shapes.

parts.label: 飠
parts.name: food side
parts.description: Eight strokes form the narrow Traditional food component on the left.

parts.label: 官
parts.name: right-hand block
parts.description: The eight-stroke 官 starts with a roof and ends with a vertically arranged inner block.

課.note: 課 is the class character in 上課, to attend class. It is different from 書, a book.
課.memory: Speech on the left sits beside a fruit-shaped block with a tree-like base.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech side
parts.description: The seven-stroke 言 begins with a dot and horizontal lines, with a small mouth box below.

parts.label: 果
parts.name: fruit-shaped right
parts.description: The eight-stroke 果 has a divided upper box and a long central stroke that continues into the spreading lower strokes.

到.note: 到 dào marks the destination in 到學校去: go to school. It does not by itself mark a completed arrival.
到.memory: Remember 到 as 至 + 刂: a broad left block beside two slim upright strokes.

parts.label: 至
parts.name: left part
parts.description: 至 forms the left block; notice the 土 shape at its bottom.

parts.label: 刂
parts.name: knife component
parts.description: 刂 forms the right edge: a short vertical followed by a longer vertical hook.

朋.note: 朋 is the first character of 朋友. Learn the complete word for a friend.
朋.memory: Two 月-shaped blocks stand side by side: a pair to remember 朋.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: left moon-shaped block
parts.description: The left 月-shaped block is narrow, with two short interior bars.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: right moon-shaped block
parts.description: A second 月-shaped block stands on the right; keep both bases aligned.

友.note: 友 is the second character of 朋友, with third-tone yǒu.
友.memory: A slanting upper arm crosses above 又: remember the meeting strokes in 友.

parts.label: 𠂇
parts.name: upper crossing strokes
parts.description: A horizontal and a long left-falling stroke form the upper frame.

parts.label: 又
parts.name: lower hand-shaped part
parts.description: 又 sits below the frame; its crossing diagonals spread toward the lower corners.

找.note: 找 can mean look for something or go see a person, as in 找朋友. Do not confuse it with 我.
找.memory: A narrow hand 扌 stands beside 戈: reach out to look for someone.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: 扌 has a horizontal, vertical hook and rising stroke on the left.

parts.label: 戈
parts.name: right crossing component
parts.description: 戈 has a long slanting hook, a crossing left-fall and a small upper dot.

遠.note: 遠 is the opposite of 近. Both describe distance; they do not need 是 before them.
遠.memory: 袁 inside 辶: look for 土 above 口 in the inner block, then the long wrapping base.

parts.label: 袁
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: 袁 begins with 土 over 口 and ends with spreading lower strokes. Keep the inner block above the base.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: This is the wrapping movement component also seen in 近. Its final stroke extends below 袁.

近.note: 近 jìn means near or close. Use 很近 for a distance description. Follow the eight-stroke Taiwan form shown here.
近.memory: 斤 sits above the wrapping movement component 辶, whose final stroke sweeps along the bottom.

parts.label: 斤
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: 斤 has a short top slant, a longer left slant, a horizontal stroke, and a vertical.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The movement component wraps around the left and bottom of 斤. Its long final stroke supports the whole character.

附.meaning: attach; first character of 附近
附.note: Learn 附 together with 近 as 附近, meaning nearby or the surrounding area.
附.memory: 阝 + 付: a narrow folded left side beside 亻 and 寸 on the right.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: left mound component
parts.description: The left 阝 has a folded upper stroke, a rounded lower turn, and a long vertical.

parts.label: 付
parts.name: right component
parts.description: 付 contains 亻 beside 寸. Look for the long hook and separate dot in 寸.

東.meaning: east; first character of 東西
東.note: 東 means east on its own. In 東西 dōngxi, learn the whole word meaning things.
東.memory: A central box crossed by a long vertical and spreading lower strokes anchors 東.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top bar
parts.description: The top horizontal stretches above the central box.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: central box
parts.description: Four strokes make the box and its middle bar; a later vertical crosses through it.

parts.label: 木形
parts.name: crossing and spreading strokes
parts.description: The long vertical passes through the box; the final two strokes spread left and right.

西.meaning: west; second character of 東西
西.note: 西 is xī on its own, but light xi in 東西 dōngxi, things.
西.memory: A wide top bar and an outer box contain two bent inner legs in 西.

parts.label: 外框
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The top bar, left edge, folded top-right edge and final bottom stroke surround the inner strokes.

parts.label: 內部
parts.name: inner legs
parts.description: A left-falling stroke and a bent right leg fill the box without crossing.

商.note: 商 refers to commerce. Learn it in 商店 shāngdiàn, shop or store.
商.memory: A dot and bar above two short strokes; below them, a tall outer frame holds a small 口.

parts.label: 亠丷
parts.name: top group
parts.description: A dot sits above a long horizontal line, followed by two short inward strokes.

parts.label: 冏
parts.name: lower frame
parts.description: The outer frame has an open bottom. Inside it, two short strokes sit above the small 口 box.

宿.meaning: lodging; first character of 宿舍
宿.note: In 宿舍, 宿 is sù. It refers to lodging here; other readings belong to other words.
宿.memory: A roof 宀 covers a small person 亻 beside 百: picture lodging under the roof.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The roof has a top dot, a left dot and a horizontal hook sheltering everything below.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person at the left
parts.description: The narrow person component stands under the left side of the roof.

parts.label: 百
parts.name: lower right block
parts.description: 百 has a horizontal cap above 白; the rectangular lower section contains a middle bar.

舍.meaning: dwelling; second character of 宿舍
舍.note: 舍 is fourth-tone shè in 宿舍. Keep it distinct from other readings and from the separate character 捨.
舍.memory: Two spreading roof-like strokes sit above 干 and 口 in 舍.

parts.label: 𠆢
parts.name: top cover
parts.description: The two top strokes spread left and right over the middle bar.

parts.label: 干
parts.name: middle cross
parts.description: Two horizontal strokes crossed by a vertical form the middle group.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: bottom box
parts.description: The three-stroke 口 closes the base directly under the middle vertical.

樓.note: 樓 names a floor in 二樓. 大樓 names a multi-storey building; the two uses share this character.
樓.memory: A narrow tree 木 stands beside the dense 婁 block, whose bottom resembles 女.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood component
parts.description: The left 木 narrows its right-falling stroke to make room for 婁.

parts.label: 婁
parts.name: right sound component
parts.description: The upper bars and boxes stack above a 女-shaped base; keep the central vertical aligned.

下.note: 下 means below or down in 樓下. Here it identifies a lower floor relative to the understood place.
下.memory: A long horizontal roof, a vertical descending beneath it, and a short stroke to the right.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top bar
parts.description: Write the long top horizontal first; the other two strokes hang beneath it.

parts.label: 卜
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: A vertical drops from the top bar. Add the short rightward stroke beside it.

棟.note: 棟 counts whole buildings: 一棟大樓. Its right side is 東, already taught in 東西.
棟.memory: 木 beside 東: a familiar tree at left and the crossed box of 東 at right.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood component
parts.description: Four strokes form a narrow 木 at the left; its final stroke is shortened.

parts.label: 東
parts.name: right sound component
parts.description: The eight-stroke 東 contains a central box crossed by a vertical, with two spreading strokes below.

前.note: 前 means front. In 前面, it names the front or the area in front of a reference point.
前.memory: Remember 前 by the two short strokes and bar at the top, above a box-like left side and a slim right hook.

parts.label: 䒑
parts.name: top group
parts.description: The top group has two short strokes above a long horizontal bar.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: Below the bar, a 月-shaped group sits on the left and two upright strokes sit on the right.

後.note: 後 is the Traditional character in 後面. This unit uses its spatial meaning, behind.
後.memory: A narrow 彳 stands beside 幺 over three spreading lower strokes in 後.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: left step component
parts.description: Two short left-falling strokes precede the long left-side vertical.

parts.label: 幺
parts.name: upper right component
parts.description: Two bent strokes and a small dot form 幺 above the lower crossing strokes.

parts.label: 夊
parts.name: lower right component
parts.description: The three lower strokes cross and spread at the bottom right.

旁.meaning: side; first character of 旁邊
旁.note: 旁 is second-tone páng in 旁邊, beside. The lower 方 is already familiar.
旁.memory: A broad upper cover shelters 方 at the bottom of 旁.

parts.label: 六
parts.name: top group
parts.description: A dot and horizontal bar sit over two short spreading strokes.

parts.label: 冖
parts.name: middle cover
parts.description: Two strokes make a shallow cover between the top group and 方.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the familiar four-stroke 方 below the cover.

邊.note: 邊 forms the second syllable of 旁邊. This Taiwan guide uses 19 strokes.
邊.memory: A tall 臱 block stands above the wrapping 辶, with 自 at its top and 方 near its base.

parts.label: 臱
parts.name: inner block
parts.description: Start with 自, then the middle roof and short spreading strokes, and finish with 方 below.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: Four strokes wrap the left and bottom; the final sweep supports the tall inner block.

室.note: 室 is shì in 教室, classroom. The upper roof suggests an indoor space.
室.memory: A roof 宀 shelters 至, the same block seen at the left of 到.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The three roof strokes cover the lower block without touching its central vertical.

parts.label: 至
parts.name: lower block
parts.description: 至 has a horizontal cap, a bent stroke and dot, then a 土-shaped base.

池.note: 池 names a pool in 游泳池. The familiar swimming activity gains a place word.
池.memory: Water 氵 flows down the left of the wide 也 on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: Two dots and a rising stroke make the left-side water component.

parts.label: 也
parts.name: right component
parts.description: 也 begins with its wide hooked turn, followed by a central vertical and the low turning hook.

迎.note: 迎 is second-tone yíng in 歡迎. 歡 is already familiar from 喜歡.
迎.memory: The compact 卬 block sits above the wrapping movement component in 迎.

parts.label: 卬
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: A slanted top and upright turn face a narrow hooked right section.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: Four strokes wrap left and below 卬; finish with the long supporting sweep.

唱.note: 唱 is the action verb in 唱歌, “to sing.” It is fourth-tone chàng.
唱.memory: A small 口 on the left faces a stacked 昌 on the right: picture a mouth producing song.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The three-stroke 口 sits tightly on the left and cues an action done with the mouth.

parts.label: 昌
parts.name: right sound block
parts.description: The right side is two 日-like boxes stacked vertically; keep both compact and aligned.

歌.note: 歌 is first-tone gē. In 唱歌, it names song while 唱 supplies the action.
歌.memory: The repeated square-and-hook shapes of 哥 stand beside 欠, whose final strokes open outward like a singer taking a breath.

parts.label: 哥
parts.name: left block
parts.description: The first ten strokes build the dense 哥 block on the left, with two 口-like sections and hooks.

parts.label: 欠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 欠 on the right, ending with the long right-falling stroke.

見.note: 見 is fourth-tone jiàn. In 見面 it contributes the idea of seeing or meeting someone.
見.memory: A five-stroke 目 eye stands above two 儿-like legs: an eye that goes out to see.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 目, a tall eye-shaped box with two inner horizontals.

parts.label: 儿
parts.name: lower legs
parts.description: The final two strokes spread below the eye; the last one bends and extends to the right.

分.note: 分 is first-tone fēn when it counts minutes in clock time, as in 二十分.
分.memory: 八 opens at the top over 刀 below; the four strokes divide the character into two clear parts.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: top split
parts.description: Two short spreading strokes form 八 at the top.

parts.label: 刀
parts.name: lower knife
parts.description: The last two strokes form 刀 underneath, with the second stroke sweeping down-left.

午.note: 午 is third-tone wǔ. In 中午 it refers to noon or midday.
午.memory: A short slant leads into two horizontals crossed by one vertical; keep the lower horizontal longer.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: top slant
parts.description: Begin with the short left-falling stroke at the upper left.

parts.label: 干
parts.name: two bars and a vertical
parts.description: The remaining three strokes form 干: two horizontal strokes followed by the vertical through them. This group has three strokes; it is not the two-stroke 十.

時.note: 時 is second-tone shí. It appears in 時候, a common way to talk about when something happens.
時.memory: 日 on the left is the sun/time cue; 寺 fills the right side with 土 above 寸.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The first four strokes make the narrow 日 on the left.

parts.label: 寺
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last six strokes form 寺 on the right, with a compact upper cross and 寸-like base.

候.note: 候 is fourth-tone hòu in 時候. The word 時候 is used in questions such as 什麼時候 “when.”
候.memory: A slim 亻 person stands at the left of a taller right block; keep the right side narrow enough to balance the person.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow person radical on the left.

parts.label: right block
parts.name: vertical and lower right block
parts.description: After 亻, the remaining eight strokes include a separate short vertical alongside the compact lower shape. This whole right group is not the complete character 侯.

從.note: 從 introduces the starting point of movement.
從.memory: Remember 從 by 彳 on the left and two person-like shapes above the spreading lower strokes on the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: step component
parts.description: 彳 is the narrow three-stroke component along the left edge.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right group
parts.description: The right group has two person-like shapes at the top and a long stroke extending toward the lower right.

空.note: 空 is fourth-tone kòng in 有空 (yǒu kòng), meaning to have time available. The audio uses 有空 to make this reading clear; 空 has other readings in other words.
空.memory: 穴 opens like a roofed space above 工: picture an empty space under a roof.

parts.label: 穴
parts.name: cave/space component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 穴, a roof with two small strokes opening underneath.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 工, centered under the upper space.

次.note: 次 is fourth-tone cì. In 下次 it means the next time or next occasion.
次.memory: Two small strokes on the left sit beside 欠 on the right; the final stroke of 欠 opens far to the right.

parts.label: 冫
parts.name: two-dot left side
parts.description: The first two strokes are a dot and rising stroke on the left.

parts.label: 欠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 欠, finishing with the long right-falling stroke.

題.note: 題 is second-tone tí. In 問題 it means a question or problem; 沒問題 means “no problem.”
題.memory: 是 fills the left side while the traditional 頁 head/page component forms the right side.

parts.label: 是
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first nine strokes form 是, beginning with 日 and ending in the sweeping lower strokes.

parts.label: 頁
parts.name: head/page component
parts.description: The last nine strokes form traditional 頁 on the right, with a boxed middle and two closing lower strokes.

對.note: 對 is fourth-tone duì. In 對了, it is a conversational cue meaning “by the way” or “oh, right.”
對.memory: A dense vertical left block balances 寸 on the lower right; keep the final dot of 寸 distinct.

parts.label: left block
parts.name: upper cluster and lower 土
parts.description: The first eleven strokes form the left block, including its upper cluster and lower 土-shaped base. The label describes the entire highlighted group, not just its upper portion.

parts.label: 寸
parts.name: right-lower component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 寸: a horizontal-hook structure followed by the small dot.

剛.note: 剛 is first-tone gāng. As an adverb it places an action just before the present moment.
剛.memory: 岡 forms the broad left block and 刂 stands as two knife strokes on the right.

parts.label: 岡
parts.name: left block
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 岡, with an enclosing outer shape around the inner mountain-like strokes.

parts.label: 刂
parts.name: knife component
parts.description: The last two strokes are the narrow vertical knife component on the right.

半.note: 半 is fourth-tone bàn. In clock time, 四點半 means 4:30, literally four o’clock plus half an hour.
半.memory: Two small upper strokes sit above a crossed lower frame; the final vertical runs down through the center.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: two upper strokes
parts.description: Begin with the two short strokes that open above the center.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: crossed lower group
parts.description: The last three strokes make the horizontal framework and central vertical that complete 半.

比.meaning: compare; first character of 比賽
比.note: 比 is third-tone bǐ. In 比賽 it is part of the noun/verb meaning game or competition.
比.memory: Two compact two-stroke shapes sit side by side, like two sides being compared.

parts.label: left
parts.name: left two strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form the tighter left half.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right two strokes
parts.description: The final two strokes form the right half, ending in the hooked sweep.

賽.note: 賽 is fourth-tone sài. Together with 比 it forms 比賽, “game; competition.”
賽.memory: A roof 宀 covers a dense middle, while traditional 貝 forms the seven-stroke base.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof across the top of 賽.

parts.label: middle
parts.name: middle crossing group
parts.description: The next seven strokes build the compact crossed middle between the roof and 貝.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: shell component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form traditional 貝 at the bottom, including the two closing lower strokes.

結.meaning: tie; join; first character of 結束
結.note: 結 is second-tone jié in 結束, “to end; finish.” Keep the traditional silk radical 糹 on the left.
結.memory: The silk radical 糹 stands beside 吉, linking the idea of tying something together.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: silk component
parts.description: The first six strokes form the traditional silk radical on the left.

parts.label: 吉
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The last six strokes form 吉 on the right, with 士 above 口.

束.meaning: bundle; second character of 結束
束.note: 束 is fourth-tone shù in 結束. This unit learns it inside the common word 結束.
束.memory: A central vertical passes through the boxed middle and opens into two lower strokes, making the whole form look tightly bundled.

parts.label: 束
parts.name: whole bundled form
parts.description: Write the seven-stroke form as one connected design: top horizontal, boxed middle, central vertical, then the two spreading lower strokes.

開.note: 開 is first-tone kāi. In 開始, it helps form the verb “to begin; start.”
開.memory: Traditional 門 forms the outer gate, with the four-stroke inner shape centered inside it.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: gate component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the traditional 門 frame around the character.

parts.label: 开
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The final four strokes sit inside the gate as the open inner structure.

始.note: 始 is third-tone shǐ. It appears in 開始, the process verb “to begin; start.”
始.memory: 女 on the left stands beside 台 on the right; keep the lower 口 of 台 compact.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the narrow 女 on the left.

parts.label: 台
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The last five strokes form 台 on the right, ending with the three-stroke 口.

寫.note: 寫 is third-tone xiě and is the Traditional form used in Taiwan. It means to write.
寫.memory: A roof 宀 sits above the dense 舄-shaped lower block; the four dots anchor the bottom.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof across the top.

parts.label: 舄
parts.name: lower block
parts.description: The remaining twelve strokes make the dense lower block, ending with the four bottom dots.

忙.note: 忙 is second-tone máng. It is a state verb meaning busy.
忙.memory: The heart radical 忄 stands on the left of 亡; picture a heart pulled in many directions.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the narrow heart radical on the left.

parts.label: 亡
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 亡 on the right, with the dot over its horizontal frame.

每.note: 每 is third-tone měi. It introduces each/every and is normally paired with 都 in the sentence pattern taught here.
每.memory: Two short upper strokes sit over a 母-like lower box; keep the central crossing lines clear.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form the short top of 每.

parts.label: 母
parts.name: lower mother-like form
parts.description: The last five strokes form the boxed, crossed lower shape related visually to 母.

法.meaning: method; law; second character of 書法
法.note: 法 is third-tone fǎ. In 書法 it refers to the art/method of writing: calligraphy.
法.memory: Three water dots 氵 sit beside 去; keep the left dots light and the right side compact.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes are the water radical along the left edge.

parts.label: 去
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 去 on the right, with 土 above the bent lower strokes.

字.note: 字 is fourth-tone zì. Here it means a written Chinese character, as in 寫字.
字.memory: A three-stroke roof 宀 sits over the three-stroke 子. Keep the child component centered under the roof.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof across the top of 字.

parts.label: 子
parts.name: child component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 子 beneath the roof, ending with the long horizontal.

等.note: 等 is third-tone děng. In 等一下 it means to wait a moment or do something a little later.
等.memory: The six-stroke bamboo top 𥫗 sits over 寺. Think of waiting under the paired bamboo marks.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The first six strokes form the paired bamboo component across the top.

parts.label: 寺
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 寺 underneath the bamboo top.

事.note: 事 is fourth-tone shì. 有事 literally means to have a matter to deal with, so it often means being occupied.
事.memory: The middle box and hand-like strokes are crossed by a final vertical hook. Keep the whole eight-stroke form compact.

parts.label: main
parts.name: upper and middle frame
parts.description: The first seven strokes build the top line, central 口-like box, and hand-shaped middle.

parts.label: 亅
parts.name: final hook
parts.description: The eighth stroke is the long central vertical hook that locks the form together.

example.meaning: have something to do; be occupied

意.note: 意 is fourth-tone yì. In 有意思, it combines with 思 to describe something as interesting or engaging.
意.memory: 音 fills the upper nine strokes and 心 forms the four-stroke base. Keep the heart component broad enough to support the top.

parts.label: 音
parts.name: sound component
parts.description: The first nine strokes form 音 at the top of 意.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 心 across the bottom.

思.note: 思 is normally read sī on its own; in 意思 the second syllable is commonly neutral: yìsi.
思.memory: 田 forms the five-stroke top and 心 forms the four-stroke bottom. Keep the heart slightly wider than the box above.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: field component
parts.description: The first five strokes form the square 田 at the top.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 心 under 田.

坐.note: 坐 is fourth-tone zuò. Before a vehicle, it means to take or travel by that vehicle.
坐.memory: Two 人-like figures sit above 土. Keep the final three 土 strokes centered under the four upper strokes.

parts.label: 从
parts.name: two-person upper group
