parts.description: The first four strokes form the paired person-like upper group.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 土 underneath.

火.note: 火 is third-tone huǒ. In 火車 it is the first character of the word for train.
火.memory: Two small side strokes frame the central 人-like pair, making a four-stroke flame shape.

parts.label: side
parts.name: side strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes are the shorter side strokes of the flame.

parts.label: 人
parts.name: central pair
parts.description: The final two strokes spread downward through the center like 人.

車.note: 車 is first-tone chē. It appears in 火車 'train' and 車票 'ticket'.
車.memory: A central vertical passes through a boxed middle and three horizontal levels. Keep the seven strokes balanced around the center.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: whole vehicle form
parts.description: Write the seven-stroke traditional 車 as a single centered framework with the long vertical crossing its horizontal levels.

跟.note: 跟 is first-tone gēn. In this lesson it introduces the person who accompanies someone in an activity.
跟.memory: The seven-stroke 足 component stands on the left; 艮 fills the six-stroke right side.

parts.label: 𧾷
parts.name: foot component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form the compressed foot component on the left.

parts.label: 艮
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 艮 on the right.

慢.note: 慢 is fourth-tone màn. It describes something as slow, including a mode of transportation.
慢.memory: The three-stroke 忄 heart side stays narrow; the eleven-stroke 曼 block fills the right.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart side
parts.description: The first three strokes form 忄 on the left.

parts.label: 曼
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The final eleven strokes form the larger 曼 component on the right.

較.note: 較 is fourth-tone jiào. Together with 比 it forms 比較, the adverb used for an implicit comparison.
較.memory: Traditional 車 takes the first seven strokes; 交 supplies the six-stroke right side.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: vehicle component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 車 on the left.

parts.label: 交
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 交 on the right.

快.note: 快 is fourth-tone kuài. It contrasts with 慢 when comparing transportation.
快.memory: Three-stroke 忄 on the left is followed by four-stroke 夬 on the right.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart side
parts.description: The first three strokes form the narrow 忄 component.

parts.label: 夬
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 夬 on the right, ending in the spreading lower stroke.

高.note: 高 is first-tone gāo. In 高鐵 it is part of Taiwan's common abbreviation for High Speed Rail.
高.memory: A two-stroke 亠 sits above a small 口, then the five-stroke lower enclosure completes 高.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top
parts.description: The first two strokes form the cap at the top.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: middle mouth
parts.description: The next three strokes form the small central 口.

parts.label: 冋
parts.name: lower frame
parts.description: The final five strokes form the broad lower enclosure.

鐵.note: 鐵 is third-tone tiě. In 高鐵 it refers to the rail part of High Speed Rail.
鐵.memory: 金 uses the first eight strokes on the left; the dense thirteen-stroke 𢧜 fills the right.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: metal component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the metal radical 金 on the left.

parts.label: 𢧜
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The final thirteen strokes form the compact right-side component.

票.note: 票 is fourth-tone piào. 車票 means a ticket for transportation.
票.memory: Six-stroke 覀 forms the top; five-stroke 示 forms the lower half.

parts.label: 覀
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 覀 across the top.

parts.label: 示
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 示 below.

又.note: 又 is fourth-tone yòu. Repeated as 又…又…, it links two properties: both A and B.
又.memory: 又 is only two crossing strokes: a bent first stroke followed by a long falling-right stroke.

parts.label: 又
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: The two strokes cross to form the complete character; keep the second stroke long and open.

舒.note: 舒 is first-tone shū. It is the first character of 舒服, 'comfortable'.
舒.memory: 舍 fills the first eight strokes on the left and 予 uses the final four strokes on the right.

parts.label: 舍
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 舍 on the left.

parts.label: 予
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 予 on the right.

服.note: 服 is read with a neutral tone in the common word 舒服: shūfu. The character's citation reading is fú.
服.memory: 月 forms the four-stroke left side; the final four strokes form 𠬝 on the right.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 月 on the left.

parts.label: 𠬝
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form the right-hand component.

同.note: 同 means same or together; 同學 is someone who studies alongside you, a classmate.
同.memory: The outer frame surrounds 一 and 口; keep the box balanced around the center.

parts.label: 冂
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The first two strokes make the tall outer frame, open at the bottom.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: inner horizontal
parts.description: The third stroke is the short horizontal inside the frame.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: inner mouth
parts.description: The last three strokes make a compact 口 below the inner bar.

參.note: Use the first-tone reading cān in 參觀. Learn this word-specific reading rather than guessing from other words containing 參.
參.memory: Three 厶-like marks sit above the 人/彡 lower structure; keep the lower strokes open and descending.

parts.label: 厽
parts.name: three upper loops
parts.description: The first six strokes form three 厶-like loops in a triangle. Each loop uses two strokes.

parts.label: 人
parts.name: spreading middle
parts.description: The next two strokes spread outward below the three loops.

parts.label: 彡
parts.name: three lower slants
parts.description: The final three strokes descend diagonally underneath the spreading middle.

觀.note: 觀 is first-tone guān in 參觀. The 見 component on the right provides a useful visual connection to seeing.
觀.memory: The dense left side balances 見 on the right; leave enough width for the final 見 component.

parts.label: 雚
parts.name: dense left component
parts.description: The first eighteen paths form the dense left component in this licensed Taiwan glyph: the top cluster, two small boxes, and the lower bird-shaped block.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: seeing component
parts.description: The last seven strokes make 見: a tall 目 shape above two spreading lower strokes.

騎.note: 騎 means to ride astride, as on a scooter or bicycle. Here learn 騎機車; 坐 names taking transport such as a bus.
騎.memory: 馬 fills the left side and 奇 fills the right; keep both halves narrow enough to fit together.

parts.label: 馬
parts.name: horse component
parts.description: The first ten strokes form 馬 on the left, including its four lower dots.

parts.label: 奇
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last eight strokes form 奇, with 大 above the lower 可-shaped structure.

載.note: 載 is fourth-tone zài when it means carrying someone in a vehicle or giving them a ride. 載我 means give me a ride.
載.memory: The 車 element sits inside the larger 戈-like structure; keep the central 車 readable before the sweeping final strokes.

parts.label: outer
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The upper cross and long horizontal are written first; the curved 戈 strokes finish after the inner 車. These six highlighted strokes form one visual frame, but are not consecutive in writing order.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: inner vehicle component
parts.description: The seven middle strokes form 車 inside the surrounding frame. Follow the animation for the interleaved whole-character stroke order.

捷.meaning: quick; first character of 捷運
捷.note: 捷 is second-tone jié. Learn it with 運 in 捷運, the Taiwan term for the MRT.
捷.memory: 扌 is the narrow left component; the right side carries most of the character’s width.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: The first three strokes make the narrow 扌 on the left.

parts.label: 疌
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last eight strokes form the wider right block, with a central vertical and spreading lower strokes.

公.note: 公 is first-tone gōng. In 公車, it forms the common Taiwan word for a bus.
公.memory: The two upper strokes spread like 八 above 厶; center the lower turn beneath them.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: upper spreading strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes open to the left and right above the lower loop.

parts.label: 厶
parts.name: lower loop
parts.description: The final bent stroke and dot make 厶 beneath the spreading top.

計.meaning: calculate; first character of 計程車
計.note: 計 is fourth-tone jì. 計程車 is the Taiwan word for taxi; keep the three syllables jì-chéng-chē distinct.
計.memory: 言 forms the left side and 十 the right; keep the left speech component compact and even.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form the narrow 言 on the left, ending in its small 口.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: right cross
parts.description: The last two strokes form 十 on the right: horizontal, then vertical.

程.note: 程 is second-tone chéng in 計程車. Its left component is 禾, not the speech component 言 in 計.
程.memory: 禾 is on the left and 呈 on the right; align the lower strokes so the character does not lean.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 on the left, ending with its two lower side strokes.

parts.label: 呈
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last seven strokes form 呈, with 口 above the lower horizontal framework.

差.note: 差 is fourth-tone chà in 差不多. This expression says the difference is small, so the two things are about the same.
差.memory: The upper 羊-like strokes lead into 工 below; keep the lower 工 centered under the slanting middle stroke.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper sloping group
parts.description: The first six paths form the upper group: two short strokes, three horizontal levels, and the long left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: lower work component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 工 beneath the upper group.

古.note: 古 is gǔ in 古代, meaning ancient times or something ancient.
古.memory: 十 sits above 口. Keep the top cross centered over the box.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: top cross
parts.description: The first two strokes form 十 above the lower box.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower box
parts.description: The last three strokes form 口 beneath the cross.

代.note: 代 is fourth-tone dài. In 古代 it completes the word for ancient times.
代.memory: 亻 is narrow on the left; 弋 opens to the right with a final dot.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 弋
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 弋 on the right.

行.note: Read 行 as xíng in 不行 bùxíng, meaning that a proposal will not work. 行 is polyphonic; another reading is háng in words such as 銀行.
行.memory: 彳 gives three stepping strokes on the left; 亍 supplies the two horizontals and vertical hook on the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: left step component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 彳 on the left.

parts.label: 亍
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 亍 on the right.

星.meaning: star; first character of 星期
星.note: 星 is first-tone xīng. Learn it here as the first character of 星期, week.
星.memory: 日 sits above 生. Keep the lower 生 centered and slightly wider.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 日 at the top.

parts.label: 生
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The last five strokes form 生 below.

期.note: 期 is second-tone qí in 星期. It refers to a period or scheduled span of time.
期.memory: 其 fills the left side and 月 the right; keep 月 tall and narrow.

parts.label: 其
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 其 on the left.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 月 on the right.

放.meaning: release; put; first character of 放假
放.note: 放 is fourth-tone fàng. In 放假 it means to be released from normal work or class for a break.
放.memory: 方 is on the left; 攵 on the right ends with the long falling stroke.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 方 on the left.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: action component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 攵 on the right.

假.note: Read 假 as jià in 放假, where it means a holiday or leave from work or class.
假.memory: 亻 is the two-stroke left side; the larger 叚 component fills the right.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 叚
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The remaining nine strokes form 叚 on the right.

回.note: 回 is second-tone huí. In 回國 it means return to one's country.
回.memory: The outer 囗 surrounds a smaller 口. The outside closes only after the inner box is finished.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: The outer enclosure uses the first two strokes and the final closing stroke; this visual group is interrupted by the inner 口.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: inner box
parts.description: The middle three strokes form the inner 口.

國.note: 國 is the Traditional character for country. Learn it in 回國.
國.memory: The outer 囗 encloses 或; write the closing bottom stroke of 囗 last.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: The enclosure begins with two strokes and closes with the final stroke after the inside is complete.

parts.label: 或
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The eight middle strokes form 或 inside the enclosure.

出.note: 出 is first-tone chū. 出去 combines 出 with the familiar 去 to mean go out.
出.memory: The central vertical runs through an upper open bowl and a lower bowl. Write the central stroke first, then the upper bowl, then the lower bowl; the two visual groups interleave.

parts.label: 山-shape
parts.name: linked mountain strokes
parts.description: The first, fourth, and fifth strokes complete the 山-like linked shape.

parts.label: 凵
parts.name: lower open box
parts.description: The second and third strokes form the upper open 凵; the central vertical and lower bowl form the other visual group.

算.note: 算 is fourth-tone suàn. In 打算, the whole word means to plan or intend to do something.
算.memory: The six-stroke bamboo top 𥫗 sits over the eight-stroke lower block 𥃲.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The first six strokes form the paired bamboo marks at the top.

parts.label: 𥃲
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The remaining eight strokes form the lower component.

旅.note: 旅 is third-tone lǚ. In 旅行 it names travel or a trip.
旅.memory: 方 begins the left side; two short middle strokes lead into the four-stroke lower-right 𧘇 shape.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 方.

parts.label: 𠂉
parts.name: upper-right strokes
parts.description: The next two strokes form the small upper-right group.

parts.label: 𧘇
parts.name: lower-right group
parts.description: The final four strokes spread through the lower-right portion.

視.note: 視 is fourth-tone shì. In 電視 it is the second character of the word for television.
視.memory: 礻 is the narrow four-stroke left side; 見 is the seven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 礻
parts.name: spirit component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 礻 on the left.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: seeing component
parts.description: The last seven strokes form 見 on the right.

功.note: 功 is first-tone gōng. In 功課, the whole word means homework.
功.memory: 工 forms the left three strokes and 力 forms the two-stroke right side.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: work component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 工 on the left.

parts.label: 力
parts.name: strength component
parts.description: The final two strokes form 力 on the right.

概.note: 概 is fourth-tone gài. In 大概, the whole word means approximately or probably.
概.memory: 木 is narrow on the left; 既 fills the larger right side.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 木 on the left.

parts.label: 既
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The remaining nine strokes form 既 on the right.

久.note: 久 is third-tone jiǔ. In 多久, it asks the length of time: how long?
久.memory: A short left-falling stroke leads into the bent middle stroke and the long final right-falling stroke.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: first stroke
parts.description: The first left-falling stroke sets the upper-left edge.

parts.label: lower pair
parts.name: bent and final strokes
parts.description: The last two strokes open downward and to the right.

女.note: 女 is third-tone nǚ. In 女朋友 it forms the word for girlfriend.
女.memory: The first turning stroke creates the left curve; the next two strokes cross through the center.

parts.label: turn
parts.name: first turning stroke
parts.description: The first stroke bends through the left and lower part of the character.

parts.label: crossing pair
parts.name: crossing strokes
parts.description: The final two strokes cross the first stroke and balance the character.

建.note: 建 is fourth-tone jiàn. In 建議, the whole word is the noun “suggestion/advice” in this lesson.
建.memory: 聿 is the inner six-stroke body; 廴 wraps around its lower-left side with three finishing strokes.

parts.label: 聿
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 聿 in the center.

parts.label: 廴
parts.name: walking enclosure
parts.description: The final three strokes form the wrapping 廴 around the lower-left.

議.note: 議 is fourth-tone yì. Learn it with 建 as 建議, “suggestion/advice.”
議.memory: 言 is the seven-stroke left side; the larger 義 component fills the right.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言 on the left.

parts.label: 義
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The remaining thirteen strokes form 義 on the right.

夜.note: 夜 is fourth-tone yè. 夜市 is the common word for a night market.
夜.memory: 亠 sits at the top, 亻 on the left below it, and the four-stroke lower-right group finishes with a long sweep.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亠 across the top.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: left person component
parts.description: The next two strokes form 亻 below the top on the left.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower-right group
parts.description: The final four strokes form the lower-right group, including the long last stroke.

市.note: 市 is fourth-tone shì. In 夜市 it means market.
市.memory: 亠 forms the two-stroke top and 巾 forms the three-stroke lower section.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亠.

parts.label: 巾
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 巾 below.

應.note: Read 應 as first-tone yīng in 應該. The whole word means should or ought to.
應.memory: A broad thirteen-stroke upper body sits over 心, whose four strokes anchor the bottom.

parts.label: 䧹
parts.name: upper body
parts.description: The first thirteen strokes form the large upper component.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 心 along the bottom.

該.note: 該 is first-tone gāi. Together, 應該 means should.
該.memory: 言 is the seven-stroke left side; 亥 is the six-stroke right side.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言 on the left.

parts.label: 亥
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 亥 on the right.

特.note: 特 is fourth-tone tè. In 特別 it contributes the meaning special or distinctive.
特.memory: 牜 is the four-stroke left side; 寺 is the six-stroke right side.

parts.label: 牜
parts.name: cow component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 牜 on the left.

parts.label: 寺
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last six strokes form 寺 on the right.

別.note: 別 is second-tone bié. In 特別, the two-character word means special or distinctive.
別.memory: The five-stroke left block sits beside the two-stroke 刂 knife component.

parts.label: 𠮠
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first five strokes form the left block.

parts.label: 刂
parts.name: knife component
parts.description: The final two strokes form 刂 on the right.

決.note: 決 is second-tone jué. In 決定, the whole word means to decide.
決.memory: 氵 forms the three water dots on the left; 夬 forms the four-stroke right side.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵 on the left.

parts.label: 夬
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 夬 on the right.

年.note: 年 is second-tone nián and names a year or a duration measured in years.
年.memory: The six strokes interlock around a central vertical; keep the middle horizontals distinct before the final vertical finish.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes establish the upper-left and top horizontal of 年.

parts.label: middle
parts.name: middle cross
parts.description: The next two strokes build the central horizontal-and-vertical structure.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower finish
parts.description: The last two strokes complete the lower bar and final vertical.

日.note: 日 is fourth-tone rì. In dates it can mean day of the month, as in 三十日.
日.memory: 日 is a tall box with one inner horizontal; the bottom edge closes the frame last.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The outer frame uses the first two strokes and the final closing stroke; the bottom is written last.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: inner horizontal
parts.description: The third stroke is the short horizontal inside the frame.

鐘.meaning: clock; bell; hour in 鐘頭
鐘.note: 鐘 is first-tone zhōng. In 鐘頭, the whole word means an hour.
鐘.memory: 金 fills the left eight strokes and 童 fills the right twelve; keep the dense right side tall and narrow.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: metal component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 金 on the left.

parts.label: 童
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final twelve strokes form 童 on the right.

頭.meaning: head; final character of 鐘頭
頭.note: 頭 is second-tone tóu. In 鐘頭 it completes the everyday word for an hour.
頭.memory: 豆 takes the first seven strokes on the left and 頁 takes the last nine on the right.

parts.label: 豆
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 豆 on the left.

parts.label: 頁
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last nine strokes form 頁 on the right.

非.meaning: not; non-; first character of 非常
非.note: 非 is first-tone fēi. In 非常, it forms the common adverb meaning “very.”
非.memory: Write the left vertical and its three short bars first, then the right vertical and its three bars. The halves face outward and are written consecutively.

parts.label: left half
parts.name: left comb-like group
parts.description: The first four strokes are the left vertical followed by three bars extending left. This is a visual group, not a separate character.

parts.label: right half
parts.name: right comb-like group
parts.description: The last four strokes are the right vertical followed by three bars extending right.

但.meaning: but; however; first character of 但是
但.note: 但 is fourth-tone dàn. In 但是, it introduces a contrast: “but; however.”
但.memory: 亻stands on the left; 旦 on the right has 日 over a final horizontal.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 旦
parts.name: dawn component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 旦 on the right: 日 above the bottom horizontal.

站.note: 站 is fourth-tone zhàn. In 高鐵站, it means a station or stop.
站.memory: 立 takes the left five strokes and 占 takes the right five; keep both halves narrow.

parts.label: 立
parts.name: stand component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 立 on the left.

parts.label: 占
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 占 on the right.

或.meaning: or; perhaps; first character of 或是
或.note: 或 is fourth-tone huò. In 或是, it means “or.”
或.memory: The 戈-like outer strokes wrap around 口 and 一. Because the wrapping strokes are interleaved with the inside, learn 或 as one ordered whole rather than a fake side-by-side split.

parts.label: 或
parts.name: wrapped whole form
parts.description: The eight strokes combine an outer 戈-like frame with the inner 口 and 一 in interleaved stroke order.

利.meaning: benefit; second character of 便利
利.note: 利 is fourth-tone lì. In 便利商店, 便利 is biànlì, “convenient”; note that 便 is biàn here but pián in 便宜.
利.memory: 禾 is the five-stroke left side; the two-stroke 刂 blade finishes the right edge.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 on the left.

parts.label: 刂
parts.name: knife side
parts.description: The last two strokes form 刂 on the right.

汽.meaning: steam; first character of 汽車
汽.note: 汽 is fourth-tone qì. In 公共汽車, 汽車 contributes the vehicle/bus meaning.
汽.memory: Three water dots 氵go on the left; 气 fills the right with four strokes.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water side
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵 on the left.

parts.label: 气
parts.name: air component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 气 on the right.

月.note: 月 is fourth-tone yuè. After a number, it names a month, as in 九月.
月.memory: The first two strokes make the tall outer shape; the final two short horizontals sit inside it.

parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The first two strokes form the tall outer frame of 月.

parts.label: 二
parts.name: inner lines
parts.description: The last two strokes are the two short horizontal lines inside.

號.note: 號 is fourth-tone hào. After a number in a date, it means the numbered day of the month.
號.memory: A compact five-stroke left sound component balances the eight-stroke 虎 component on the right.

parts.label: 号
parts.name: left sound component
parts.description: The first five strokes form the compact left component with 口 above a hooked lower shape.

parts.label: 虎
parts.name: tiger component
parts.description: The final eight strokes form 虎 on the right.

就.note: 就 is fourth-tone jiù. In 要是…就…, it introduces the consequence of the condition.
就.memory: 京 fills the left eight strokes; 尤 completes the right with four strokes.

parts.label: 京
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 京 on the left.

parts.label: 尤
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 尤 on the right.

example.pinyin: Yàoshi yǒu kòng, jiù yìqǐ qù.
example.meaning: If there is time, then go together.

貓.meaning: cat; first character of 貓空
貓.note: 貓 is first-tone māo. Here it is learned as the first character of the Taipei place name 貓空.
貓.memory: 豸 uses the first seven strokes on the left; 苗 uses the final nine strokes on the right.

parts.label: 豸
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 豸 on the left.

parts.label: 苗
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final nine strokes form 苗 on the right, with 艹 above 田.

水.meaning: water; first character of 水果
水.note: 水 is third-tone shuǐ. In 水果, the word as a whole means fruit.
水.memory: 水 is a basic four-stroke radical form. Its central vertical hook anchors the two flowing side strokes, so it is best learned as one whole shape.

parts.label: 水
parts.name: water radical
parts.description: All four strokes form the independent water radical 水; forcing it into borrowed components would be less useful than learning its balanced whole shape.

果.note: 果 is third-tone guǒ. In 水果, it supplies the fruit meaning directly.
果.memory: Write a four-stroke 日-shaped box first. The following 木-shaped group sends its vertical through that box, creating the final 田-like appearance.

parts.label: 日-shaped box
parts.name: upper box
parts.description: The first four strokes form a 日-shaped box, not a complete five-stroke 田. The vertical through its center comes later with the 木-shaped group.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: tree component
parts.description: The last four strokes form the 木-shaped lower portion that passes through the center of the character.

黃.note: 黃 is second-tone huáng and is the color word yellow.
黃.memory: The four-stroke top sits above a broad middle and the final 八-like two strokes at the bottom.

parts.label: 廿
parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the compact 廿-like top of 黃.

parts.label: 一 + 田 + 八
parts.name: lower body
parts.description: After the four-stroke top, write the long horizontal, the five-stroke 田-like middle, and the two separate lower strokes.

色.note: 色 is fourth-tone sè. After a color word such as 黃, it forms 黃色, “yellow.”
色.memory: Two short ⺈ strokes sit above the four-stroke 巴 shape.

parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the small ⺈ shape at the top.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: bottom component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 巴 underneath.

給.note: 給 is third-tone gěi. In this lesson it is the verb “to give.”
給.memory: 糹 takes six strokes on the left; 合 takes six on the right.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: silk component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 糹 on the left.

parts.label: 合
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 合 on the right.

香.note: 香 is first-tone xiāng. For food, it describes a pleasant smell.
香.memory: 禾 forms the five-stroke top; 日 forms the four-stroke bottom.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 at the top.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 日 below.

逛.note: 逛 is fourth-tone guàng. this lesson uses 去逛逛 for going to look around a night market.
逛.memory: Write the seven-stroke 狂 body first, then finish with the three-stroke movement component 辶 wrapping along the lower-left.

parts.label: 狂
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 狂, the compact inner body of 逛.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 辶 and sweep around the lower-left of the inner body.

紅.note: 紅 is second-tone hóng, the color red. In this lesson it combines with 色 to form 紅色.
紅.memory: A six-stroke 糹 thread side stands on the left; the simple three-stroke 工 sits on the right.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: The first six strokes form the narrow 糹 thread component on the left.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: work component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 工 on the right: horizontal, vertical, horizontal.

瓜.note: 瓜 is first-tone guā. In 西瓜, it forms the common word for watermelon.
瓜.memory: 瓜 is a compact five-stroke form: two left-falling strokes frame the bent center, a dot sits inside, and the final right-falling stroke opens outward.

parts.label: 瓜
parts.name: melon form
parts.description: All five strokes interlock in the independent character 瓜; learning the whole five-stroke silhouette is clearer than forcing a false compound split.

拍.note: 拍 is first-tone pāi. this lesson uses 拍照片, 'take a photo.'
拍.memory: 扌, the hand side, takes three strokes on the left; 白 fills the right with five.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 扌, linking 拍 to hand actions.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: white component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 白 on the right.

笑.note: 笑 is fourth-tone xiào and means to laugh or smile.
笑.memory: The six small strokes of 𥫗 form the bamboo top; the four strokes of 夭 spread underneath.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The first six strokes form the paired bamboo top 𥫗.

parts.label: 夭
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 夭 underneath the bamboo top.

心.note: 心 is first-tone xīn. In 開心, the whole word means happy or cheerful.
心.memory: Begin with the left dot, write the curved hook, then add the middle and right dots. The three dots balance the hooked center.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart radical
parts.description: The independent 心 form has a left dot, a curved hook, then two more dots; all four strokes belong to the heart radical.

穿.note: 穿 is first-tone chuān. With clothing, it means to wear or put on.
穿.memory: 穴 makes the five-stroke roof-and-space at the top; 牙 completes the lower four strokes.

parts.label: 穴
parts.name: cave component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 穴 across the top.

parts.label: 牙
parts.name: tooth component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 牙 below.

衣.note: 衣 is first-tone yī. In 衣服, it supplies the clothing meaning.
衣.memory: Begin with the two-stroke 亠 top, then open the four lower strokes into the familiar garment shape.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the small 亠 top.

parts.label: 𧘇
parts.name: garment body
parts.description: The final four strokes open beneath the top to form the lower garment body.

芒.note: 芒 is second-tone máng. In this course, learn it primarily as the first character of 芒果, mango.
芒.memory: The three-stroke 艹 grass top sits above the three-stroke 亡 shape.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the compact 艹 grass component across the top.

parts.label: 亡
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 亡 below the grass top.

住.note: 住 is fourth-tone zhù. In this lesson it means to stay at a hotel or live somewhere.
住.memory: 亻 takes the first two strokes on the left; 主 fills the right with a dot above three horizontals crossed by a vertical.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow person component 亻.

parts.label: 主
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 主 on the right.

男.note: 男 is second-tone nán. this lesson uses 男 before another noun, such as 男學生.
男.memory: 田 forms the five-stroke top; 力 adds the two-stroke lower part.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: field component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 田 at the top.

parts.label: 力
parts.name: strength component
parts.description: The final two strokes form 力 underneath.

矮.note: 矮 is third-tone ǎi and describes a person's short height.
矮.memory: 矢 makes the five-stroke left side; 委 makes the eight-stroke right side with 禾 above 女.

parts.label: 矢
parts.name: arrow component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 矢 on the left.

parts.label: 委
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final eight strokes form 委 on the right, with 禾 above 女.

弟.note: 弟 is fourth-tone dì. The family word 弟弟 repeats it and means younger brother.
弟.memory: Two 丷 dots sit at the top; the lower five-stroke body bends through a bow-like center and finishes with a left sweep.

parts.label: 丷
parts.name: top dots
parts.description: The first two strokes form the paired 丷 top.

parts.label: 𢎨
parts.name: lower body
parts.description: The final five strokes form the bent lower body of 弟.

些.note: 些 is first-tone xiē. With 這, it forms 這些, 'these.'
些.memory: 此 forms the six-stroke upper body; two horizontal strokes 二 sit underneath.

parts.label: 此
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 此 across the top.

parts.label: 二
parts.name: two component
parts.description: The final two horizontal strokes form 二 underneath.

乾.meaning: dry; first character of 乾淨
乾.note: 乾 is first-tone gān in 乾淨, 'clean.' This unit teaches it as part of that word.
乾.memory: The dense eight-stroke 𠦝 group occupies the left; compact 乞 uses the final three strokes on the right.

parts.label: 𠦝
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes build the compact left side 𠦝.

parts.label: 乞
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 乞 on the right.

淨.note: 淨 is fourth-tone jìng. Together with 乾 it forms 乾淨, 'clean.'
淨.memory: Three water dots 氵 stand on the left; 爭 supplies the eight-stroke right side.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵 on the left.

parts.label: 爭
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final eight strokes form 爭 on the right.

藍.note: 藍 is second-tone lán. With 色 it forms 藍色, blue.
藍.memory: The four-stroke 艹 top sits above the dense fourteen-stroke 監 body.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the Traditional 艹 top.

parts.label: 監
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final fourteen strokes form 監 beneath the grass top.

往.note: 往 is third-tone wǎng. It introduces direction; the conversation uses 從窗戶往外看, look outward from the window.
往.memory: 彳 takes three narrow walking strokes on the left; 主 fills the right with five strokes.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: step component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 彳, a movement-related component.

parts.label: 主
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 主 on the right.

因.note: 因 is first-tone yīn. In 因為, it introduces a cause.
因.memory: The outer 囗 begins first, 大 is written inside it, and the last horizontal closes the enclosure.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: enclosure component
parts.description: Strokes 1–2 begin the outer enclosure and the final stroke closes its bottom.

parts.label: 大
parts.name: big component
parts.description: The middle three strokes form 大 inside the enclosure before the box closes.

窗.note: 窗 is first-tone chuāng. Learn it with 戶 as 窗戶, window.
窗.memory: The five-stroke 穴 roof sits above the seven-stroke lower 囱-shaped body.

parts.label: 穴
parts.name: cave/roof component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 穴 across the top.

parts.label: 囱
parts.name: lower window-shaped body
parts.description: The final seven strokes form the enclosed lower body beneath 穴.

戶.meaning: door; household; second character of 窗戶
戶.note: 戶 is fourth-tone hù. In 窗戶, the whole word means window.
戶.memory: 戶 is a compact four-stroke form with a top stroke and a broad sloping lower shape; keep the left side open and tall.

parts.label: 戶
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: All four strokes form the independent Traditional character 戶.

租.note: 租 is first-tone zū. In this lesson it is the verb “to rent,” especially a room or apartment.
租.memory: 禾 forms the five-stroke left side; 且 forms the five-stroke right side. Keep the two blocks narrow and balanced.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 on the left.

parts.label: 且
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 且, with its stacked horizontal lines, on the right.

房.note: 房 is the first character of 房子, house. Notice the upper-left 戶 and the 方 beneath it.
房.memory: 房 shelters 方 beneath 戶. The long left stroke of 戶 runs down beside the lower group.

parts.label: 戶
parts.name: door-shaped upper group
parts.description: 戶 begins above 方, then its long sloping stroke extends down the left side of the lower group.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: 方 sits underneath the upper part of 戶. Leave room for its hooked and slanting strokes below the horizontal.

客.meaning: guest; first character of 客廳
客.note: 客 is fourth-tone kè. In 客廳 it is part of the word for living room.
客.memory: 宀 is the three-stroke roof; 各 fills the lower space with a crossing top above 口.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 宀 across the top.

parts.label: 各
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 各 under the roof.

廚.meaning: kitchen; first character of 廚房
廚.note: 廚 is second-tone chú. Learn it as the first character of 廚房, “kitchen.”
廚.memory: 广 makes a three-stroke shelter; the remaining 尌-shaped body fills the inside without crossing the left shelter.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: shelter component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the sloping 广 shelter.

parts.label: 尌
parts.name: inner body
parts.description: The remaining twelve strokes build the dense inner body beneath 广.

左.note: 左 gives the left direction. Notice 工 below the upper strokes.
左.memory: Look for 工 under the overhanging top of 左; compare the 口 in 右.

parts.label: 𠂇
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form a horizontal top and a long slant down to the left.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: work-shaped part
parts.description: 工 has two horizontal lines joined by a short vertical. It distinguishes 左 from 右.

右.note: 右 gives the right direction. Notice 口 below the upper strokes. Follow the guide: its opening stroke order differs from 左.
右.memory: Look for 口 under the overhanging top of 右; compare the 工 in 左.

parts.label: 𠂇
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form the overhanging top and the slant down to the left.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth-shaped part
parts.description: 口 is the small box below the top strokes. It distinguishes 右 from 左.

浴.meaning: bathe; first character of 浴室
浴.note: 浴 is fourth-tone yù. In 浴室 it is part of the word for bathroom.
浴.memory: Three water dots 氵 stay narrow on the left; 谷 fills the right with spreading upper strokes above 口.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵.

parts.label: 谷
parts.name: valley component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 谷 on the right.

超.meaning: surpass; first character of 超商
超.note: 超 is the first character of 超商, the everyday Taiwan word for a convenience store.
超.memory: 走 + 召: the familiar 走 stretches underneath 召, which has 刀 above 口.

parts.label: 走
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: 走 occupies the left side and sends its long final stroke underneath the right component.

parts.label: 召
parts.name: upper-right component
parts.description: 召 is 刀 above 口. Nest this smaller group above the long base of 走.

走.note: 走 means walk; in a directions question it asks how to get somewhere.
走.memory: Remember 走 by 土 above a long, spreading lower stroke.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: upper shape
parts.description: The upper three strokes form a 土 shape: a vertical crossing two horizontal lines.

parts.label: 龰
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: The lower group leads down to the long final stroke sweeping out to the right.

路.note: 路 means road. 路口 means an intersection.
路.memory: Remember 路 as 足 + 各: a small mouth above foot strokes on the left, and a crossing top above 口 on the right.

parts.label: 足
parts.name: foot component
parts.description: 足 forms the left side, with 口 at the top and the foot-shaped strokes below.

parts.label: 各
parts.name: right part
parts.description: 各 has crossing, spreading strokes at the top and a small 口 underneath.

間.note: 間 is first-tone jiān here. It counts rooms and houses: 兩間房間.
間.memory: The eight-stroke 門 surrounds a four-stroke 日. Keep the inner 日 centered with space around it.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: door frame
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the Traditional door frame 門.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 日 inside the frame.

套.meaning: set; first character of 套房
套.note: 套 is fourth-tone tào. 套房 is a suite: a room with its own bathroom in this lesson.
套.memory: 大 spreads across the top; 镸 fills the lower seven strokes and stays centered under it.

parts.label: 大
parts.name: big component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 大.

parts.label: 镸
parts.name: long component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form the lower component.

再.note: 再 is fourth-tone zài. In this lesson it orders a later action: think first, then call.
再.memory: A single top bar sits over 冉. The lower frame is crossed by a central vertical and finishes with the long horizontal.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top bar
parts.description: Begin with the single horizontal roof.

parts.label: 冉
parts.name: lower structure
parts.description: The remaining five strokes form 冉 below the roof.

話.note: 話 is fourth-tone huà. It appears in 電話 and 打電話.
話.memory: 言 forms the seven-stroke left side; 舌 forms the six-stroke right side with 口 at the bottom.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言.

parts.label: 舌
parts.name: tongue component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 舌.

進.note: 進 is fourth-tone jìn. In 請進, it means enter / come in.
進.memory: Write the eight-stroke 隹 body first, then add the four-stroke movement component 辶 wrapping along the lower-left.

parts.label: 隹
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 隹, the compact inner body.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The final four strokes form the Traditional movement component 辶 around the lower-left.

喂.note: 喂 is fourth-tone wèi here, the conventional way to answer or address someone on the phone.
喂.memory: 口 is a compact three-stroke block on the left; 畏 fills the taller right side.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 口.

parts.label: 畏
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final nine strokes form 畏 on the right.

收.note: 收 is first-tone shōu. In 收到, it combines with 到 to mean receive.
收.memory: The two-stroke left shape stays narrow; 攵 uses four active strokes on the right.

parts.label: 丩
parts.name: left shape
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow left group.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: action component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 攵.

已.note: 已 is third-tone yǐ. It is the first character of 已經, “already.”
已.memory: 已 is a compact three-stroke bent shape. Keep the final rising stroke inside the upper bend rather than closing a box.

parts.label: 已
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: All three strokes form one compact bent character.

經.meaning: pass through; second character of 已經
經.note: 經 is first-tone jīng. In 已經 it completes the fixed adverb meaning “already.”
經.memory: 糹 forms six thread strokes on the left; 巠 forms the seven-stroke right block.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 糹.

parts.label: 巠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 巠.

習.note: 習 is second-tone xí. In 習慣 it is part of the verb “to get used to; be accustomed to.”
習.memory: 羽 forms two wing-like groups across the top; 白 is the five-stroke block underneath.

parts.label: 羽
parts.name: feather component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 羽.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: white component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 白.

慣.meaning: accustomed; second character of 習慣
慣.note: 慣 is fourth-tone guàn. Learn 習慣 as the complete word “to get used to; be accustomed to.”
慣.memory: 忄 supplies three narrow heart strokes on the left; 貫 fills the denser eleven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 忄.

parts.label: 貫
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final eleven strokes form 貫.

器.note: 器 is fourth-tone qì. In 熱水器 it means an appliance or device: a water heater.
器.memory: Four 口 boxes surround 犬 in the middle. Keep the top pair and bottom pair balanced around the central four strokes.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: upper-left mouth
parts.description: The first three strokes form the upper-left 口.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: upper-right mouth
parts.description: The next three strokes form the upper-right 口.

parts.label: 犬
parts.name: central component
parts.description: Four strokes form 犬 in the middle.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower-left mouth
parts.description: The next three strokes form the lower-left 口.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower-right mouth
parts.description: The final three strokes form the lower-right 口.

像.note: 像 is fourth-tone xiàng. In 好像 it helps express “seem; appear to be,” often softening a comment.
像.memory: 亻 + 象: a narrow person component beside the full twelve-stroke 象 shape.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 象
parts.name: elephant component
parts.description: The remaining twelve strokes form 象 on the right; keep its stacked turns and lower sweeping strokes open and balanced.

裝.note: 裝 is first-tone zhuāng. In the rental conversation it is the verb “to install,” as in installing cable TV.
裝.memory: 壯 forms the seven-stroke upper block; 衣 supplies the six lower strokes.

parts.label: 壯
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 壯.

parts.label: 衣
parts.name: clothing component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 衣.

過.note: 過 is fourth-tone guò. Here it appears inside 不過, “however/but”; that use is different from the later direction verb 過 “go past.”
過.memory: Build the nine-stroke 咼 first; then add the four-stroke movement component 辶, whose final sweep runs underneath.

parts.label: 咼
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The first nine strokes form 咼.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 辶 and sweep under the inner block.

付.note: 付 is fourth-tone fù. In this lesson it means to pay money.
付.memory: 亻 takes two strokes on the left; 寸 uses the final three strokes on the right.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻.

parts.label: 寸
parts.name: inch component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 寸.

關.note: 關 is first-tone guān. In 沒關係, the whole expression means “it doesn't matter / no problem.”
關.memory: The eight-stroke 門 creates the outer door frame; the remaining eleven strokes form the compact inner structure.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: door frame
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 門.

parts.label: inner
parts.name: inner structure
parts.description: The final eleven strokes fill the space inside the door frame.

係.note: 係 is fourth-tone xì. It is the final character of 沒關係.
係.memory: 亻 is the two-stroke left component; 系 supplies the seven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻.

parts.label: 系
parts.name: thread-related component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 系.

線.note: 線 is fourth-tone xiàn. In 有線電視 it refers to a cable or wired line.
線.memory: 糹 makes the six-stroke thread component on the left; 泉 makes the nine-stroke right block.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 糹.

parts.label: 泉
parts.name: spring component
parts.description: The final nine strokes form 泉.

臺.note: 臺 is the Traditional character used in 臺灣. Hanzi Steps formally adds it here because the cumulative curriculum had used Taiwan as context without first teaching this character.
臺.memory: Build 士 and 口 at the top, place the 冖 cover through the middle, then finish with 至 at the bottom.

parts.label: 士
parts.name: scholar component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 士 at the top.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The next three strokes form 口.

parts.label: 冖
parts.name: cover component
parts.description: Two strokes make the cover across the middle.

parts.label: 至
parts.name: arrive component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 至 below the cover.

灣.meaning: bay; gulf (second character of 臺灣)
灣.note: 灣 is first-tone wān. In 臺灣 it is the second character of the place name Taiwan.
灣.memory: Keep the three-dot water component 氵 narrow on the left; the dense 彎 component occupies the full right side.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵.

parts.label: 彎
parts.name: bend component
parts.description: The remaining twenty-two strokes form 彎 on the right.

畫.meaning: draw; second character of 計畫
畫.note: 畫 is fourth-tone huà. Here, learn it inside 計畫 'to plan to'; do not translate the two characters separately when reading the compound.
畫.memory: Write the 聿-like upper frame first, build 田 beneath it, and close with the long final 一.

parts.label: 聿
parts.name: brush-like upper component
parts.description: The first six strokes form the brush-like upper structure.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: field component
parts.description: The next five strokes form 田.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: final horizontal
parts.description: The last stroke closes the character along the bottom.

先.note: 先 is first-tone xiān. Put it before the first action in 先…再… to mark what happens first.
先.memory: The four-stroke upper shape stands above 儿, whose two legs spread at the bottom.

parts.name: upper shape
parts.description: The first four strokes form the compact upper structure.

parts.label: 儿
parts.name: legs component
parts.description: The final two strokes form 儿.

念.note: 念 is fourth-tone niàn. In this lesson it is the Taiwan Mandarin verb 'to study,' as in 念中文 or 念大學.
念.memory: 今 sits on top of 心: four strokes above and four heart strokes below.

parts.label: 今
parts.name: now component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 今.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 心.

語.note: 語 is third-tone yǔ. Together with 言 it forms 語言, 'language.'
語.memory: 言 occupies the left seven strokes; 吾 fills the right seven.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言.

parts.label: 吾
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 吾.

言.note: 言 is second-tone yán. Learn it here as the second character of 語言.
言.memory: Start with the top mark and horizontal lines, then finish the lower 口-shaped speech block.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top mark
parts.description: The first two strokes establish the top of 言.

parts.label: 二
parts.name: middle lines
parts.description: The next two strokes form the paired middle lines.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth shape
parts.description: The final three strokes form the lower 口.

需.note: 需 is first-tone xū. In this lesson, learn it inside 需要 'to need.'
需.memory: 雨 forms the eight-stroke top; 而 supplies the six-stroke lower block.

parts.label: 雨
parts.name: rain component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 雨.

parts.label: 而
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 而.

花.note: 花 is first-tone huā. In 這得花不少錢 it is the lesson verb 'to spend (time or money),' not the noun 'flower.'
花.memory: The four-stroke 艹 sits across the top; 化 forms the four strokes below.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the Taiwan-form 艹 top.

parts.label: 化
parts.name: change component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 化.

獎.note: 獎 is third-tone jiǎng. In 獎學金 it refers to an award or scholarship fund.
獎.memory: 將 fills the upper part; 犬 forms the four-stroke bottom. The last dot is the final stroke of 犬.

parts.label: 將
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first eleven strokes form 將.

parts.label: 犬
parts.name: dog component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 犬; its dot is written last.

金.note: 金 is first-tone jīn. In 獎學金 it contributes the sense of money or funds.
金.memory: The top opens outward, a central vertical anchors the character, and the final horizontal closes the base.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: All eight strokes form the balanced 金 character.

成.note: 成 is second-tone chéng. Here it is the first character of 成績, 'grades; academic results.'
成.memory: Keep the inner bend compact while the long slanting stroke and final hook open the character to the right.

parts.label: 成
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: All six strokes form the compact 成 shape.

績.note: 績 is first-tone jī. In 成績 it completes the word for grades or academic results.
績.memory: 糹 is the six-stroke thread component on the left; 責 forms the eleven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 糹.

parts.label: 責
parts.name: responsibility component
parts.description: The final eleven strokes form 責.

費.note: 費 is fourth-tone fèi. In this lesson, learn it inside 學費, 'tuition.'
費.memory: Write the five-stroke 弗 upper part first, then place the seven-stroke 貝 below it.

parts.label: 弗
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 弗 at the top.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: shell component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 貝 at the bottom.

司.note: 司 is first-tone sī. Here it is learned as the second character of 公司, 'company.'
司.memory: Keep the outer turning stroke compact around the inner 一 and 口 structure.

parts.label: 司
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: All five strokes form the compact 司 character.

替.note: 替 is fourth-tone tì and is a preposition meaning 'for; on behalf of.' Put 替 + person before the action: 公司替我付 = 'the company pays for me.'
替.memory: Write 㚘—two 夫 shapes side by side—across the top, then finish with the four-stroke 曰 at the bottom.

parts.label: 㚘
parts.name: paired 夫 component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 㚘, visually two 夫 shapes side by side.

parts.label: 曰
parts.name: 曰 component
parts.description: The final four strokes form the wide 曰 component at the bottom.

example.meaning: pay for me; pay on my behalf

希.note: 希 is first-tone xī. Learn it together with 望 in 希望, 'to hope.'
希.memory: Start with the crossed top strokes, then build the 布-like lower structure underneath.

parts.label: 乂
parts.name: crossed top
parts.description: The first two strokes form the crossed top.

parts.label: 布
parts.name: lower structure
parts.description: The final five strokes form the lower 布-like structure.

望.note: 望 is fourth-tone wàng. In this lesson it completes 希望, 'to hope.'
望.memory: Set 亡 and 月 across the upper area, then anchor the character with 王 at the bottom.

parts.label: 亡
parts.name: upper-left component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 亡.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: moon component
parts.description: The next four strokes form 月.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: king component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 王.

班.note: 班 is first-tone bān. Here it appears in 上班, 'to go to work.' In Taiwan's standard form, the center is written as two narrow strokes between the two 王 sides; do not confuse 班 with 斑.
班.memory: Balance 王 on the left and 王 on the right; the two narrow middle strokes, 丶 then 丿, are the modern form of the knife-derived center.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: left jade component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 王 on the left.

parts.label: 丶丿
parts.name: knife-derived middle strokes
parts.description: The next two strokes are a dot and a left-falling stroke in the narrow center.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: right jade component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 王 on the right.

累.note: 累 is fourth-tone lèi. The this lesson line 真的很累 describes being exhausted from working and studying.
累.memory: Write 田 first, then place the six-stroke 糸 thread component underneath.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: field component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 田.

parts.label: 糸
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 糸.

加.meaning: add; first character of 加油
加.note: 加 is first-tone jiā. In 加油, the whole expression is encouragement: 'keep it up / keep up the good work.'
加.memory: Write 力 on the left, then add the three-stroke 口 on the right.

parts.label: 力
parts.name: strength component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 力.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 口.

油.meaning: oil; second character of 加油
油.note: 油 is second-tone yóu. In 加油, do not translate the two characters literally; the phrase is used to encourage someone.
油.memory: Keep 氵 narrow on the left and write the five-stroke 由 clearly on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵.

parts.label: 由
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 由.

工.note: 工 is first-tone gōng. It is the first character of 工作, the this lesson word for both 'to work' and 'job/work'.
工.memory: A top line, a central vertical, and a longer base make a simple workbench-like 工.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: whole 工 form
parts.description: All three strokes form the simple, indivisible learner shape of 工.

作.note: 作 is fourth-tone zuò. In 工作 it combines with 工 to form 'work'; do not confuse it with the already-known 做, which is also pronounced zuò.
作.memory: Write the two-stroke person 亻 on the left, then the five-stroke 乍 on the right.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻, the person component.

parts.label: 乍
parts.name: 乍 component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 乍 on the right.

試.note: 試 is fourth-tone shì. the conversation uses 試 in 試試看, 'give it a try / try and see what happens.'
試.memory: Build 言 on the left for speech, then 式 on the right; together they form 試.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言 on the left.

parts.label: 式
parts.name: 式 component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 式 on the right.

難.note: 難 is second-tone nán. Before an action verb in this lesson, it means 'hard/difficult to': 難找 'hard to find', 難學 'hard to learn'.
難.memory: Build the eleven-stroke left side as 廿 above an interwoven 口 and 夫, then add the eight-stroke 隹 'short-tailed bird' on the right.

parts.label: 廿＋口／夫
parts.name: left structural component
parts.description: The first eleven strokes form the left side: 廿 above an interwoven 口 and 夫, matching the Traditional decomposition ⿱廿⿻口夫.

parts.label: 隹
parts.name: short-tailed bird component
parts.description: The final eight strokes form 隹 on the right.

忘.note: 忘 is fourth-tone wàng, 'to forget'. In the reaction 我怎麼忘了, it means 'How could I forget!'
忘.memory: Put 亡 'lost/gone' above 心 'heart': when something is gone from the heart/mind, you 忘 'forget'.

parts.label: 亡
parts.name: 亡 component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 亡 at the top.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 心 at the bottom.

記.note: 記 is fourth-tone jì. In 記得 jìde it contributes the idea of remembering.
記.memory: Write 言 'speech/words' on the left and 己 on the right: words kept for oneself can be 記 'recorded/remembered'.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言 on the left.

parts.label: 己
parts.name: 己 component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 己 on the right.

當.meaning: to be; act as; in 當然 'of course'
當.note: 當 is first-tone dāng in 當然 dāngrán, the this lesson word for 'of course / certainly'.
當.memory: Build 尚 on top and 田 below; together they form 當.

parts.label: 尚
parts.name: 尚 component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 尚 at the top.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: field component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 田 at the bottom.

然.meaning: so; thus; in 當然 'of course'
然.note: 然 is second-tone rán. In this unit it is learned inside 當然 dāngrán, 'of course / certainly'.
然.memory: The upper eight strokes form the 肰-like body (月 plus 犬), and the four-dot fire 灬 finishes 然 at the bottom.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: meat/moon-shaped component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the 月-shaped component at upper left.

parts.label: 犬
parts.name: dog component
parts.description: The next four strokes form 犬 at upper right.

parts.label: 灬
parts.name: four-dot fire
parts.description: The final four strokes form 灬 across the bottom.

交.note: 交 appears in 交換 jiāohuàn, “exchange.” Learn the two-character word as a unit.
交.memory: A dot and horizontal sit over two small strokes and a wide crossing pair. The crossing shape is a visual cue for exchange.

parts.label: 交
parts.name: crossing form
parts.description: A dot and horizontal sit over two small strokes and a wide crossing pair. The crossing shape is a visual cue for exchange.

換.note: 換 means “change; exchange.” 交換 jiāohuàn means to exchange something with someone.
換.memory: A hand 扌 stands beside 奐. Use the hand as a cue for changing or exchanging something.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: Hand component in 換: strokes 1–3. A hand 扌 stands beside 奐. Use the hand as a cue for changing or exchanging something.

parts.label: 奐
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 換: strokes 4–12. A hand 扌 stands beside 奐. Use the hand as a cue for changing or exchanging something.

牙.note: 牙 means “tooth” on its own. In 西班牙文, it is part of the name for Spanish; do not translate that name character by character.
牙.memory: Notice the angular top, the long hooked stroke, and the final slant crossing down to the left.

parts.label: 牙
parts.name: tooth form
parts.description: Notice the angular top, the long hooked stroke, and the final slant crossing down to the left.

必.note: 必 relates to necessity. 不必 in 不必客氣 means “there is no need to”; the phrase means “You’re welcome / don’t mention it.”
必.memory: It resembles 心 with an extra diagonal passing through it. Follow the animation: the writing order is not simply 心 plus a final slash.

parts.label: 必
parts.name: crossed-heart form
parts.description: It resembles 心 with an extra diagonal passing through it. Follow the animation: the writing order is not simply 心 plus a final slash.

example.meaning: no need to be so polite

氣.meaning: air; manner; component of 客氣
氣.note: 氣 means “air; breath,” but 客氣 kèqì is a whole word about politeness. 不必客氣 is a polite response to thanks.
氣.memory: The sweeping 气 encloses 米. Leave room for the rice-like lower strokes beneath the top.

parts.label: 气
parts.name: outer component
parts.description: Outer component in 氣: strokes 1–4. The sweeping 气 encloses 米. Leave room for the rice-like lower strokes beneath the top.

parts.label: 米
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: Inner component in 氣: strokes 5–10. The sweeping 气 encloses 米. Leave room for the rice-like lower strokes beneath the top.

門.note: 門 mén means “door; gate.” 門口 ménkǒu is the entrance or doorway.
門.memory: Picture two tall door panels facing each other, with an opening between them. Write the left panel before the right.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: paired door panels
parts.description: Picture two tall door panels facing each other, with an opening between them. Write the left panel before the right.

口.note: You have seen 口 inside other characters. Now write it on its own. In 路口 it refers to an opening or junction.
口.memory: Remember 口 as a three-stroke box: left edge, top-and-right bend, then the bottom closes it.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: 口 is a single component. Its top and right edges are written together as one bent stroke.

禮.note: 禮 relates to ceremony or courtesy. 禮物 lǐwù means “gift; present.”
禮.memory: A narrow 礻 stands beside the dense 豊. Keep the left component distinct from 衤, which has an extra stroke.

parts.label: 礻
parts.name: ritual component
parts.description: Ritual component in 禮: strokes 1–4. A narrow 礻 stands beside the dense 豊. Keep the left component distinct from 衤, which has an extra stroke.

parts.label: 豊
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 禮: strokes 5–17. A narrow 礻 stands beside the dense 豊. Keep the left component distinct from 衤, which has an extra stroke.

物.note: 物 means “thing; object.” In 禮物 lǐwù, the whole word means “gift.”
物.memory: The narrow 牛 component stands beside 勿. Leave space for the two slanting inner strokes on the right.

parts.label: 牜
parts.name: ox component
parts.description: Ox component in 物: strokes 1–4. The narrow 牛 component stands beside 勿. Leave space for the two slanting inner strokes on the right.

parts.label: 勿
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 物: strokes 5–8. The narrow 牛 component stands beside 勿. Leave space for the two slanting inner strokes on the right.

訂.note: 訂 dìng means “order; reserve” here, as when arranging something in advance.
訂.memory: Speech 言 stands beside 丁. The two-stroke right side also helps you remember the sound dìng.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: Speech component in 訂: strokes 1–7. Speech 言 stands beside 丁. The two-stroke right side also helps you remember the sound dìng.

parts.label: 丁
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 訂: strokes 8–9. Speech 言 stands beside 丁. The two-stroke right side also helps you remember the sound dìng.

豬.note: 豬 zhū means “pig.” In 豬腳 zhūjiǎo, it identifies pork trotters as a food.
豬.memory: The pig component 豕 sits beside 者. Keep the long slanting strokes on the left separate from the right-hand block.

parts.label: 豕
parts.name: pig component
parts.description: Pig component in 豬: strokes 1–7. The pig component 豕 sits beside 者. Keep the long slanting strokes on the left separate from the right-hand block.

parts.label: 者
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 豬: strokes 8–15. The pig component 豕 sits beside 者. Keep the long slanting strokes on the left separate from the right-hand block.

腳.note: 腳 jiǎo means “foot.” 豬腳 means pork trotters, not an instruction involving feet.
腳.memory: The flesh component 月 is on the left; the larger 卻 fills the right. The body component is a cue for a foot.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: flesh component
parts.description: Flesh component in 腳: strokes 1–4. The flesh component 月 is on the left; the larger 卻 fills the right. The body component is a cue for a foot.

parts.label: 卻
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 腳: strokes 5–13. The flesh component 月 is on the left; the larger 卻 fills the right. The body component is a cue for a foot.

蛋.note: 蛋 dàn means “egg.” In 蛋糕 dàngāo, the whole word means “cake.”
蛋.memory: Stack the five-stroke upper section above 虫. Keep the lower box and its central vertical centered.

parts.label: 疋
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Upper component in 蛋: strokes 1–5. Stack the five-stroke upper section above 虫. Keep the lower box and its central vertical centered.

parts.label: 虫
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Lower component in 蛋: strokes 6–11. Stack the five-stroke upper section above 虫. Keep the lower box and its central vertical centered.

傳.note: 傳 chuán relates to passing something on. 傳統 chuántǒng means “tradition; traditional.”
傳.memory: A person 亻 stands beside 專. Imagine traditions being passed from person to person as a memory cue.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: Person component in 傳: strokes 1–2. A person 亻 stands beside 專. Imagine traditions being passed from person to person as a memory cue.

parts.label: 專
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 傳: strokes 3–13. A person 亻 stands beside 專. Imagine traditions being passed from person to person as a memory cue.

統.note: 統 tǒng appears in 傳統 chuántǒng, “tradition; traditional.” Learn the whole word rather than guessing from the parts.
統.memory: Threads 糹 stand beside 充. Think of traditions linked together like threads as a visual mnemonic.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: Thread component in 統: strokes 1–6. Threads 糹 stand beside 充. Think of traditions linked together like threads as a visual mnemonic.

parts.label: 充
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 統: strokes 7–12. Threads 糹 stand beside 充. Think of traditions linked together like threads as a visual mnemonic.

輕.note: 輕 qīng means “light,” the opposite of heavy. 年輕 niánqīng is the whole word for “young.”
輕.memory: 車 is on the left and 巠 is on the right. Keep the two seven-stroke blocks balanced.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: vehicle component
parts.description: Vehicle component in 輕: strokes 1–7. 車 is on the left and 巠 is on the right. Keep the two seven-stroke blocks balanced.

parts.label: 巠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 輕: strokes 8–14. 車 is on the left and 巠 is on the right. Keep the two seven-stroke blocks balanced.

部.note: 部 bù refers to a part or section. 大部分 dàbùfen means “most; the greater part.”
部.memory: 立 over 口 forms the left block 咅; the narrow 阝 is on the right. Compare 陪, where 阝 is on the left.

parts.label: 咅
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Left component in 部: strokes 1–8. 立 over 口 forms the left block 咅; the narrow 阝 is on the right. Compare 陪, where 阝 is on the left.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 部: strokes 9–10. 立 over 口 forms the left block 咅; the narrow 阝 is on the right. Compare 陪, where 阝 is on the left.

糕.note: 糕 gāo appears in 蛋糕 dàngāo, “cake.” It is also used in names of other cakes and prepared foods.
糕.memory: Rice 米 sits beside 羔. The rice component helps you remember that 糕 is a food character.

parts.label: 米
parts.name: rice component
parts.description: Rice component in 糕: strokes 1–6. Rice 米 sits beside 羔. The rice component helps you remember that 糕 is a food character.

parts.label: 羔
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 糕: strokes 7–16. Rice 米 sits beside 羔. The rice component helps you remember that 糕 is a food character.

祝.note: 祝 zhù means “wish” when offering good wishes: 祝你生日快樂, “Wish you a happy birthday.”
祝.memory: A four-stroke 礻 sits beside 兄. Keep 礻 distinct from the five-stroke clothing component 衤.

parts.label: 礻
parts.name: ritual component
parts.description: Ritual component in 祝: strokes 1–4. A four-stroke 礻 sits beside 兄. Keep 礻 distinct from the five-stroke clothing component 衤.

parts.label: 兄
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 祝: strokes 5–9. A four-stroke 礻 sits beside 兄. Keep 礻 distinct from the five-stroke clothing component 衤.

如.note: 如 rú means “as; like.” In 萬事如意, it expresses things going as wished: “May everything go your way.”
如.memory: 女 stands beside a small 口. Keep the woman component narrower so the mouth has room on the right.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: Woman component in 如: strokes 1–3. 女 stands beside a small 口. Keep the woman component narrower so the mouth has room on the right.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: Mouth component in 如: strokes 4–6. 女 stands beside a small 口. Keep the woman component narrower so the mouth has room on the right.

冷.note: 冷 lěng describes being cold: 天氣很冷 means “the weather is cold.”
冷.memory: The two ice strokes 冫 on the left are a cue for cold; 令 fills the right side.

parts.label: 冫
parts.name: ice component
parts.description: Ice component in 冷: strokes 1–2. The two ice strokes 冫 on the left are a cue for cold; 令 fills the right side.

parts.label: 令
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 冷: strokes 3–7. The two ice strokes 冫 on the left are a cue for cold; 令 fills the right side.

滑.note: 滑 means “slide; slippery.” In 滑雪 huáxuě, the whole word means “ski.”
滑.memory: Water 氵 on the left can remind you of a slippery surface; keep the taller 骨 on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: Water component in 滑: strokes 1–3. Water 氵 on the left can remind you of a slippery surface; keep the taller 骨 on the right.

parts.label: 骨
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 滑: strokes 4–12. Water 氵 on the left can remind you of a slippery surface; keep the taller 骨 on the right.

雪.note: 雪 xuě means “snow.” 下雪 means “to snow,” with 下 describing precipitation falling.
雪.memory: The rain component 雨 sits above a short three-stroke base. Picture snow falling from the sky.

parts.label: 雨
parts.name: rain component
parts.description: Rain component in 雪: strokes 1–8. The rain component 雨 sits above a short three-stroke base. Picture snow falling from the sky.

parts.label: 彐
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Lower component in 雪: strokes 9–11. The rain component 雨 sits above a short three-stroke base. Picture snow falling from the sky.

春.note: 春 chūn means “spring.” Learn 春天 chūntiān as the season name.
春.memory: Three horizontal lines and two spreading strokes sit above 日. Keep the lower sun centered.

parts.label: 春上部
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: Upper strokes in 春: strokes 1–5. Three horizontal lines and two spreading strokes sit above 日. Keep the lower sun centered.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: Sun component in 春: strokes 6–9. Three horizontal lines and two spreading strokes sit above 日. Keep the lower sun centered.

冬.note: 冬 dōng means “winter.” 冬天 dōngtiān names the season.
冬.memory: A three-stroke upper shape sits above two separate dots. Keep both dots below the crossing upper strokes.

parts.label: 夂
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Upper component in 冬: strokes 1–3. A three-stroke upper shape sits above two separate dots. Keep both dots below the crossing upper strokes.

parts.label: 冬下部
parts.name: lower dots
parts.description: Lower dots in 冬: strokes 4–5. A three-stroke upper shape sits above two separate dots. Keep both dots below the crossing upper strokes.

夏.note: 夏 xià means “summer.” 夏天 xiàtiān names the season.
夏.memory: Remember three levels: a top line, a tall 自, then the crossing strokes of 夂 below.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top line
parts.description: Top line in 夏: strokes 1–1. Remember three levels: a top line, a tall 自, then the crossing strokes of 夂 below.

parts.label: 自
parts.name: middle component
parts.description: Middle component in 夏: strokes 2–7. Remember three levels: a top line, a tall 自, then the crossing strokes of 夂 below.

parts.label: 夂
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Lower component in 夏: strokes 8–10. Remember three levels: a top line, a tall 自, then the crossing strokes of 夂 below.

秋.note: 秋 qiū means “autumn; fall.” 秋天 qiūtiān names the season.
秋.memory: 禾, the grain plant, stands beside 火, fire. Think of the harvest season as a memory cue.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: Grain component in 秋: strokes 1–5. 禾, the grain plant, stands beside 火, fire. Think of the harvest season as a memory cue.

parts.label: 火
parts.name: fire component
