Do not add 很 or another degree adverb such as 非常 to this pattern, because the reduplication already intensifies the description. Keep final 的; with two doubled descriptions together, the first 的 may be omitted: 香香甜甜的. This is restricted: not every state verb allows it. this lesson's permitted set is 香、甜、高、熱、大、美、遠、辣、矮; its excluded set is 多、貴、近、忙、新、少. Use this for an expressive impression, not a neutral factual request: to order hot coffee, say 我要一杯熱咖啡, rather than treating 熱熱的 as the default ordering form.
u30-state-redup.remember: Subjective impression: permitted doubled state verb + 的. No degree adverb. this lesson allows 香、甜、高、熱、大、美、遠、辣、矮 and excludes 多、貴、近、忙、新、少.

examples.meaning: This fruit smells nicely fragrant.
This fruit is fragrant and sweet.

u31-clause-modifier.title: Use a whole clause to identify a noun
u31-clause-modifier.explanation: A complete clause can modify a noun in Chinese. Put the modifying clause before the noun and place 的 directly before that noun. The modifying clause can be affirmative or negative. This lets you say things such as 'the photos I took,' 'the person wearing red clothes,' or 'people who do not go to the night market.'
u31-clause-modifier.remember: Put the entire description before 的 + noun. Negative clauses work too.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shì wǒ pāi de zhàopiàn.
examples.meaning: These are the photos I took.

examples.text: 穿紅色衣服的人是我朋友。
examples.pinyin: Chuān hóngsè yīfú de rén shì wǒ péngyǒu.
examples.meaning: The person wearing red clothes is my friend.

examples.text: 不去夜市的人可以在家喝茶。
examples.pinyin: Bú qù yèshì de rén kěyǐ zài jiā hē chá.
examples.meaning: People who do not go to the night market can drink tea at home.

u31-sentential-le.title: Mark a changed situation with sentence-final 了
u31-sentential-le.explanation: Sentence-final 了 marks that the situation is now different from before; it is not simply a past-tense marker. The sentence may be affirmative, negative, or a question. In a negative change such as 我不住這裡了, the negation describes the new state: 'I no longer stay/live here.' In a question, 了嗎 asks whether the changed situation now holds.
u31-sentential-le.remember: Final 了 signals a new situation compared with before. Do not translate it mechanically as past tense.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài xǐhuān chī shuǐguǒ le.
examples.meaning: I have come to like eating fruit now.
I don't live/stay here anymore.

examples.text: 你現在喜歡吃水果了嗎？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài xǐhuān chī shuǐguǒ le ma?
examples.meaning: Do you like eating fruit now (unlike before)?

u31-yinwei-suoyi.title: Give a reason with 因為…所以…
u31-yinwei-suoyi.explanation: 因為 introduces the cause and 所以 introduces the result. In the this lesson pattern, the cause comes first and the two conjunctions normally appear as a pair. Keep the logic clear: the 因為-clause explains why the 所以-clause follows.
u31-yinwei-suoyi.remember: Cause first with 因為; effect second with 所以.

examples.text: 因為現在去玩的人比較少，所以旅館不太貴。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiànzài qù wán de rén bǐjiào shǎo, suǒyǐ lǚguǎn bú tài guì.
examples.meaning: Because fewer people are traveling now, the hotel is not too expensive.

examples.text: 因為我喜歡水果，所以我想吃吃看。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ xǐhuān shuǐguǒ, suǒyǐ wǒ xiǎng chīchīkàn.
examples.meaning: Because I like fruit, I want to try it.

u32-lai-vp.title: Come here to do something
u32-lai-vp.explanation: 來 + VP says that the subject comes toward the speaker or the relevant deictic location in order to do the activity. It parallels the earlier 去 + activity pattern, but the direction is toward rather than away. Negation, auxiliary verbs, and adverbs go before 來: 不來上課, 要來看房子, 常來游泳. Do not use 來 merely as a generic future marker.
u32-lai-vp.remember: 來 points toward the relevant location; 去 points away. Put 不, 要, 常 and similar words before 來.

examples.meaning: I came here to study Chinese.
He came here to play basketball.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào lái kàn fángzi ma?
examples.meaning: Are you coming to look at the place?
I am not coming to class tomorrow.

u32-early-jiu.title: Sooner than expected with 就
u32-early-jiu.explanation: In a time or distance context, 就 can present an event as occurring sooner, more directly, or with less delay than expected: 走路五分鐘就到了. This is different from the linking 就 in 要是…就…: here the sentence can stand alone without a condition. Sentence-final 了 often appears with arrival or change, but it is not required in every 就 sentence.
u32-early-jiu.remember: Here 就 signals unexpectedly little time or distance. Do not automatically treat every 就 as the consequence half of 要是…就….

examples.pinyin: Zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
examples.meaning: It is only a five-minute walk to get there.
He will be here in just a moment.

examples.text: 那個地方很近，很快就到了。
examples.pinyin: Nàge dìfang hěn jìn, hěn kuài jiù dào le.
examples.meaning: That place is close; you get there very quickly.

u33-existential-you.title: Introduce an indefinite subject with 有
u33-existential-you.explanation: 有 introduces the existence of an indefinite subject, and the following VP says what that subject does: 有人住這裡, 有兩個學生來找你. Because a bare subject is normally definite, a new indefinite subject is introduced with 有. Existential 有 is always negated with 沒有. The rule here also contrasts 地上有一支手機 with 有一支手機在地上: the basic existence is similar, but the first puts the new cellphone information in focus, while the second makes the location 地上 the focus.
u33-existential-you.remember: Use 有 before a new indefinite subject and 沒有 for its negative. Word order can shift the information focus even when the existence meaning stays similar.

examples.meaning: Someone lives here.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu liǎng ge xuéshēng lái zhǎo nǐ.
examples.meaning: Two students came to look for you.
No one lives in this room.
Does anyone live here?
There is a cellphone on the floor.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu yì zhī shǒujī zài dìshang.
examples.meaning: There is a cellphone on the floor.

u33-hui-likelihood.title: 會: learned skill or likelihood?
u33-hui-likelihood.explanation: The rule here distinguishes two uses of 會. The earlier 會 means an acquired skill: 他會做飯, 'he knows how to cook.' this lesson adds 會 for possibility or likelihood, commonly about a future event: 我明天會去看看他. Context—not the character alone—determines the reading. 不會 likewise can mean either 'doesn't know how' or 'will probably not / won't.'
u33-hui-likelihood.remember: With a learned activity, 會 can mean know how. With a future event, 會 can mean will / be likely to. Read the whole context.

examples.meaning: He knows how to cook.
I don't know how to play basketball.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kànkan tā.
examples.meaning: I'll probably go see him tomorrow.

examples.text: 他明天不會去上書法課。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngtiān bú huì qù shàng shūfǎkè.
examples.meaning: He won't / probably won't go to calligraphy class tomorrow.

u33-zero-pronoun.title: Leave understood subjects and objects unspoken
u33-zero-pronoun.explanation: Chinese often omits old information when the listener can recover it from the immediate situation or from an earlier mention. The rule here calls an omitted pronoun a zero pronoun. The most frequent omissions are subjects and objects: a subject can be understood from context even without being spoken (請進! has an understood 你), a previously mentioned subject can disappear in the next clause, and a previously mentioned object can be left unspoken. Keep the noun or pronoun whenever omission would make the meaning ambiguous.
u33-zero-pronoun.remember: If the listener already knows who or what you mean, Chinese often says less. Context-predictable subjects, repeated subjects, and repeated objects can all be omitted when the referent stays clear.

examples.meaning: Please come in! (understood subject: you)

examples.text: 我常打籃球，也常踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cháng dǎ lánqiú, yě cháng tī zúqiú.
examples.meaning: I often play basketball, and also often play soccer.

examples.text: 朋友給我一個西瓜，我不想吃。
examples.pinyin: Péngyǒu gěi wǒ yí ge xīguā, wǒ bù xiǎng chī.
examples.meaning: A friend gave me a watermelon; I don't want to eat it.

u34-first-then.title: First…, then… with 先…再…
u34-first-then.pattern: Subject + 先 + Event 1，(Subject) + 再 + Event 2
u34-first-then.explanation: 先…再… presents the temporal sequence of two consecutive events. Put 先 before the first event and 再 before the next event. The rule here explicitly uses the pattern for past and future sequences, and its drills also include habitual sequences such as 每天…. When the same subject continues into the second event, the examples normally leave it understood before 再. Here 再 means 'then / next,' not merely 'again.'
u34-first-then.remember: 先 marks Event 1; 再 marks Event 2. Keep the two actions in the real order you mean.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiān niàn Zhōngwén, zài niàn dàxué.
examples.meaning: I study Chinese first, then attend university.

examples.text: 我想先吃晚飯，再給媽媽打電話。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiān chī wǎnfàn, zài gěi māma dǎ diànhuà.
examples.meaning: I want to eat dinner first, then call my mom.

examples.text: 我昨天晚上先寫功課，再看電視。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang xiān xiě gōngkè, zài kàn diànshì.
examples.meaning: Last night I did my homework first, then watched TV.

examples.text: 我明天先去圖書館看書，再去超市買東西。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān xiān qù túshūguǎn kàn shū, zài qù chāoshì mǎi dōngxi.
examples.meaning: Tomorrow I will go to the library to read first, then go to the supermarket to buy things.

u35-shi-de.title: Focus a past event with 是…的
u35-shi-de.pattern: Subject / Topic + 是 + Focus + Activity + 的
u35-shi-de.explanation: 是…的 highlights one element of a past event as the focus or contrast. Put 是 directly before the focused element and 的 at the end. The focused element can be the subject, time, place, manner, and occasionally the verb, but never the object. An object is often moved to the very front as the topic, as in 學費是公司替我付的. Put 不 before 是 for negation. The rule here also forms yes/no questions with 嗎, notes that 是 can sometimes be omitted, and allows wh-questions asking who, when, how, or where about a past event; it specifically excludes using the construction to ask 'what' when 'what' is the object.
u35-shi-de.remember: Past event: put 是 before the focused information and 的 at the end. Object focus is not allowed. Negation is 不是…的; yes/no questions can add 嗎; 是 can sometimes be omitted; wh-questions can ask who, when, how, or where.

examples.pinyin: Xuéfèi shì gōngsī tì wǒ fù de.
examples.meaning: My tuition is paid by my company for me.

examples.text: 他是昨天晚上到臺灣的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zuótiān wǎnshang dào Táiwān de.
examples.meaning: It was last night that he arrived in Taiwan.

examples.text: 他是在學校附近吃晚飯的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zài xuéxiào fùjìn chī wǎnfàn de.
examples.meaning: It was near the school that he ate dinner.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuò gōngchē lái shàngkè de.
examples.meaning: I came to class by bus.

examples.text: 我不是在圖書館看書的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì zài túshūguǎn kàn shū de.
examples.meaning: It wasn't at the library that I read.

u36-yihou-after.title: After an event with …以後
u36-yihou-after.pattern: Event / Time expression + 以後，Later event
u36-yihou-after.explanation: this lesson gives 以後 two functions. Unit 35 already taught standalone 以後 as a time word meaning 'in the future'. Here, an event or time expression comes before 以後: A + 以後 means 'after A' or 'later than A', and the later event follows. The rule here uses 回國以後, 來臺灣以後, 下課以後, and time expressions such as 半年以後.
u36-yihou-after.remember: Put the event or time anchor before 以後: 回國以後 = after returning home. Standalone 以後, already learned in Unit 35, means 'in the future'.

examples.text: 我回國以後，也想找個有機會說中文的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huíguó yǐhòu, yě xiǎng zhǎo ge yǒu jīhuì shuō Zhōngwén de gōngzuò.
examples.meaning: After I go back home, I would also like to find a job with opportunities to speak Chinese.

examples.text: 來臺灣以後，我每星期上五天的中文課。
examples.pinyin: Lái Táiwān yǐhòu, wǒ měi xīngqí shàng wǔ tiān de Zhōngwén kè.
examples.meaning: After coming to Taiwan, I have Chinese class five days a week.

examples.text: 我下課以後，常在圖書館上網。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàkè yǐhòu, cháng zài túshūguǎn shàngwǎng.
examples.meaning: After class, I often go online in the library.

examples.text: 半年以後，你打算做什麼？
examples.pinyin: Bàn nián yǐhòu, nǐ dǎsuàn zuò shénme?
examples.meaning: What do you plan to do half a year later?

u36-hao-nan-verb.title: Special meanings of 好 / 難 + verbs
u36-hao-nan-verb.explanation: The rule here separates two uses. With perception verbs, forms such as 好吃/難吃, 好喝/難喝, 好看/難看, and 好聽/難聽 are single words describing a pleasant or unpleasant perception. With action verbs, 好 means 'easy to' and 難 means 'hard/difficult to': 好學/難學, 好寫/難寫, 好做/難做, 好找/難找. Degree adverbs such as 很 can modify either type. Negation puts 不 before the whole predicate (不好找, 不難學, 不好喝). Both branches can form 嗎 questions. For A-not-A questions, the source's perception example repeats the whole compound (好看不好看), while action-verb examples put the contrast before the action verb (好不好賣, 難不難學).
u36-hao-nan-verb.remember: Perception branch: 好吃、好看, etc. are whole perception words; a source A-not-A form is 好看不好看. Action branch: 好 = easy to and 難 = hard to; ask 好不好 + V or 難不難 + V. Put 不 before the whole predicate in negatives.

examples.meaning: Japanese food tastes good and also looks good.
Good jobs are hard to find.
This song is nice to listen to and easy to sing.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén juéde Zhōngwén hěn nán xué.
examples.meaning: Some people think Chinese is hard to learn.

examples.text: 學校附近便宜的套房不好找。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào fùjìn piányí de tàofáng bù hǎo zhǎo.
examples.meaning: Cheap suites near the school are not easy to find.

u38-yi-jiu.title: As soon as… with 一…就…
u38-yi-jiu.pattern: Subject + 一 + Event A，(Subject) + 就 + Event B
u38-yi-jiu.explanation: 一…就… links two events when Event B follows Event A immediately. 一 comes before Event A and 就 before Event B; both follow the subject. If the subject is the same, the repeated subject may be omitted. Either event can be affirmative or negative. The rule here does not use ordinary A-not-A inside this construction; yes/no questions can use 嗎 or 是不是. Both question strategies are valid.
u38-yi-jiu.remember: 一 before Event A; 就 before the immediate Event B. Same subject may be omitted. Either event may be negative; ask with 嗎 or 是不是, not ordinary A-not-A.

examples.meaning: As soon as class ends, I come back.

examples.pinyin: Nàlǐ yì méi rén, wǒ jiù huí jiā.
examples.meaning: As soon as nobody is there, I go home.

examples.text: 老闆今天早上一到公司，就不開心。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn jīntiān zǎoshang yí dào gōngsī, jiù bù kāixīn.
examples.meaning: As soon as the boss got to the company this morning, he was unhappy.

u39-verbal-le.title: Completed action with verbal 了
u39-verbal-le.explanation: Postverbal 了 indicates that an action/event has been completed or has taken place. It is not simply a past-tense ending. Negate the completed action with 沒（有） before the verb and remove verbal 了: 我沒吃晚飯, not *我沒吃了晚飯. A yes/no form here puts 沒有 after the completed clause. This is distinct from sentence-final changed-situation 了.
u39-verbal-le.remember: Completed action: V + 了. Negative: 沒（有） + V, with no verbal 了. Do not equate 了 with past tense.

examples.meaning: I ate dinner.
I didn't eat dinner.
Have you eaten dinner?

u39-bu-vs-mei.title: 不 vs. 沒（有）
u39-bu-vs-mei.pattern: 不 + V/state vs. 沒（有） + event V
u39-bu-vs-mei.explanation: For action verbs, 不 expresses habitual non-action or an intention not to act; 沒（有） says an action did not happen in the past. State verbs use 不 in this system. Process/change events use 沒（有） for non-happening, as in 還沒到. In Taiwan, 沒有 + V is more common than bare 沒 + V, but bare 沒 + V is still grammatical. When 沒 negates a completed action, verbal 了 disappears; sentence-final changed-situation 了 is a different function.
u39-bu-vs-mei.remember: 不: habit/intention or contrary state. 沒（有）: an event did not happen. Taiwan commonly prefers 沒有 + V, but bare 沒 + V remains valid.

examples.meaning: I don't drink coffee (habit).
I'm not going today (intention).
I didn't go yesterday.
He hasn't arrived yet.

u40-questionword-totality.title: All-inclusive question words with 都 / 也
u40-questionword-totality.pattern: Question word + 都 + … / Question word + 都 or 也 + 不／沒…
u40-questionword-totality.explanation: Question words can form total inclusion: 誰都 'everyone', 哪裡都 'everywhere', 什麼都 'everything', 什麼時候都 'anytime', and 怎麼 + V + 都 'whichever way'. For total exclusion, use question word + 都 or 也 + 不／沒, with the negative after 都/也. Both 都 and 也 are valid in negative total-exclusion. The pattern forms questions for this pattern with 嗎.
u40-questionword-totality.remember: Affirmative: question word + 都. Negative: question word + 都/也 + 不/沒. Put the negative after 都/也.

examples.meaning: I eat anything/everything.
Nobody came.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ nǎlǐ dōu méi qù.
examples.meaning: Yesterday I didn't go anywhere.

u40-more-less-verb.title: Do more / do less with 多／少 + Verb
u40-more-less-verb.pattern: 多 / 少 + Verb (+ 一點 + Object)
u40-more-less-verb.explanation: Before a verb, 多 means do more than planned/usual and 少 means do less/fewer than planned/usual. This differs from earlier quantity uses. The pattern can refer to past or future events, and 一點 often modifies the object.
u40-more-less-verb.remember: Put 多 or 少 before the action verb to mean do more or less than planned/usual.

examples.meaning: Eat a little more.
You should buy fewer things.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng duō xué yìdiǎn Zhōngwén.
examples.meaning: I want to study a little more Chinese.

u41-shibushi.title: Confirmation questions with 是不是
u41-shibushi.explanation: 是不是 asks the listener to confirm information the speaker already knows, expects, or sees as likely. It is not simply interchangeable with every neutral 嗎 or A-not-A question. This lesson uses 是不是 in environments where ordinary A-not-A is unavailable, including 比 comparisons and 太…了. When multiple grammatical strategies are possible, context must make the confirmation reading clear.
u41-shibushi.remember: Use 是不是 when checking/confirming information, not merely asking neutral new information.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bú shì zuìjìn tài máng le?
examples.meaning: You've been too busy lately, right?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bú shì bǐ tā gāo?
examples.meaning: You're taller than him, right?

examples.text: 臺灣人過生日是不是都吃這些東西？
examples.pinyin: Táiwān rén guò shēngrì shì bú shì dōu chī zhèxiē dōngxi?
examples.meaning: Do Taiwanese people all eat these things for birthdays?

u41-gen-yiyang.title: Comparison with 跟…一樣
u41-gen-yiyang.pattern: A + 跟 + B + 一樣 (+ property)
u41-gen-yiyang.explanation: A 跟 B 一樣 says A and B are the same; a property can follow 一樣 to show equal degree. Put 不 before 一樣 to say the two differ in the relevant quality. Put 不 before 跟 to reject B as the comparison target, often followed by another target. Questions can use 一樣不一樣 or 是不是一樣; both are valid.
u41-gen-yiyang.remember: Same: A 跟 B 一樣. Different quality: A 跟 B 不一樣. Different comparison target: A 不跟 B 一樣. Ask with 一樣不一樣 or 是不是一樣.

examples.text: 我的生日跟你的生日一樣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shēngrì gēn nǐ de shēngrì yíyàng.
examples.meaning: My birthday is the same as yours.
I am as tall as you.

examples.text: 我的生日跟你的生日不一樣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shēngrì gēn nǐ de shēngrì bù yíyàng.
examples.meaning: My birthday is different from yours.

examples.text: 他不跟我一樣高，跟你一樣高。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù gēn wǒ yíyàng gāo, gēn nǐ yíyàng gāo.
examples.meaning: He isn't as tall as me; he's as tall as you.

u43-completed-duration.title: Completed duration with verbal 了
u43-completed-duration.pattern: Subject + V + 了 + Duration / Subject + V + Object + V + 了 + Duration
u43-completed-duration.explanation: Use verbal 了 followed by a duration when an activity is viewed as completed. If a transitive verb keeps its object before the duration, repeat the verb before 了 + Duration: 打網球打了兩個鐘頭. If the object or location is fronted as the topic, the repeated verb is not required: 中文我只學了五個月. This integrates earlier duration grammar, object-repeat duration, and completed-action 了.
u43-completed-duration.remember: Completed duration: verbal 了 + duration. With an object before the duration, repeat the verb; fronting the object/location can avoid the repetition.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Táiwān zhù le yì nián.
examples.meaning: I lived in Taiwan for one year.

examples.text: 我打網球打了兩個鐘頭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ wǎngqiú dǎ le liǎng ge zhōngtóu.
examples.meaning: I played tennis for two hours.

examples.pinyin: Zhōngwén wǒ zhǐ xué le wǔ ge yuè.
examples.meaning: I studied Chinese for only five months.

u43-duration-to-now.title: Duration accumulated up to now
u43-duration-to-now.pattern: Subject + V + 了 + Duration + 了
u43-duration-to-now.explanation: Use the double-了 pattern for a duration accumulated up to the time of speaking. The situation may continue or may stop depending on context. Do not treat this as automatically “still continuing.” Contrast it with u43-completed-duration, which presents the duration as completed. 多久了 asks for the accumulated duration; 已經 often appears in this context.
u43-duration-to-now.remember: One 了 after the verb + duration can present a completed duration; final 了 adds the “up to now” duration frame. Continuation depends on context.

examples.text: 我在臺灣住了半年多了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Táiwān zhù le bànnián duō le.
examples.meaning: I have been in Taiwan for a little over half a year.

examples.text: 她已經工作了兩個月了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng gōngzuò le liǎng ge yuè le.
examples.meaning: She has worked for two months up to now.

examples.text: 他學中文學了三個星期了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xué Zhōngwén xué le sān ge xīngqí le.
examples.meaning: He has studied Chinese for three weeks up to now.

u43-imminent.title: Something is about to happen
u43-imminent.pattern: 快…了 / 要…了 / 快要…了
u43-imminent.explanation: These patterns present an event or change as imminent. 快 here means “soon/about to,” and 要 is the imminent-event auxiliary “will / going to” in this imminent-event system. In Taiwan Mandarin that Taiwan Mandarin prefers the disyllabic 快要 form. Under the rule here this lesson rule, do not combine an explicit time word such as 明天 directly with 快要: *他明天快要回來了. Use this pattern when the context shows that the event is close, not as a generic future marker.
u43-imminent.remember: Imminence, not generic future: 快／要／快要…了. The source prefers 快要 in Taiwan Mandarin and blocks explicit-time + 快要 in this this lesson rule.

examples.meaning: It is about to rain.
The game is about to start.

examples.pinyin: Bàba kuài yào dào jiā le.
examples.meaning: Dad is about to get home.

u44-even-more.title: Comparison with 更 — even more
u44-even-more.pattern: A + 比 + B + 更 + State Verb
u44-even-more.explanation: 更 means “even more” relative to an established or understood baseline. It goes before a state verb. this lesson first shows the baseline meaning in 星期天我更忙, then uses 更 inside 比 comparisons. Do not flatten 更 to neutral “more”; the “even more” baseline is part of the meaning. Confirmation questions can use 是不是.
u44-even-more.remember: 更 = even more relative to a baseline. In the this lesson comparison: A 比 B 更 + property.

examples.meaning: I am even busier on Sunday.
This year is even colder than last year.

examples.text: 這次的颱風是不是比上次的更大？
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì de táifēng shì bú shì bǐ shàng cì de gèng dà?
examples.meaning: Is this typhoon even bigger than the last one?

u44-not-as.title: Not as…as with 沒有
u44-not-as.pattern: A + 沒有 + B + 那麼／這麼 + State Verb
u44-not-as.explanation: Use 沒有…那麼／這麼… to say A has a lower degree of a property than B: A is not as X as B. 那麼/這麼 may sometimes be omitted. The pattern notes that the positive form A 有 B 那麼／這麼 + State Verb is rare except in 嗎 questions. Questions can use 有沒有. Keep this distinct from earlier 不比. The source explicitly contrasts equality 跟…一樣, inferiority 沒有…那麼, and superiority 比.
u44-not-as.remember: Equal: 跟…一樣. Lower degree: 沒有…那麼／這麼. Higher degree: 比….

examples.meaning: The train is not as fast as the HSR.

examples.text: 這次的颱風沒有上次的那麼可怕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì de táifēng méiyǒu shàng cì de nàme kěpà.
examples.meaning: This typhoon is not as scary as the last one.
Is today as hot as yesterday?

u46-noncommittal-question-words.title: Negative, non-specific question words
u46-noncommittal-question-words.pattern: NEG + clause containing 什麼 / 多少 / 幾 / 哪裡 / 誰 / 什麼時候
u46-noncommittal-question-words.explanation: In this lesson, a question word inside a declarative sentence can avoid a specific commitment. The rule is always negative and is not the Unit-40 都/也 totality pattern.
u46-noncommittal-question-words.remember: This pattern is negative. Do not add 都/也 merely because a question word appears.

examples.meaning: I didn't buy anything in particular.
I didn't go anywhere in particular.
She has only a few friends.

u46-ba-disposal.title: Introductory 把 disposal
u46-ba-disposal.pattern: 把 + definite/referential object + bare outward-transitive action verb + sentence-final 了
u46-ba-disposal.explanation: Use 把 for what is done to a salient object. At this introductory introductory stage, favor definite/referential objects and outward actions such as 吃、喝、寫、賣; excluded inward verbs include 買、學. 沒/別 precede 把. Questions use 了沒有 or 是不是.
u46-ba-disposal.remember: Specific object + outward action + final-了 pattern taught here; 沒/別 before 把.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zhège xiǎolóngbāo chī le.
examples.meaning: I ate this xiaolongbao.

examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ de yào chī le.
examples.meaning: Don't take my medicine.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ gōngkè xiě le méiyǒu?
examples.meaning: Did you finish the homework?

u47-vle-jiu.title: V了…就… — do B right after completing A
u47-vle-jiu.explanation: Event 2 follows immediately or very soon after completion of event 1. This pattern can use 以後, contrasts with prior 一…就…, and uses 嗎/是不是 rather than an ordinary A-not-A route.
u47-vle-jiu.remember: Completed first event + 就 + next event; 以後 is compatible; ordinary A-not-A is not the question route.

examples.pinyin: Tā chī le yào jiù shuìjiào.
examples.meaning: After taking medicine, he went right to sleep.

examples.pinyin: Tā chī le yào yǐhòu, jiù shuìjiào.
examples.meaning: After taking medicine, he went to sleep.

examples.text: 妹妹喝了熱湯，就不覺得冷了。
examples.pinyin: Mèimei hē le rè tāng, jiù bù juéde lěng le.
examples.meaning: After younger sister drank hot soup, she no longer felt cold.

u48-a-little-degree.title: 一點 — quantity and degree
u48-a-little-degree.pattern: 一點 + NP / Vs + 一點 / 有（一）點 + Vs / 一點點
u48-a-little-degree.explanation: 一點 + NP gives a small quantity; Vs + 一點 gives a slightly different degree, often comparative; 有（一）點 + Vs gives a slight state rather than a comparison; 一點點 emphasizes a tiny amount or degree.
u48-a-little-degree.remember: Post-state 一點 can express comparative improvement; pre-state 有（一）點 expresses a slight state.

examples.meaning: a little bit of something
a little better
a little cold

u48-action-comparison-de.title: Comparing actions with 得
u48-action-comparison-de.pattern: Comparative + Action + 得 + State / Action + 得 + Comparative + State
u48-action-comparison-de.explanation: Compare how an action is performed using 得 de with 比. Pattern 2 often repeats the verb where an object/action noun requires it. 不 precedes 比; questions use 嗎 or 是不是. This 得 is complement de, not modal děi.
u48-action-comparison-de.remember: Action comparison uses complement 得 de; put 不 before 比.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ zǒu de kuài.
examples.meaning: He walks faster than I do.

examples.pinyin: Tā zǒulù zǒu de bǐ wǒ kuài.
examples.meaning: He walks faster than I do.

examples.text: 我吃了一包藥以後，睡得比昨天好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī le yì bāo yào yǐhòu, shuì de bǐ zuótiān hǎo.
examples.meaning: After taking one packet of medicine, I slept better than yesterday.

u48-comparison-degree.title: Degree complements in comparisons
u48-comparison-degree.explanation: Use 一點 for a small comparison difference and 得多 or 多了 for a large difference. Keep this state-degree system distinct from action comparison with 得.
u48-comparison-degree.remember: Use 一點 for a small difference; 得多 / 多了 for a much larger difference.

examples.text: 他的房間比我的大一點。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān bǐ wǒ de dà yìdiǎn.
examples.meaning: His room is a little bigger than mine.

examples.text: 捷運站比公車站遠得多。
examples.pinyin: Jiéyùn zhàn bǐ gōngchē zhàn yuǎn de duō.
examples.meaning: The MRT station is much farther than the bus stop.

examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang bǐ zǎoshang shūfu duō le.
examples.meaning: The evening is much more comfortable than the morning.

u48-separable-verbs.title: Separable verbs and insertion
u48-separable-verbs.explanation: Certain V+N forms can separate for verbal 了, recipient/object material, or duration. this lesson productive forms are restricted to lexically available separable verbs.
u48-separable-verbs.remember: Insert the material between the verbal and nominal parts; only split forms already lexically available.

examples.text: 他回了家以後，就開始工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā huí le jiā yǐhòu, jiù kāishǐ gōngzuò.
examples.meaning: After he went home, he started working.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiàn nǐ yí miàn.
examples.meaning: I want to see you once.

examples.pinyin: shuì le bā ge xiǎoshí de jiào
examples.meaning: slept for eight hours

b2u1-l4-from-toward.title: From a point toward a direction
b2u1-l4-from-toward.pattern: 從 + start + 往 + direction + movement
b2u1-l4-from-toward.explanation: 從 (cóng) marks where movement starts; 往 (wǎng) marks the direction or destination toward which it goes. Put both before 走. If the start is understood, 往前走 is enough. 不能 before the movement means you cannot go that way. To check a route, put 是不是 before the route description.
b2u1-l4-from-toward.remember: 從 = starting point; 往 = direction; 到 = endpoint.

examples.meaning: Go forward from here.

examples.text: 不能從這個路口往前走。
examples.pinyin: Bù néng cóng zhège lùkǒu wǎng qián zǒu.
examples.meaning: You cannot go forward from this intersection.

examples.pinyin: Shì bu shì cóng zhèlǐ wǎng qián zǒu?
examples.meaning: Do I go forward from here?

b2u2-l4-evaluative.title: How something seems: V 起來
b2u2-l4-evaluative.explanation: Verb + 起來 introduces an impression from seeing, hearing, eating, or doing something. 看起來 (kàn qǐlái) means looks; 聽起來 (tīng qǐlái) means sounds; 吃起來 (chī qǐlái) means tastes. Put the judgment afterward. Negate the judgment: 聽起來不遠 means it does not sound far. Ask with 怎麼樣 after 起來, or make the judgment an affirmative-negative question.
b2u2-l4-evaluative.remember: The evaluation follows 起來; it is a judgment from sensory experience.

examples.meaning: NTNU does not sound far.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài chī qǐlái bú là.
examples.meaning: This dish does not taste spicy.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài chī qǐlái zěnme yàng?
examples.meaning: How does this dish taste?

examples.pinyin: Shīdà kàn qǐlái yuǎn bu yuǎn?
examples.meaning: Does NTNU look far away?

b2u3-l3-ongoing.title: Keep an action or state going: 著
b2u3-l3-ongoing.explanation: 著 (zhe, neutral tone) follows the verb and presents an action or state as continuing: 看著 means looking, 拿著 (názhe) means holding. In 他看著地圖往前走, looking at the map continues while he walks. 沒 negates the continuing situation; 不是 does not replace it. In a question, 是不是 can come before the whole verb phrase. 著 is not a marker that an action has finished.
b2u3-l3-ongoing.remember: 著 is neutral-tone zhe after the verb; it does not mean the action has ended.

examples.meaning: He keeps looking at the map.
He is holding the map.
He is not holding the map.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì bu shì názhe dìtú?
examples.meaning: Is he holding the map?

b2u4-l2-simultaneous.title: Two actions at the same time
b2u4-l2-simultaneous.pattern: 一邊 + action A，一邊 + action B
b2u4-l2-simultaneous.explanation: 一邊 (yìbiān) comes before each of two actions performed by the same person at the same time. Both action phrases follow the shared subject. 不可以 or 不要 before the pattern forbids the combination; 沒 before the pattern says the actions did not happen together. Add 好不好 after the two actions to propose doing them together. This pattern does not mean first one action and then the other.
b2u4-l2-simultaneous.remember: Both actions overlap; keep both 一邊 parts.

examples.text: 我一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú.
examples.meaning: I eat noodles while looking at the map.

examples.text: 不要一邊走路，一邊看手機。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào yìbiān zǒulù, yìbiān kàn shǒujī.
examples.meaning: Do not look at your phone while walking.

examples.text: 我們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖，好不好？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú, hǎo bu hǎo?
examples.meaning: Shall we look at the map while eating noodles?

examples.text: 他沒一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú.
examples.meaning: He did not look at the map while eating noodles.

b2u4-l3-distance.title: Distance between two places: 離
b2u4-l3-distance.pattern: place A + 離 + place B + distance (遠/近)
b2u4-l3-distance.explanation: Place A + 離 + place B + 遠/近 describes the distance between two places. B is the reference point. 很近 means close and 不遠 means not far. Put 不 before the distance word, not before 離. To ask, say 遠不遠 or 是不是很遠. Unlike 從, which gives the start of movement, 離 measures distance without saying that anyone moves.
b2u4-l3-distance.remember: Negate or question 遠/近, not 離.

examples.meaning: The post office is close to the school.
The noodle shop is not far from school.

examples.pinyin: Miàndiàn lí xuéxiào yuǎn bu yuǎn?
examples.meaning: Is the noodle shop far from school?
